temas.titulo: Adverbios de modo: cómo se hace
temas.resumen: Cómo haces algo: quickly, carefully, clearly, well. Cómo se forman (-ly, -y → -ily, -le → -ly, -ic → -ically), los irregulares (good → well, fast, hard, late; ojo con hardly y lately), dónde van (después del verbo + objeto) y por qué se dice It looks good y no «It looks well».

teoria.paraQue: Para decir cómo haces algo: rápido, despacio, con cuidado, bien, mal, en voz baja. Sirve para describir cómo maneja alguien, cómo habla inglés tu hija, cómo salió una presentación o cómo trabaja tu equipo.
teoria.llave: La llave es adjetivo + -ly: quick → quickly, careful → carefully. El adjetivo describe a una persona o una cosa (a careful driver); el adverbio describe la acción (he drives carefully). Va después del verbo, o después del verbo + objeto: She speaks English well (nunca «speaks well English»). Ojo con los irregulares: good → well, y fast, hard, late y early no cambian. Y con look, sound, feel, taste, seem y be no va adverbio sino adjetivo: It looks good.

formulas.formula: adjetivo + -ly
formulas.ejemplo: quick → quick((ly)) · careful → careful((ly)) · She {{drive((s))}} careful((ly)).

formulas.formula: consonante + y → i + ly
formulas.ejemplo: easy → eas((ily)) · happy → happ((ily)) · We {{won}} the pitch eas((ily)).

formulas.formula: quita la e y pon y
formulas.ejemplo: simple → simpl((y)) · comfortable → comfortabl((y)) · [[Can]] you {{explain}} it simpl((y))?

formulas.formula: adjetivo en -ic + ally
formulas.ejemplo: basic → basic((ally)) · automatic → automatic((ally)) · The app {{save((s))}} your work automatic((ally)).

formulas.formula: good → well · fast → fast · hard → hard · late → late · early → early
formulas.ejemplo: She {{speak((s))}} English well. We {{work((ed))}} hard and {{finish((ed))}} late.

formulas.formula: Sujeto + verbo (+ objeto) + adverbio
formulas.ejemplo: Laura {{read((s))}} the brief careful((ly)). Mike {{answer((ed))}} calm((ly)).

formulas.formula: look / sound / feel / taste / smell / seem / be + adjetivo (sin -ly)
formulas.ejemplo: The new logo {{look((s))}} good. Your idea {{sound((s))}} great. I {{feel}} tired.

formulas.formula: feel + adjetivo (estado) · do / go + well (resultado)
formulas.ejemplo: I {{feel}} good today. I {{did}} well in the interview. The meeting {{went}} well.

reglas: Casi todos se forman con adjetivo + -ly: slow → slowly, careful → carefully, polite → politely, calm → calmly.
Si el adjetivo termina en consonante + y, la y cambia a i: easy → easily, happy → happily, busy → busily.
Si termina en -le, cambia la e por y: simple → simply, comfortable → comfortably, terrible → terribly.
Si termina en -ic, se agrega -ally: basic → basically, automatic → automatically, dramatic → dramatically (excepción: public → publicly).
Good → well. Es el error más común: She speaks English well, you did well (nunca «speaks English good»).
Fast, hard, late y early son iguales como adjetivo y como adverbio: a fast car / he drives fast. «Fastly» y «earlily» no existen.
Hardly no es «duramente»: es «apenas, casi no». I work hard (trabajo duro) ≠ I hardly work (casi no trabajo).
Lately no es «tarde»: es «últimamente», y va con presente perfecto. I arrived late (llegué tarde) ≠ I've been tired lately (he estado cansado últimamente).
El adverbio de modo va después del verbo, o después del verbo + objeto. Nunca entre el verbo y el objeto: She speaks English fluently (no «speaks fluently English»).
Con look, sound, feel, taste, smell, seem y be va adjetivo, no adverbio, porque describes al sujeto y no una acción: It looks good, the soup tastes great, you seem tired.
I feel good = me siento bien (estado: adjetivo). I did well / it went well = me fue bien, salió bien (resultado de una acción: adverbio).
Algunos adjetivos ya terminan en -ly y no tienen adverbio: friendly, lovely, lonely. Se dice in a friendly way (no «friendlily»).

usos.ejemplo: My dad {{drive((s))}} slow((ly)) and careful((ly)).
My daughter {{speak((s))}} English fluent((ly)), and I {{speak}} it quite well.

usos.uso: Cómo sabe o se ve algo
usos.ejemplo: This ajiaco {{taste((s))}} amazing and the restaurant {{look((s))}} nice.
You {{present((ed))}} the idea clear((ly)) and {{answer((ed))}} the questions calm((ly)).
The team {{work((ed))}} hard and {{deliver((ed))}} the campaign early.
[[Could]] you {{read}} the contract careful((ly)) before you {{sign}} it?

errores.mal: She speaks English very good.
errores.porque: Good es adjetivo; para la acción (hablar) usa well.

errores.mal: He drives very careful.
errores.porque: Para decir cómo maneja hace falta el adverbio con -ly.

errores.mal: She speaks fluently English.
errores.porque: El adverbio no va entre el verbo y el objeto.

errores.mal: The new logo looks greatly.
errores.porque: Con look, sound, feel y taste va adjetivo.

errores.mal: I work hardly every day.
errores.porque: El adverbio de hard es hard. Hardly significa «casi no».

errores.mal: He arrived lately for the meeting.
errores.bien: He arrived late for the meeting.
errores.porque: Late = tarde. Lately = últimamente.

errores.mal: We won the pitch easyly.
errores.porque: Consonante + y → -ily: easy → easily.

errores.mal: The app updates automaticly.
errores.porque: Los adjetivos en -ic hacen -ically.

contraste.nota: El adjetivo describe a la persona; el adverbio describe la acción.
hard = duro, con esfuerzo · hardly = casi no.
Estado (adjetivo) vs. resultado de una acción (adverbio).
late = tarde · lately = últimamente (con presente perfecto).

frases.en: Please read it carefully before you sign.
frases.es: Léelo con cuidado antes de firmar.

teoria.tip: Pregúntale a la frase: ¿describo a alguien o algo (adjetivo: a slow driver, it looks good) o describo cómo se hace la acción (adverbio: he drives slowly)? Y recuerda la pareja de oro: good → well.

palabras.ejemplo: Andrés speaks English really well.

hueco.frase: Andrés speaks English really ___. (good)

palabras.nota: good → well. Good describe cosas (a good idea); well describe acciones (you did well).

palabras.ejemplo: She answered the client's email quickly.

hueco.frase: She answered the client's email ___. (quick)

palabras.nota: quick + -ly. Para velocidad también se dice fast.

palabras.ejemplo: Can you speak more slowly, please?

hueco.frase: Can you speak more ___, please? (slow)

palabras.nota: Speak more slowly = habla más despacio.

palabras.ejemplo: Please read the contract carefully.

hueco.frase: Please read the contract ___. (careful)

palabras.nota: careful + -ly: con doble l. Lo contrario es carelessly.

palabras.ejemplo: My brother drives too fast.

hueco.frase: My brother drives too ___. (rápido)

palabras.nota: Igual que el adjetivo: a fast car, he drives fast. «Fastly» no existe.

palabras.ejemplo: The team worked hard on the pitch.

hueco.frase: The team worked ___ on the pitch. (con esfuerzo)

palabras.nota: Igual que el adjetivo. Ojo: hardly es otra palabra y significa «casi no».

palabras.ejemplo: The client arrived late for the meeting.

hueco.frase: The client arrived ___ for the meeting. (tarde)

palabras.nota: Igual que el adjetivo. Lately significa «últimamente», no «tarde».

palabras.ejemplo: I got up early to go to the gym.

hueco.frase: I got up ___ to go to the gym. (temprano)

palabras.nota: Adjetivo y adverbio a la vez: an early flight, I left early.

palabras.ejemplo: We played badly in the second half.

hueco.frase: We played ___ in the second half. (bad)

palabras.nota: bad + -ly. Con feel o look va bad: I feel bad (me siento mal).

palabras.ejemplo: We won the pitch easily.

hueco.frase: We won the pitch ___. (easy)

palabras.nota: Consonante + y → -ily: easy → easily.

palabras.ejemplo: Laura explained the strategy clearly.

hueco.frase: Laura explained the strategy ___. (clear)

palabras.nota: En presentaciones: speak clearly, explain it clearly.

palabras.ejemplo: The baby is sleeping, so please talk quietly.

hueco.frase: The baby is sleeping, so please talk ___. (quiet)

palabras.nota: No lo confundas con quite (bastante).

palabras.ejemplo: My neighbor plays music loudly every Friday.

hueco.frase: My neighbor plays music ___ every Friday. (loud)

palabras.nota: loud + -ly. Al hablar también se oye play music loud.

palabras.ejemplo: The kids played happily in the park.

hueco.frase: The kids played ___ in the park. (happy)

palabras.nota: Consonante + y → -ily: happy → happily.

palabras.ejemplo: She politely said no to the client.

hueco.frase: She ___ said no to the client. (polite)

palabras.nota: Puede ir antes del verbo o al final: she politely said no / she said no politely.

palabras.ejemplo: We waited patiently for the client's feedback.

hueco.frase: We waited ___ for the client's feedback. (patient)

palabras.nota: patient + -ly.

palabras.ejemplo: The client takes deadlines very seriously.

hueco.frase: The client takes deadlines very ___. (serious)

palabras.nota: Seriously? = ¿En serio?

palabras.ejemplo: Suddenly, the lights went out in the meeting room.

hueco.frase: ___, the lights went out in the meeting room. (sudden)

palabras.nota: En historias suele ir al inicio, con coma.

palabras.ejemplo: The client replied immediately.

hueco.frase: The client replied ___. (immediate)

palabras.nota: Un poco más formal que right away.

palabras.ejemplo: Honestly, I don't like the new logo.

hueco.frase: ___, I don't like the new logo. (honest)

palabras.nota: Al inicio de la frase = «la verdad». La h no suena.

palabras.ejemplo: My daughter speaks English fluently.

hueco.frase: My daughter speaks English ___. (fluent)

palabras.nota: Va después del idioma: speaks English fluently.

palabras.ejemplo: Mike answered the angry client calmly.

hueco.frase: Mike answered the angry client ___. (calm)

palabras.nota: La l no suena: /ˈkɑmli/.

palabras.ejemplo: Did I spell your name correctly?

hueco.frase: Did I spell your name ___? (correct)

palabras.nota: correct + -ly.

palabras.es: como se debe, como es debido
palabras.ejemplo: I didn't sleep properly last night.

hueco.frase: I didn't sleep ___ last night. (proper)

palabras.nota: Muy común: work properly (funcionar bien), eat properly (comer como se debe).

palabras.ejemplo: The new laptop works perfectly.

hueco.frase: The new laptop works ___. (perfect)

palabras.nota: perfect + -ly.

palabras.ejemplo: Let me briefly explain the plan.

hueco.frase: Let me ___ explain the plan. (brief)

palabras.nota: En reuniones: Let me briefly explain… (puede ir antes del verbo).

palabras.ejemplo: You can send the invoice directly to me.

hueco.frase: You can send the invoice ___ to me. (direct)

palabras.nota: direct + -ly.

palabras.ejemplo: I've been really busy lately.

hueco.frase: I've been really busy ___. (últimamente)

palabras.nota: No es «tarde» (late). Va con presente perfecto, al final de la frase.

palabras.ejemplo: Basically, the client wants a cheaper version.

hueco.frase: ___, the client wants a cheaper version. (basic)

palabras.nota: -ic → -ically: basic → basically (no «basicly»).

palabras.ejemplo: The app saves your work automatically.

hueco.frase: The app saves your work ___. (automatic)

palabras.nota: -ic → -ically: automatic → automatically.

palabras.ejemplo: Can you explain it simply?

hueco.frase: Can you explain it ___? (simple)

palabras.nota: -le → -ly: simple → simply (no «simplely»).

palabras.ejemplo: Eight people can sit comfortably in this room.

hueco.frase: Eight people can sit ___ in this room. (comfortable)

palabras.nota: -le → -ly: comfortable → comfortably.

palabras.ejemplo: We arrived safely in Medellín.

hueco.frase: We arrived ___ in Medellín. (safe)

palabras.nota: Drive safely! = ¡Maneja con cuidado! (al hablar también: Drive safe!).

palabras.ejemplo: Our new team works very efficiently.

hueco.frase: Our new team works very ___. (efficient)

palabras.nota: efficient + -ly.

palabras.ejemplo: We need to think creatively about this problem.

hueco.frase: We need to think ___ about this problem. (creative)

palabras.nota: Think creatively = pensar de forma creativa.

ejercicios.q: Please drive ___. The roads are wet.
ejercicios.explica: Para decir cómo manejas va el adverbio: careful + -ly = carefully (con doble l).

ejercicios.q: Andrés speaks English very ___.
ejercicios.explica: Good es adjetivo; su adverbio es well. Para la acción (hablar): speaks very well.

ejercicios.q: The new logo looks ___.
ejercicios.explica: Con look va adjetivo, porque describes el logo, no una acción: looks great.

ejercicios.q: The meeting started ___ because the client was in traffic.
ejercicios.explica: Late (tarde) es igual como adjetivo y como adverbio. Lately significa «últimamente».

ejercicios.q: Sarah works ___. She's always the last one to leave.
ejercicios.explica: Hard (duro, con esfuerzo) no cambia como adverbio. Hardly significa «casi no».

ejercicios.q: Camila answered all the client's questions ___. (calm)
ejercicios.explica: Regla general: adjetivo + -ly. Calm → calmly.

ejercicios.q: We won the pitch ___. (easy)
ejercicios.explica: Consonante + y → -ily: easy → easily.

ejercicios.q: The report updates ___ every Monday. (automatic)
ejercicios.explica: Los adjetivos en -ic hacen -ically: automatic → automatically.

ejercicios.q: Can you explain it ___, please? (simple)
ejercicios.explica: Los adjetivos en -le cambian la e por y: simple → simply.
Ojo con lately (últimamente) y hardly (casi no): no significan «tarde» ni «duro».

ejercicios.frase: He drives very fast.
ejercicios.explica: Fast es igual como adjetivo y como adverbio; «fastly» no existe.

ejercicios.frase: My son plays the guitar very good.
correccion: My son plays the guitar very well.
My son plays the guitar really well.
ejercicios.explica: Para la acción (tocar) va el adverbio well, no el adjetivo good.

ejercicios.frase: Laura is a careful designer.
ejercicios.explica: Careful va antes de un sustantivo (designer): es adjetivo. Para la acción sería she designs carefully.

ejercicios.texto: She explained the idea clearly.
ejercicios.explica: Clear + -ly = clearly, después del verbo + objeto.

ejercicios.q: Your idea sounds ___. Let's present it on Monday.
ejercicios.explica: Con sound va adjetivo: describes la idea, no una acción. Sounds good.

ejercicios.q: My daughter ___.
ejercicios.explica: El adverbio va después del verbo + objeto (speaks English fluently), nunca entre los dos, y lleva -ly.

ejercicios.q: I've been really tired ___. I think I need a vacation.
ejercicios.explica: Lately = últimamente, con presente perfecto. Late es «tarde» y later «más tarde».

ejercicios.q: The call was so noisy that I could ___ hear the client.
ejercicios.explica: Hardly = apenas, casi no. Hard es «duro, con esfuerzo» y no encaja aquí.

ejercicios.q: The client paid ___: two months after the deadline! (late)
ejercicios.explica: Late no cambia: es igual como adjetivo y como adverbio. Lately es otra palabra (últimamente).

ejercicios.q: Mike checked the numbers ___ and found three mistakes. (careful)
ejercicios.explica: Para describir cómo revisó: careful + -ly = carefully, después del verbo + objeto.

ejercicios.q: Your English is very good. You speak English very ___. (good)
ejercicios.explica: Good es el adjetivo (your English is good); well es el adverbio (you speak it well).

ejercicios.en: She speaks English fluently.
ejercicios.explica: Verbo + objeto + adverbio con -ly: speaks English fluently.

ejercicios.en: We read the brief carefully.
ejercicios.explica: Careful + -ly = carefully, después del objeto (the brief).

ejercicios.en: Your proposal sounds really good.
ejercicios.explica: Con sound va adjetivo: sounds good, no sounds well.

ejercicios.frase: She speaks very well English.
correccion: She speaks English very well.
ejercicios.explica: El adverbio no se mete entre el verbo y el objeto: speaks English very well.

ejercicios.frase: This coffee tastes amazing.
ejercicios.explica: Con taste va adjetivo (amazing), porque describe el café, no una acción.

ejercicios.frase: I work hardly every day, even on weekends.
correccion: I work hard every day, even on weekends.
ejercicios.explica: El adverbio de hard es hard. Hardly significa «casi no», lo contrario de lo que quieres decir.

ejercicios.frase: He is a slow driver.
ejercicios.instruccion: Dilo con el verbo drive y un adverbio
ejercicios.explica: Adjetivo + sustantivo (a slow driver) → verbo + adverbio (drives slowly).

ejercicios.es: El equipo trabajó duro y terminó temprano.
respuestas: The team worked hard and finished early.
The team worked hard and they finished early.
The team worked really hard and finished early.
ejercicios.explica: Hard y early no cambian como adverbios: worked hard, finished early.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta cómo salió tu última presentación o reunión importante: cómo hablaste, cómo reaccionó el cliente, cómo trabajó el equipo y cómo te sentiste al final.
ejercicios.objetivo: adverbios con -ly después del verbo (+ objeto) · well / hard / early / late · look / sound / feel + adjetivo
ejercicios.ejemplo: Last week I presented a new campaign to a client. I was nervous, but I spoke slowly and clearly, and I answered all the questions calmly. The client listened carefully and said the idea sounded great. The team worked really hard, and we finished the deck early. It went really well, and I felt great after the meeting.
ejercicios.explica: Adverbio para la acción (spoke clearly, went well); adjetivo con sound y feel (sounded great, felt great).

ejercicios.instruccion: Escribe el adverbio de la palabra entre paréntesis; si va con look, sound o feel, deja el adjetivo.
ejercicios.texto: Monday was a big day at Brava. I got up {1} (early) and drove {2} (careful) to the office because it was raining. The client arrived {3} (late), so we checked the deck {4} (quick) one more time. Andrés presented the idea {5} (clear) and answered every question {6} (calm). At the end, the client said: "Your proposal sounds {7} (great)." We worked {8} (hard) for three weeks, and it was worth it.
ejercicios.explica: Adjetivo + -ly para la acción (drove carefully); early, late y hard no cambian; con sound va adjetivo (sounds great).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el adjetivo o el adverbio de la palabra entre paréntesis.
ejercicios.texto: My dad is a very {1} (careful) driver. Last Sunday we drove to Villa de Leyva. The road was wet, so he drove {2} (slow), and we arrived {3} (late) for lunch. Nobody cared: the food tasted {4} (delicious) and the town looked {5} (beautiful). My son ate {6} (quick) because he wanted to play in the main square. On the way back, my dad drove {7} (safe), and we all slept {8} (peaceful) in the car.
ejercicios.explica: Antes de un sustantivo (a careful driver) y con taste o look va adjetivo; para describir la acción (drove slowly, ate quickly) va adverbio.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la palabra correcta en cada hueco.
ejercicios.texto: Hi team, thank you for this week. You all worked really {1} on the juice campaign, and the client loved it. {2} we have had too many late nights, so on Friday we finish at four. Laura, your headlines sound {3}. Mike, you presented the numbers very {4}. I know we {5} had time to sleep, but it was worth it. The client says the campaign looks {6}. Well done, everyone!
ejercicios.explica: Hard = con esfuerzo, hardly = casi no; lately = últimamente; well para la acción; con sound y look va adjetivo.

ejercicios.titulo: La app nueva de la oficina
ejercicios.instruccion: Escribe el adverbio de la palabra entre paréntesis. Cuidado con la ortografía (-ily, -ically, -ly).
ejercicios.texto: Our new project app is great. Tasks update {1} (automatic), and the app sends reminders {2} (immediate) when a deadline is close. You can find any file {3} (easy). {4} (basic), it's a calendar and a chat in one place. Camila set it up {5} (quick) and explained it to us {6} (patient). Now the team works more {7} (efficient), and nobody misses a meeting. {8} (honest), I wasn't sure at first.
ejercicios.explica: -ic → -ically (automatically, basically), consonante + y → -ily (easily) y el resto + -ly (quickly, patiently, honestly).

ejercicios.texto: Sarah is the new account director at Brava, and the team likes her a lot. She speaks Spanish fluently because she lived in Medellín for five years. She works hard, but she never stays late: she arrives early and leaves at six. In meetings she listens carefully and speaks quietly, so everybody pays attention. Last week a client shouted angrily during a call. Sarah answered calmly and politely, and in ten minutes the problem was solved. "She makes it look easy," says Andrés. Lately the team has been more relaxed, and the campaigns look better too. Her only problem? She drives terribly. Nobody wants to go to a client meeting in her car.

preguntas.q: How does Sarah speak Spanish?
What did Sarah do when the client shouted?
What is Sarah's only problem?
¿Por qué el texto dice «makes it look easy» y no «easily»?
opciones: Con look va adjetivo, porque describe la cosa y no una acción
Easy es un adverbio irregular, como fast

ejercicios.explica: Los adverbios describen cómo hace Sarah las cosas (fluently, carefully, calmly); con look va adjetivo (look easy, look better).

ejercicios.texto: Every Thursday, Andrés and his wife Paula take salsa classes in Chapinero. Paula dances beautifully; she learned as a child in Cali. Andrés dances badly, but he tries hard and he never gives up. The teacher, Mike, speaks slowly and explains every step clearly. "Move your feet quickly but softly," he says. At first Andrés hardly moved; now he dances quite well. Last week he stepped on Paula's foot. She laughed and said, "Don't worry, you're doing well." After class they usually eat empanadas. They taste great after an hour of dancing.

preguntas.q: How does Paula dance?
How does Mike explain the steps?
¿Qué significa «At first Andrés hardly moved»?
opciones: Al principio Andrés casi no se movía
Al principio Andrés se movía con mucho esfuerzo
Al principio Andrés se movía muy duro

preguntas.q: ¿Por qué «They taste great» y no «greatly»?
opciones: Con taste va adjetivo: describe las empanadas
Great es irregular, como good → well

ejercicios.explica: Hard = con esfuerzo, hardly = casi no; con taste va adjetivo (taste great).

ejercicios.texto: Hi Camila, thanks for your presentation yesterday. Honestly, it went really well. You explained the strategy clearly, and the client understood it immediately. Your slides looked great, and the video worked perfectly. Two small things for next time: speak a little more slowly at the beginning, and read the numbers carefully before the meeting, because one of the budget figures was wrong. Lately you have been working very hard, so please take Friday afternoon off. You deserve it. Best, Mike

preguntas.q: How did the presentation go, according to Mike?
What should Camila do at the beginning next time?
Why can Camila take Friday afternoon off?
opciones: She has been working very hard lately

preguntas.q: ¿Qué palabra del correo es adjetivo y no adverbio?

ejercicios.explica: It went well (resultado: adverbio), looked great (look + adjetivo), lately = últimamente, hard = con esfuerzo.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe a alguien de tu familia o a un amigo: cómo maneja, cómo cocina, cómo habla inglés o cómo baila. Usa adverbios de modo y al menos un adjetivo después de look, sound, taste o feel.

requisitos.texto: Usa un adverbio con -ly (slowly, carefully, fluently…)
Usa un adverbio irregular: well, fast, hard, late o early
Usa look, sound, taste o feel + adjetivo

ejercicios.ejemplo: My mom is an amazing cook. She cooks slowly and carefully, and her ajiaco always tastes delicious. My dad is different: he cooks fast and he talks loudly in the kitchen. My sister speaks English fluently because she lived in Toronto, and she dances beautifully too. When we are all together on Sundays, I feel great.
ejercicios.explica: Adverbio para la acción (cooks slowly, speaks English fluently); adjetivo con taste y feel (tastes delicious, feel great).

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe un correo corto de feedback a alguien de tu equipo después de una presentación: qué hizo bien, cómo habló y qué puede hacer diferente la próxima vez.

requisitos.texto: Usa well (no good) para una acción: did well, went well, presented well…
Usa un adverbio con -ly después del verbo o del objeto
Usa look o sound + adjetivo
Di cómo mejorar con more + adverbio (more slowly, more clearly…)

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Laura, thanks for the presentation this morning. Honestly, you did really well. You explained the strategy clearly and answered the client's questions calmly. Your slides looked great, and the video worked perfectly. For next time, try to speak more slowly at the beginning, and check the budget numbers carefully before the meeting. Great job! Best, Andrés
ejercicios.explica: Well para el resultado (you did well), -ly para cómo hizo cada cosa y adjetivo con look (looked great).

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta cómo te fue en algo reciente (una carrera, un partido, una clase, un examen): cómo lo hiciste, cómo te sentiste y qué ha cambiado últimamente.

requisitos.texto: Usa hard (con esfuerzo) o hardly (casi no)
Usa lately (últimamente)
Usa feel + adjetivo (feel good, felt tired…)
Usa did well o went well

ejercicios.ejemplo: Last Saturday I ran a 10K in Bogotá. I trained hard for two months, and I did really well: I finished in 52 minutes. At the end I felt tired but very happy. Lately I have been sleeping better and eating more carefully, and I feel great. My wife says I hardly complain about my knee now.
ejercicios.explica: Hard = con esfuerzo y hardly = casi no; lately = últimamente; feel + adjetivo (estado) y did well (resultado).

temas.resumen: Qué tiempo verbal pide cada marcador: yesterday, ago e in 2020 (pasado); now, at the moment, currently y these days (continuo); already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for y so far (perfecto); tomorrow, next week, soon e in two days (futuro). Y dónde van already, yet, still y just.

teoria.paraQue: Para que el marcador de tiempo te diga qué tiempo verbal usar antes de abrir la boca. Si dices yesterday, el verbo va en pasado; si dices already, va en perfecto; si dices tomorrow, va en futuro. El marcador es la señal de tráfico del verbo.
teoria.llave: La llave es el marcador: él elige el tiempo. Tiempo cerrado (yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020) → pasado simple. Momento presente (now, at the moment, currently, these days) → presente continuo. Periodo abierto o resultado (already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, so far) → presente perfecto con have/has. Lo que viene (tomorrow, next week, soon, later, in two days) → futuro con will o going to. Aprende cada marcador con su tiempo pegado.

formulas.formula: yesterday / last week / two years ago / in 2020 / the other day + pasado simple
formulas.ejemplo: I {{sent}} the proposal yesterday. We {{moved}} to Bogotá in 2020.

formulas.formula: now / right now / at the moment / currently / these days + be + -ing
formulas.ejemplo: We[['re]] {{work((ing))}} on a pitch at the moment.

formulas.formula: have/has + already / just / never / ever + participio · … yet (al final)
formulas.ejemplo: I[['ve]] {{already}} {{sent}} it. She [[has]]n't {{answered}} yet.

formulas.formula: have/has + participio + since + inicio / for + cantidad · so far / lately / recently
formulas.ejemplo: I[['ve]] {{worked}} here since 2020, for six years. So far we[['ve]] {{won}} three accounts.

formulas.formula: tomorrow / next week / soon / later / in two days / tonight + will / going to / be + -ing
formulas.ejemplo: I[['ll]] {{call}} you tomorrow. We[['re]] {{present((ing))}} next week.

formulas.formula: still antes del verbo y después de be · anymore al final, solo en negativas
formulas.ejemplo: I[['m]] still {{wait((ing))}}. I [[do]]n't {{work}} there anymore.

formulas.formula: by Friday (a más tardar) · until 6 (hasta) · during the meeting (durante) · on time (puntual) · in time (con margen)
formulas.ejemplo: I[['ll]] {{send}} it by Friday. I[['ll]] {{be}} here until 6.

reglas: Si el marcador cierra el tiempo (yesterday, last night, last week, two years ago, in 2020, the other day), el verbo va en pasado simple. Nunca have + yesterday.
Ago va después de la cantidad: two years ago, ten minutes ago. Y siempre con pasado simple.
Now, right now, at the moment, currently y these days piden presente continuo: lo que está pasando ahora o una tendencia temporal.
Already, just, ever y never van entre have y el participio: I've already sent it, Have you ever been…? Yet va al final, solo en negativas y preguntas: I haven't finished yet.
Since + punto de inicio (since 2020, since Monday); for + cantidad (for six years, for two hours). Los dos responden a How long…? y van con presente perfecto si el periodo sigue abierto.
So far, lately, recently y before (al final) piden presente perfecto porque el periodo sigue abierto o importa el resultado hoy.
Tomorrow, next week, soon, later, tonight e in two days (dentro de dos días) piden futuro: will para decisiones y promesas, going to o be + -ing para planes.
Still va antes del verbo y después de be: I still work there, I'm still waiting. Anymore va al final y solo en negativas: I don't work there anymore.
Nowadays pide presente simple (un hecho general de hoy). Eventually es «al final / con el tiempo», no «eventualmente». Finally es «por fin».
By Friday = a más tardar el viernes (plazo); until Friday = hasta el viernes (duración). On time = puntual; in time = a tiempo, con margen. During + nombre del evento, nunca + número.
Last, next, this, every, yesterday, tomorrow y tonight no llevan preposición: last week, next Monday, tonight (nunca in next week, in tonight).

usos.ejemplo: I {{went}} to the gym yesterday and I {{slept}} badly last night.

I[['ve]] never {{been}} to the Amazon. [[Have]] you ever {{been}} there?

usos.ejemplo: So far we[['ve]] {{finished}} the strategy, but the client [[has]]n't {{approved}} the budget yet.
I[['ll]] {{send}} you the files by Friday.
I[['ve]] {{worked}} at Brava since 2020, for six years.
We [[do]]n't {{work}} with print anymore. We[['ve]] recently {{hired}} two video editors.

errores.mal: I have sent the proposal yesterday.
errores.porque: Yesterday cierra el tiempo: pasado simple, nunca perfecto.

errores.mal: I am working at Brava since 2020.
errores.bien: I have worked at Brava since 2020.
errores.porque: Since pide presente perfecto, no continuo. En español «estoy trabajando desde» engaña.

errores.mal: We finished the video since two days.
errores.bien: We finished the video two days ago.
errores.porque: «Hace dos días» es ago, después de la cantidad.

errores.mal: I already send the invoice.
errores.porque: Already pide have + participio: 've sent.

errores.mal: I didn't finish yet the report.
errores.bien: I haven't finished the report yet.
errores.porque: Yet va al final y con presente perfecto.

errores.mal: I call you tomorrow.
errores.porque: Tomorrow pide futuro: will. El presente simple es para horarios fijos.

errores.mal: I don't work there still.
errores.porque: «Ya no» es anymore al final. Still va antes del verbo y significa «todavía sigo».

errores.mal: I'll be in the office by 6 pm, all afternoon.
errores.bien: I'll be in the office until 6 pm.
errores.porque: Until es hasta (duración); by es a más tardar (plazo).

contraste.nota: Yesterday cierra el tiempo (pasado). Just mira el resultado hoy (perfecto).
Pasado + for: ya terminó. Perfecto + for: sigo ahí.
Still = todavía sigue. Anymore = ya no (al final, negativa).
By = fecha límite. Until = hasta ese momento, todo el tiempo.

contraste.b: We {{arrived}} in time for the meeting.
contraste.nota: On time = puntual, a la hora. In time = a tiempo, con margen.

frases.en: I'll get back to you tomorrow.
We haven't received the feedback yet.
frases.es: Todavía no hemos recibido la retroalimentación.

frases.en: I've just sent you the files.
I need it by Friday at the latest.
frases.es: Lo necesito a más tardar el viernes.

frases.en: We're currently working on three campaigns.
frases.es: Actualmente estamos trabajando en tres campañas.

frases.en: I'm still waiting for the client's approval.
frases.es: Todavía estoy esperando la aprobación del cliente.

Long time no see! How long has it been?

teoria.tip: Mira el marcador antes que el verbo. Si tiene fecha o «ago», es pasado. Si dice «ya, todavía, desde, alguna vez», es perfecto. Si dice «ahora», es continuo. Si mira al futuro, will. El marcador elige el tiempo; tú solo obedeces.

palabras.ejemplo: I sent the proposal yesterday.

hueco.frase: I sent the proposal ___. (ayer)

palabras.nota: Pide pasado simple: el tiempo está cerrado. Nunca con have.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll call you tomorrow.

hueco.frase: I'll call you ___. (mañana)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro: will, going to o presente continuo con plan.

palabras.ejemplo: I'm working on the budget now.

hueco.frase: I'm working on the budget ___. (ahora)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo: algo que pasa en este momento.

palabras.ejemplo: She joined Brava two years ago.

hueco.frase: She joined Brava two years ___. (hace)

palabras.nota: Va después de la cantidad (two years ago) y pide pasado simple, nunca perfecto.

palabras.ejemplo: I've already sent the invoice.

hueco.frase: I've ___ sent the invoice. (ya)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto. Va entre have y el participio.

palabras.ejemplo: The client hasn't approved the budget yet.

hueco.frase: The client hasn't approved the budget ___. (todavía)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto en negativas y preguntas. Va al final de la frase.

palabras.ejemplo: We've just finished the presentation.

hueco.frase: We've ___ finished the presentation. (acabamos de)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto: have + just + participio. En EE. UU. también se oye con pasado simple.

palabras.ejemplo: We launched the campaign last week.

hueco.frase: We launched the campaign ___. (la semana pasada)

palabras.nota: Pide pasado simple. Sin preposición: nunca «in last week». Igual last month, last year.

palabras.ejemplo: We're presenting to the client next week.

hueco.frase: We're presenting to the client ___. (la próxima semana)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro. Sin preposición: nunca «in next week». Igual next month, next year.

palabras.ejemplo: I'm still waiting for the client's answer.

hueco.frase: I'm ___ waiting for the client's answer. (todavía)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo o presente simple. Va antes del verbo y después de be.

palabras.ejemplo: Laura is in a meeting at the moment.

hueco.frase: Laura is in a meeting ___. (en este momento)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo (o be en presente). Equivale a right now.

palabras.ejemplo: I've worked at Brava since 2020.

hueco.frase: I've worked at Brava ___ 2020. (desde)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto. Since + fecha o momento de inicio.

palabras.ejemplo: I've lived in Chapinero for six years.

hueco.frase: I've lived in Chapinero ___ six years. (durante / hace)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto cuando el periodo sigue abierto (for six years = y sigo). Con pasado simple si ya terminó.

palabras.ejemplo: Have you ever worked with a bank?

hueco.frase: Have you ___ worked with a bank? (alguna vez)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto en preguntas de experiencia. Va entre have y el participio.

palabras.ejemplo: I've never been to the Amazon.

hueco.frase: I've ___ been to the Amazon. (nunca)

palabras.nota: Con have pide presente perfecto: experiencia que no has tenido. Va entre have y el participio.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll send you the files soon.

hueco.frase: I'll send you the files ___. (pronto)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro con will. See you soon.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll finish the report later.

hueco.frase: I'll finish the report ___. (más tarde)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro, casi siempre will. Talk to you later.

palabras.ejemplo: I'm going to the gym tonight.

hueco.frase: I'm going to the gym ___. (esta noche)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro: going to o presente continuo con plan.

palabras.ejemplo: I slept badly last night.

hueco.frase: I slept badly ___. (anoche)

palabras.nota: Pide pasado simple. Nunca «yesterday night».

palabras.ejemplo: We moved to Bogotá in 2020.

hueco.frase: We moved to Bogotá ___ 2020. (en)

palabras.nota: Un año cerrado pide pasado simple. Si quieres «desde 2020», es since + perfecto.

palabras.ejemplo: We're currently working with three clients.

hueco.frase: We're ___ working with three clients. (actualmente)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo. Ojo: no significa «corrientemente».

palabras.ejemplo: Everyone is talking about AI these days.

hueco.frase: Everyone is talking about AI ___. (en estos días)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo: una tendencia temporal.

palabras.ejemplo: We've recently hired two designers.

hueco.frase: We've ___ hired two designers. (recientemente)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto (va entre have y participio o al final). Con una fecha concreta, pasado simple.

palabras.ejemplo: I haven't slept well lately.

hueco.frase: I haven't slept well ___. (últimamente)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto, sobre todo en negativas y preguntas. Va al final.

palabras.ejemplo: So far we've received ten proposals.

hueco.frase: ___ we've received ten proposals. (hasta ahora)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto: el periodo sigue abierto.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll send you the files by Friday.

hueco.frase: I'll send you the files ___ Friday. (a más tardar el)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro: una fecha límite. No es until.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll be at the office until 7.

hueco.frase: I'll be at the office ___ 7. (hasta)

palabras.nota: Marca el fin de una duración; va con cualquier tiempo. Para plazos usa by.

palabras.ejemplo: Please don't check your phone during the meeting.

hueco.frase: Please don't check your phone ___ the meeting. (durante)

palabras.nota: During + el nombre del evento (the meeting, the trip). Con cantidades (two hours) es for. Cualquier tiempo.

palabras.ejemplo: We had lunch and then we went back to the office.

hueco.frase: We had lunch and ___ we went back to the office. (luego)

palabras.nota: Ordena una historia en pasado simple. También «en esa época»: I was a student then.

palabras.ejemplo: The meeting ended at 5 and afterwards we had a beer.

hueco.frase: The meeting ended at 5 and ___ we had a beer. (después)

palabras.nota: Pasado simple en una narración (o futuro en un plan). En EE. UU. también afterward.

palabras.ejemplo: I don't drink coffee at night anymore.

hueco.frase: I don't drink coffee at night ___. (ya no)

palabras.nota: Solo en negativas, al final. Pide presente simple: un hábito que terminó.

palabras.ejemplo: Nowadays most people watch series on their phones.

hueco.frase: ___ most people watch series on their phones. (hoy en día)

palabras.nota: Pide presente simple: un hecho general de la época actual.

palabras.ejemplo: The designers are finishing the layout; meanwhile, I'm writing the copy.

hueco.frase: The designers are finishing the layout; ___, I'm writing the copy. (mientras tanto)

palabras.nota: Dos acciones a la vez: pide continuo (presente o pasado). Va al inicio de la frase.

palabras.ejemplo: We'll eventually move to a bigger office.

hueco.frase: We'll ___ move to a bigger office. (con el tiempo)

palabras.nota: Futuro (will) o pasado simple. Ojo: no es «eventualmente» (eso es occasionally).

palabras.ejemplo: We've finally signed the contract!

hueco.frase: We've ___ signed the contract! (por fin)

palabras.nota: Perfecto cuando algo por fin se logró; pasado simple al cerrar una historia.

palabras.ejemplo: The meeting started on time.

hueco.frase: The meeting started ___ time. (puntual: a la hora)

palabras.nota: A la hora exacta, ni antes ni después. Cualquier tiempo.

palabras.es: a tiempo (antes de que sea tarde)
palabras.ejemplo: We finished the video just in time for the launch.

hueco.frase: We finished the video just ___ time for the launch. (a tiempo: con margen)

palabras.nota: Con margen, antes del límite. Suele ir con for. Cualquier tiempo.

palabras.es: en dos días, dentro de dos días
palabras.ejemplo: The client arrives in two days.

hueco.frase: The client arrives ___ two days. (dentro de)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro: in + cantidad = dentro de. Nunca «within two days ago».

palabras.ejemplo: I ran into Mike the other day.

hueco.frase: I ran into Mike ___. (el otro día)

palabras.nota: Pide pasado simple: un día reciente no concreto.

palabras.ejemplo: Sorry, I can't talk right now.

hueco.frase: Sorry, I can't talk ___. (ahora mismo)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo o presente simple con modales (I can't talk right now).

palabras.ejemplo: I'm working from home this week.

hueco.frase: I'm working from home ___. (esta semana)

palabras.nota: Pide continuo si es algo temporal; perfecto si cuentas lo hecho hasta hoy (I've had three meetings this week).

palabras.ejemplo: I've seen this movie before.

hueco.frase: I've seen this movie ___. (antes)

palabras.nota: Al final de la frase pide presente perfecto: experiencia previa.

palabras.ejemplo: How long have you worked here?

hueco.frase: ___ have you worked here? (cuánto tiempo)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto; la respuesta lleva for o since.

palabras.ejemplo: The client is coming the day after tomorrow.

hueco.frase: The client is coming ___. (pasado mañana)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro. Lo contrario es the day before yesterday (pasado simple).

palabras.ejemplo: From now on, we'll send the report on Fridays.

hueco.frase: ___, we'll send the report on Fridays. (de ahora en adelante)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro con will: una regla nueva desde hoy.

ejercicios.explica: At the moment pide presente continuo: algo que pasa ahora.

ejercicios.q: I've ___ sent the invoice.
ejercicios.explica: Con have + participio, «ya» es already, entre have y el participio.

ejercicios.q: Have you ___ worked with a bank?
ejercicios.explica: «Alguna vez» en preguntas de experiencia es ever, entre have y el participio.

ejercicios.q: I ___ you tomorrow.
ejercicios.explica: Tomorrow pide futuro: will + verbo base.

ejercicios.q: We moved to Bogotá ___ 2020.
ejercicios.explica: Un año cerrado va con in y pasado simple. Since pediría perfecto.

ejercicios.q: She joined Brava two years ___.
ejercicios.explica: «Hace dos años» es two years ago: la cantidad primero y ago al final.

ejercicios.q: The client hasn't approved the budget ___.
ejercicios.explica: En negativas, «todavía no» es yet, al final de la frase.

ejercicios.q: Mike ___ (work) from home yesterday.
ejercicios.explica: Yesterday pide pasado simple: worked.

ejercicios.q: We ___ (present) the campaign next week.
ejercicios.explica: Next week pide futuro: will present, are going to present o are presenting (plan).

ejercicios.q: I ___ (live) in Chapinero since 2018.
ejercicios.explica: Since + inicio pide presente perfecto: have lived (o have been living).

ejercicios.frase: I'm reading a lot about AI these days.
ejercicios.explica: These days marca una tendencia temporal: presente continuo.

ejercicios.frase: Have you ever worked with a bank?
ejercicios.explica: Ever + have + participio: experiencia hasta hoy, sin fecha.
Cada marcador tiene su tiempo pegado: apréndelos en pareja.

ejercicios.frase: I have sent the proposal yesterday.

ejercicios.explica: Yesterday cierra el tiempo: pasado simple, sin have.

ejercicios.frase: We launched the campaign last week.

ejercicios.texto: I've just finished the report.
respuestas: I have just finished the report.

ejercicios.q: Last night I ___ (watch) a movie with my wife.
ejercicios.explica: Last night cierra el tiempo: pasado simple.

ejercicios.q: Right now we ___ (wait) for the client's feedback.
ejercicios.explica: Right now pide presente continuo: are waiting.

ejercicios.q: So far we ___ (receive) ten proposals.
ejercicios.explica: So far = hasta ahora: el periodo sigue abierto, presente perfecto.

ejercicios.q: The client ___ (arrive) in two days.
ejercicios.explica: In two days = dentro de dos días: futuro (will, going to, continuo) o presente simple si es un horario fijo.

ejercicios.q: I ___ (not / see) Andrés lately.
ejercicios.explica: Lately pide presente perfecto: haven't seen.

ejercicios.q: I don't eat meat ___. (ya no)
ejercicios.explica: «Ya no» en negativa es anymore, al final.

ejercicios.q: I ___ at Brava for six years, and I love it here.
ejercicios.explica: For six years con el periodo abierto (sigo ahí) pide presente perfecto.

ejercicios.q: We ___ the budget during yesterday's meeting.
ejercicios.explica: Yesterday's meeting cierra el tiempo: pasado simple aunque haya during.

ejercicios.q: Don't worry, I ___ it later.
ejercicios.explica: Later pide futuro con will: una promesa o decisión del momento.

ejercicios.es: Todavía estoy esperando la respuesta del cliente.
ejercicios.en: I'm still waiting for the client's answer.
ejercicios.explica: Still va después de be y antes del verbo -ing. Yet iría al final de una negativa.

ejercicios.es: ¿Alguna vez has trabajado con un banco?
ejercicios.en: Have you ever worked with a bank?
ejercicios.explica: Ever va entre have y el participio. Did pediría un momento concreto.

ejercicios.es: Te llamo mañana después de la reunión.
ejercicios.en: I'll call you tomorrow after the meeting.
ejercicios.explica: Tomorrow pide will: I'll call. Called es la trampa del pasado.

ejercicios.es: Hace dos años nos mudamos a Bogotá.
ejercicios.en: We moved to Bogotá two years ago.
ejercicios.explica: Ago va después de la cantidad y pide pasado simple: moved, sin have.

ejercicios.frase: I am working at Brava since 2020.
correccion: I have worked at Brava since 2020.
I've worked at Brava since 2020.
I have been working at Brava since 2020.
I've been working at Brava since 2020.

ejercicios.frase: We have finished the video two days ago.
correccion: We finished the video two days ago.
ejercicios.explica: Two days ago cierra el tiempo: pasado simple, sin have.

ejercicios.frase: I don't work with that client anymore.
ejercicios.explica: Anymore al final y en negativa: «ya no». La frase está bien.

ejercicios.frase: I have already send the invoice.
correccion: I have already sent the invoice.
I've already sent the invoice.
ejercicios.explica: Already pide have + participio: sent, no send.

ejercicios.frase: I sent the files yesterday.
ejercicios.instruccion: Cámbiala para hablar de mañana (tomorrow).
respuestas: I will send the files tomorrow.
I am going to send the files tomorrow.

I am sending the files tomorrow.

ejercicios.frase: We finished the report.

respuestas: We have just finished the report.

I have not finished the presentation yet.
I still haven't finished the presentation.
I still have not finished the presentation.

We're currently working with three clients.

Currently, we are working with three clients.

Currently, we're working with three clients.

Soon mira al futuro: see you soon o I'll see you soon.

respuestas: I didn't sleep well last night.
I did not sleep well last night.
Last night I didn't sleep well.
Last night I did not sleep well.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta qué hiciste ayer, qué estás haciendo esta semana, qué has hecho hasta ahora en el proyecto y qué vas a hacer mañana.
ejercicios.objetivo: yesterday + pasado simple · this week / at the moment + presente continuo · so far / already + presente perfecto · tomorrow + will / going to
ejercicios.ejemplo: Yesterday I had three meetings and I sent the budget to the client. This week I'm working on a pitch for a coffee brand. So far we've finished the strategy and we've already started the creative work. Tomorrow I'm going to present the first ideas to the team.
ejercicios.explica: Cada marcador manda su tiempo: yesterday → pasado; this week / at the moment → continuo; so far / already → perfecto; tomorrow → will / going to.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el tiempo que pide cada marcador.
ejercicios.texto: Yesterday I {1} (have) a long day at Brava. I {2} (get) to the office at 8 and we {3} (start) the status meeting on time. Right now I {4} (work) on the budget for a new client, and the designers {5} (finish) the layouts at the moment. We {6} (not / send) the proposal yet, but so far the client {7} (love) our ideas. Tomorrow I {8} (present) the final version.
ejercicios.explica: Yesterday y las horas cerradas → pasado; right now / at the moment → continuo; yet / so far → perfecto; tomorrow → futuro.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la palabra o el verbo en el tiempo correcto.
ejercicios.texto: Camila is a copywriter from Cali. She moved to Bogotá three years {1} (hace), when she got her first job at an agency. She {2} (live) in Chapinero {3} (desde) 2023, in a small apartment with a big window, and she {4} (work) at a digital agency {5} (durante: cantidad) two years now. On weekends she {6} (already / visit) Medellín and Cartagena with friends from the office, but she {7} (never / be) to the Amazon, which is her dream trip. {8} (hasta ahora), she loves the city: the food, the people and even the rain.
ejercicios.explica: Ago cierra el tiempo (pasado); since / for / already / never / so far piden presente perfecto.

ejercicios.titulo: El plan de la próxima semana
ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la opción correcta en cada desplegable.
ejercicios.texto: Next week is going to be busy. On Monday we {1} the new campaign to the client. {2} we have the budget meeting with the finance team. The designers {3} the final layouts by Wednesday. I {4} from home on Thursday because my daughter has a school event. {5}, on Friday, we're having a team lunch to celebrate the launch. I {6} back to you with the final dates soon.
ejercicios.explica: Next week y los días que vienen piden futuro (be + -ing, will, going to); afterwards y finally ordenan el plan.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el tiempo que pide cada marcador.
ejercicios.texto: Last Saturday I {1} (wake) up late, around 10. I {2} (go) to the gym and then I {3} (have) lunch with my parents in Chía. Afterwards we {4} (walk) around the town for an hour. These days I {5} (try) to spend more time with my family, because I {6} (not / see) them much lately. Tonight I {7} (stay) home and watch a series.
ejercicios.explica: Last Saturday, then y afterwards → pasado simple; these days → continuo; lately → perfecto; tonight → futuro.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la opción correcta en cada desplegable.
ejercicios.texto: Hi Sarah, I hope you're well. I {1} the revised proposal on Monday afternoon, with the new budget and the updated timeline, but I {2} your feedback yet. On our side, we {3} finished the video {4}, and the team is {5} working on the social media posts and the landing page. Could you confirm the budget {6} Friday? We need the final approval {7} time for the launch on the 25th, because the media plan starts that same week. Thanks a lot, and talk soon! Andrés
ejercicios.explica: On Monday (fecha) → pasado; yet y already → perfecto; still → continuo; by para el plazo e in time para llegar con margen.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el tiempo que pide cada marcador.
ejercicios.texto: Nowadays most of our clients {1} (want) short videos for social media. Five years ago, they {2} (ask) for TV commercials. At the moment we {3} (produce) around twenty videos a month, and so far this year we {4} (win) three new accounts. We {5} (not / work) with print anymore. Next month we {6} (hire) two more editors, and eventually we {7} (open) a small studio.
ejercicios.explica: Nowadays → presente simple; five years ago → pasado; at the moment → continuo; so far this year → perfecto; anymore → presente negativo; next month / eventually → futuro.

ejercicios.texto: Andrés is an account director at Brava. Last week he won a new client, a coffee brand from Huila, and yesterday he had the first meeting with their marketing team. At the moment his team is working on the strategy, and the designers are preparing three visual routes. So far the client has approved the budget and the timeline, but they haven't chosen a route yet. Andrés has already written the brief for the video, and tomorrow he's presenting the first ideas to the client's CEO. He needs the final approval by Friday, because the campaign launches in two weeks. He's a bit nervous, but so far, so good.

preguntas.q: When did Andrés win the coffee client?
What hasn't the client done yet?
When does Andrés need the final approval?
¿Por qué el texto dice «has approved» pero «had the first meeting»?
opciones: So far deja el periodo abierto (perfecto); yesterday lo cierra (pasado)
Approve siempre va en perfecto y have siempre en pasado
Son intercambiables; es cuestión de estilo

ejercicios.explica: Yesterday y last week → pasado; at the moment → continuo; so far / already / yet → perfecto; tomorrow / by Friday → futuro.

ejercicios.texto: Mike has gone to the same gym since January, so he has been a member for almost a year. Two years ago he hardly did any exercise, and he didn't sleep well. Last month he finally ran his first 10K in Bogotá, and he has already signed up for another race in Medellín. He has never lifted weights before, but these days he is trying a strength program with a trainer. He hasn't missed a class lately, and he feels much better. From now on, he says, he will train four times a week and eat less fast food. His wife, Laura, is not so sure: she has heard that promise before.

preguntas.q: How long has Mike been a member of the gym?
What did Mike do last month?
opciones: He signed up for the gym

preguntas.q: What is Mike doing these days?
¿Por qué «he has gone … since January» pero «two years ago he hardly did any exercise»?
opciones: Since abre el periodo hasta hoy (perfecto); ago lo cierra en el pasado (pasado simple)
Go siempre va en perfecto y do en pasado
Porque since es formal y ago es informal

ejercicios.explica: Since / for / never / lately → perfecto; two years ago / last month → pasado; these days → continuo; from now on → futuro.

ejercicios.texto: Hi Camila, here is a quick update on the launch. We've already finished the TV spot and we've just sent the final cut to your team. The social media posts are still in production; the designers are working on the last three pieces right now. Tomorrow we're recording the radio spot, and next week we'll present the media plan to your board. We need your comments on the posts by Thursday, so we can deliver everything in time for the launch on the 25th. So far we are on schedule and on budget. I'll send you the final report soon. From now on, we'll have a short status call every Monday at 9. Thanks, Mike.

preguntas.q: What has the agency just sent?
opciones: The final cut of the TV spot

preguntas.q: When are they recording the radio spot?
Why does Mike need the comments by Thursday?
opciones: To deliver everything in time for the launch
Because the launch is on Thursday
Because the designers finish on Thursday

preguntas.q: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre «by Thursday» y «in time for the launch»?
opciones: By es el plazo máximo; in time es llegar con margen antes del evento
By es informal e in time es formal

ejercicios.explica: Tomorrow, next week, by Thursday y soon → futuro; already / just / so far → perfecto; still → continuo.

ejercicios.texto: Last weekend Laura and Andrés went to Santa Marta. They flew on Friday night and then they took a bus to Taganga. On Saturday they went snorkeling; afterwards they ate fish on the beach and slept until noon on Sunday. Laura had never been to the Caribbean before, and she loved it. Now they are planning a longer trip: at the moment they're looking at hotels in Palomino, but they haven't booked anything yet. Andrés still has two weeks of vacation this year, so they're going back next month, probably with Laura's parents. They don't travel by bus anymore, though: next time they'll rent a car.

preguntas.q: How did they get to Taganga?
opciones: They flew to Santa Marta and then took a bus
They took a bus from Bogotá

preguntas.q: Had Laura been to the Caribbean before this trip?
What are they doing at the moment?
¿Por qué «they haven't booked anything yet» va en perfecto?
opciones: Yet deja el resultado abierto hasta hoy

ejercicios.explica: Last weekend / then / afterwards → pasado; now / at the moment → continuo; never / yet → perfecto; next month → futuro.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe sobre tu semana: qué hiciste ayer (yesterday), qué estás haciendo esta semana o ahora mismo (this week, right now) y qué harás mañana o la próxima semana.

requisitos.texto: Usa yesterday con un verbo en pasado
Usa this week, right now, at the moment o these days
Usa tomorrow, next week, soon o later
Usa will, 'll o going to para el futuro

ejercicios.ejemplo: Yesterday I had two client meetings and I sent the budget for the new campaign. This week I'm working on a pitch for a bank, so right now I'm reading a lot about financial apps. Tomorrow I'll present the first ideas to my team, and next week we're going to show them to the client.
ejercicios.explica: Cada marcador elige su tiempo: yesterday + pasado, this week / right now + continuo, tomorrow + will / going to.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta tu experiencia en tu trabajo actual: cuánto tiempo llevas (for / since), qué has logrado hasta ahora (already, so far, just) y qué no has hecho todavía (yet).

requisitos.texto: Usa for o since con presente perfecto
Usa already, just, so far, ever o never
Usa yet al final de una negativa
Usa have / has / 've / 's + participio

ejercicios.ejemplo: I have worked at Brava since 2020, so I've been here for six years. So far I've led campaigns for a bank, a coffee brand and two retail clients. I've already built a team of eight people and we have just won a new account. I haven't worked with an international client yet, but I have never stopped learning, and I'd love to try.
ejercicios.explica: Since / for abren el periodo; already / just / so far cuentan lo logrado; yet al final de la negativa cierra lo pendiente.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe un correo corto a un cliente con los próximos pasos del proyecto: qué harán la próxima semana, qué enviarán y para cuándo (by…), y qué pasará después (afterwards, then, eventually).

requisitos.texto: Usa next week, tomorrow, in two days o soon
Usa by + día o fecha para el plazo
Usa afterwards, then, eventually o finally
Usa will, 'll o going to

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Sarah, here are the next steps. Next week we're going to record the video and we'll send you the first cut by Friday. Then your team can review it, and we will make the changes in two days. Afterwards, we'll prepare the social media posts and the media plan. Eventually, the full campaign will be ready by the end of the month. Talk to you soon, Andrés.
ejercicios.explica: Next week / in two days / soon piden futuro; by marca el plazo; afterwards, then y eventually ordenan los pasos.

temas.resumen: Las frases que en español funcionan y en inglés no: I have 35 years, I am agree, explain me, make a question, actually, people is, depend of, married with, sensible, carpet, realize…

teoria.paraQue: Para dejar de traducir palabra por palabra. Estos errores no son de gramática: son frases que en español suenan perfectas y en inglés delatan al hispanohablante aunque todo lo demás esté bien. Son justo las que se te escapan en reuniones y emails.
teoria.llave: Pensar en inglés, no traducir. Cada calco tiene una pieza fija que lo reemplaza y que se aprende entera: no «tengo 35 años» sino *I'm 35*; no «estoy de acuerdo» sino *I agree*; no «explícame» sino *explain it to me*; no «hacer una pregunta» sino *ask a question*. Cuando dudes, pregúntate: ¿esto lo estoy traduciendo o lo he oído así en inglés?

formulas.formula: I'm + número (years old)
formulas.ejemplo: I[['m]] 38. / I[['m]] 38 years old.

formulas.formula: I agree / I don't agree / I disagree (verbo, sin be)
formulas.ejemplo: I {{agree}} with you. I [[don't]] {{agree}} with the deadline.

formulas.formula: explain / say / suggest + cosa + to + persona
formulas.ejemplo: {{Explain}} it to me. She {{said}} that to me.

formulas.formula: tell / ask / give + persona (sin to)
formulas.ejemplo: {{Tell}} me the truth. {{Ask}} him a question.

formulas.formula: ask a question · attend a meeting · make a decision · take a photo
formulas.ejemplo: [[Can]] I {{ask}} a question? I {{attended}} the meeting.

formulas.formula: depend on · married to · discuss (sin about) · arrive in/at
formulas.ejemplo: It {{depends}} on the budget. She[['s]] married to a lawyer. Let's {{discuss}} the plan.

formulas.formula: actually ≠ actualmente · sensible ≠ sensible · carpet ≠ carpeta · realize ≠ realizar
formulas.ejemplo: I[['m]] currently working on Honda. (actualmente) / Actually, it[['s]] cheaper. (en realidad)

formulas.formula: people + verbo en plural · sin the cuando es genérico
formulas.ejemplo: People {{are}} friendly in Medellín. (no «the people is»)

formulas.formula: I'm bored (yo lo siento) · it's boring (la cosa lo causa)
formulas.ejemplo: The meeting [[was]] boring, so I [[was]] bored.

reglas: La edad va con *be*: *I'm 38*. *Years* nunca va solo: o *I'm 38* o *I'm 38 years old*.
*Agree* es verbo: *I agree*, *I don't agree*, *Do you agree?*. Jamás *I am agree*.
*Explain*, *say*, *suggest*, *describe*: primero la cosa, luego *to me*: *explain it to me*, *say it to me*. Con *tell*, *ask*, *give*, *show*: la persona va pegada: *tell me*, *ask me*.
Preguntas se hacen con *ask* (*ask a question*), reuniones se asisten con *attend* (*attend a meeting*), decisiones se toman con *make* (*make a decision*).
*Actually* significa «en realidad, de hecho». Para «actualmente» usa *currently*, *right now*, *at the moment*.
*People* es plural: *people are*, *people have*. Sin *the* cuando hablas de la gente en general.
Preposiciones que no se traducen: *depend on*, *married to*, *discuss* sin nada, *listen to*, *arrive in* una ciudad.
*Sensitive* = sensible; *sensible* = sensato. *Folder* = carpeta; *carpet* = alfombra. *Realize* = darse cuenta; «realizar» es *do*, *carry out*, *complete*.
*Bored* es cómo te sientes; *boring* es cómo es la cosa. Si dices *I'm boring*, estás diciendo que eres aburrido.
Decir «dime» es *tell me*; *say me* no existe.

usos.uso: Decir tu edad y la de tu familia
usos.ejemplo: I[['m]] 38 and my son [[is]] 7.
My sister [[is]] married to a doctor. She[['s]] very sensitive.

usos.uso: Hablar de la gente de tu ciudad
usos.ejemplo: People in Bogotá {{complain}} about the traffic all the time.

usos.uso: Estar de acuerdo en una reunión
usos.ejemplo: I {{agree}} with Laura. I [[don't]] {{agree}} with the timing.
[[Can]] I {{ask}} a question? [[Could]] you {{explain}} that to me?

usos.uso: Contar lo que hiciste en el día
usos.ejemplo: I {{attended}} two meetings and we {{discussed}} the Q4 budget.
I[['m]] currently working on three campaigns.

errores.mal: I have 35 years.
errores.porque: La edad va con be.

errores.mal: I am agree.
errores.porque: Agree es verbo, no adjetivo.

errores.mal: Explain me the brief.
errores.porque: Explain lleva la cosa primero y la persona con to.

errores.mal: Can I make a question?
errores.porque: Las preguntas se hacen con ask.

errores.mal: I assisted to the meeting.
errores.porque: Assist es ayudar; asistir es attend, sin to.

errores.mal: Actually, I work on three accounts.
errores.bien: Currently, I work on three accounts.
errores.porque: Actually es «en realidad»; «actualmente» es currently.

errores.mal: People is very friendly.
errores.porque: People es plural.

errores.mal: It depends of the budget.
errores.porque: Depend on, siempre.

contraste.nota: Bored = estoy aburrido. Boring = soy aburrido (una persona aburridora). Cuidado.
Currently = actualmente. Actually = en realidad, de hecho (corrige algo).
Sensitive = sensible (se afecta). Sensible = sensata, con criterio.
Tell + persona. Say + cosa (+ to persona). Say me no existe.

frases.es: No estoy de acuerdo con eso.

frases.en: Could you explain it to me?
Can I ask you a question?
I attended a meeting with the client.
frases.es: Asistí a una reunión con el cliente.

frases.en: We need to make a decision today.
frases.es: Tenemos que tomar una decisión hoy.

frases.en: I'm currently working on the Honda account.
frases.es: Actualmente trabajo en la cuenta de Honda.

frases.en: Actually, the budget is smaller than we thought.
frases.es: En realidad, el presupuesto es más pequeño de lo que pensábamos.

frases.en: People are very friendly in Medellín.

frases.en: People say the traffic is getting worse.

frases.en: I'm bored. This meeting is too long.
frases.es: Estoy aburrido. Esta reunión es muy larga.

frases.en: The files are in the shared folder.
frases.es: Los archivos están en la carpeta compartida.

frases.en: I didn't realize the deadline was today.
frases.es: No me di cuenta de que la entrega era hoy.

frases.en: We completed the campaign on time.

teoria.tip: Haz tu lista negra personal: las cinco frases que más se te escapan (I am agree, explain me, I have X years, make a question, actually). Antes de cada reunión, léelas con su versión correcta. En dos semanas desaparecen.

ejercicios.q: Te preguntan la edad:
ejercicios.explica: La edad va con be: I'm 35 o I'm 35 years old. Nunca con have.

ejercicios.q: Estás de acuerdo con la propuesta:
ejercicios.explica: Agree es un verbo: I agree, sin am.

ejercicios.q: Pides que te expliquen el brief:
opciones: Could you explain it to me?
ejercicios.explica: Explain + cosa + to + persona: explain it to me.

ejercicios.q: Quieres preguntar algo en la reunión:
ejercicios.explica: Las preguntas se hacen con ask, no con make ni do.

ejercicios.q: Cuentas que fuiste a una reunión:
opciones: I attended a meeting with the client.
I assisted to a meeting with the client.
I assisted a meeting with the client.
ejercicios.explica: Asistir a una reunión es attend (sin to). Assist es ayudar.

ejercicios.q: Quieres decir «actualmente trabajo en la cuenta de Honda»:
opciones: I'm currently working on the Honda account.
I'm actually working on the Honda account.
Actually I work in the Honda account.
ejercicios.explica: «Actualmente» es currently. Actually significa «en realidad».

ejercicios.q: Llegas tarde:
ejercicios.explica: Sorry I'm late es la frase fija. Late es adjetivo, no sustantivo.

ejercicios.q: Te presentan a alguien:
ejercicios.explica: Nice to meet you. Know es conocer de hace tiempo.

ejercicios.q: Hay mucha gente en la oficina hoy:
opciones: There are a lot of people in the office.
There is a lot of people in the office.
There are a lot of peoples in the office.
ejercicios.explica: People ya es plural: there are … people. Peoples solo existe para «pueblos».

ejercicios.q: Una generalización sobre la gente:
ejercicios.explica: La gente en general: people, sin the y con verbo en plural.

ejercicios.q: La fecha de lanzamiento depende del cliente:
ejercicios.explica: Depend on, siempre, y con sujeto it.

ejercicios.q: Quieres discutir la propuesta con el equipo:
ejercicios.explica: Discuss va directo: discuss the proposal. Si quieres about, usa talk about.

ejercicios.q: Hablas de tu hermana:
ejercicios.explica: Married to, no with. El with del español no se traduce.

ejercicios.q: Le pides a un colega que te diga la verdad:
ejercicios.explica: Tell + persona directa: tell me. Say me no existe.

ejercicios.q: La película era aburrida y tú te aburriste:
opciones: The movie was boring, so I was bored.
The movie was bored, so I was boring.
The movie was boring, so I was boring.
ejercicios.explica: Boring es la cosa que aburre; bored es cómo te sientes.

ejercicios.q: Tu colega se ofende con facilidad:
ejercicios.explica: Sensible (en español) es sensitive. Sensible en inglés es sensato. Y person necesitaría a.

ejercicios.q: Dices dónde está el archivo:
ejercicios.explica: Carpeta es folder. Carpet es alfombra.

ejercicios.q: Terminaron la campaña a tiempo:
opciones: We completed the campaign on time.
We realized the campaign on time.
We did the realization of the campaign on time.
ejercicios.explica: «Realizar» es complete, do o carry out. Realize es darse cuenta.

ejercicios.frase: I have 40 years.
correccion: I'm 40 years old.
I am 40.
I am 40 years old.
ejercicios.explica: La edad va con be.

ejercicios.frase: I am agree with the client.
correccion: I agree with the client.
ejercicios.explica: Agree es verbo: sin am.

ejercicios.frase: Explain me the brief, please.
correccion: Explain the brief to me, please.
Could you explain the brief to me, please?
Explain it to me, please.
Could you explain the brief, please?
ejercicios.explica: Explain + cosa + to me.

ejercicios.frase: Can I make you a question?
correccion: Can I ask you a question?
Can I ask a question?
ejercicios.explica: Las preguntas se hacen con ask.

ejercicios.frase: I assisted to the meeting yesterday.
correccion: I attended the meeting yesterday.
I went to the meeting yesterday.
I was at the meeting yesterday.
ejercicios.explica: Asistir es attend, sin to.

ejercicios.frase: Actually, I'm working on three accounts. (quieres decir «actualmente»)
correccion: Currently, I'm working on three accounts.
Currently I'm working on three accounts.
Currently, I am working on three accounts.
Right now, I'm working on three accounts.
Right now I'm working on three accounts.
At the moment, I'm working on three accounts.
At the moment I'm working on three accounts.
I'm currently working on three accounts.
I am currently working on three accounts.
ejercicios.explica: Actually es «en realidad». Para «actualmente»: currently, right now, at the moment.

ejercicios.frase: People is very friendly in Medellín.
correccion: People are very friendly in Medellín.
ejercicios.explica: People es plural: people are.

ejercicios.frase: It depends of the budget.
correccion: It depends on the budget.
ejercicios.explica: Depend on.

ejercicios.frase: We need to discuss about the timeline.
correccion: We need to discuss the timeline.
We need to talk about the timeline.
ejercicios.explica: Discuss sin about. Talk about sí lleva about.

ejercicios.frase: She said me that the client was happy.
correccion: She told me that the client was happy.
She told me the client was happy.
She said that the client was happy.
She said the client was happy.
She said to me that the client was happy.
ejercicios.explica: Say no lleva persona pegada: o tell me o say (to me).

ejercicios.frase: I'm bored. This meeting is too long.
ejercicios.explica: Correcta: bored es cómo te sientes; la reunión sería boring.

ejercicios.frase: My brother is married with a lawyer.
correccion: My brother is married to a lawyer.
ejercicios.explica: Married to.

ejercicios.frase: Can you put the files in the carpet?
correccion: Can you put the files in the folder?
Could you put the files in the folder?
ejercicios.explica: Carpeta es folder; carpet es alfombra.

ejercicios.frase: I didn't realize the mistake until the client called.
ejercicios.explica: Correcta: realize = darse cuenta. Aquí está bien usado.

ejercicios.q: I'm 36 years ___.
ejercicios.explica: Years nunca va solo: I'm 36 years old.

ejercicios.q: I ___ with you, the deadline is too tight.
ejercicios.explica: I agree, sin am.

ejercicios.q: Can I ___ you a question?
ejercicios.explica: Ask a question, nunca make.

ejercicios.q: It depends ___ the client.
ejercicios.explica: Depend on.

ejercicios.q: She's married ___ an architect.
ejercicios.explica: Married to.

ejercicios.q: I'm ___ (bore), not boring: the presentation was two hours long.
ejercicios.explica: Bored = me siento aburrido. Boring = soy aburridor.

ejercicios.en: I'm 35 years old.
ejercicios.explica: I'm + número + years old. Sin have.

ejercicios.en: Explain it to me, please.
ejercicios.explica: Explain + it + to me.

ejercicios.es: Asistí a la reunión con el cliente.
ejercicios.en: I attended the meeting with the client.
ejercicios.explica: Attend sin to. Assist es ayudar.

ejercicios.es: La gente en Bogotá es muy amable.
ejercicios.en: People in Bogotá are very friendly.
ejercicios.explica: People es plural → are. Peoples no.

ejercicios.en: Let's discuss the proposal tomorrow.
ejercicios.explica: Discuss va directo, sin about. Let's sin to.
La edad con be: I'm 42.
Agree es verbo: se niega con don't.

respuestas: Can I ask you a question?
May I ask you a question?
Could I ask you a question?
ejercicios.explica: Ask a question.

respuestas: I'm currently working on three campaigns.
I am currently working on three campaigns.
Currently, I'm working on three campaigns.
Currently I'm working on three campaigns.
Currently, I am working on three campaigns.
Currently I am working on three campaigns.
I currently work on three campaigns.
Right now I'm working on three campaigns.
Right now, I'm working on three campaigns.
At the moment I'm working on three campaigns.
At the moment, I'm working on three campaigns.
ejercicios.explica: «Actualmente» es currently (o right now, at the moment). Nunca actually.
It depends on, con sujeto it.

ejercicios.es: La gente dice que el tráfico está peor.
respuestas: People say the traffic is worse.
People say that the traffic is worse.
People say that traffic is worse.
People say the traffic is getting worse.
People say that the traffic is getting worse.
People say traffic is getting worse.
People say that traffic is getting worse.

ejercicios.texto: I'm 35 years old and I agree with you.
respuestas: I'm 35 years old and I agree with you.
I am 35 years old and I agree with you.
I'm thirty-five years old and I agree with you.
I am thirty-five years old and I agree with you.
ejercicios.explica: Dos calcos en una frase: edad con be y agree sin am.

ejercicios.texto: Can I ask you a question about the budget?
respuestas: Can I ask you a question about the budget?
ejercicios.explica: Ask you a question: la persona va pegada a ask.

ejercicios.consigna: Preséntate con tu edad, di que estás de acuerdo con una idea de Laura y pide que te expliquen el nuevo cronograma. Tres frases sin calcos.
ejercicios.objetivo: I'm… / I agree with… / Could you explain … to me?
ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi, I'm Jonathan, I'm 38. I agree with Laura: the video is too long. Could you explain the new timeline to me?
ejercicios.explica: Tres calcos a evitar: I have X years → I'm X; I am agree → I agree; explain me → explain … to me.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta qué hiciste ayer en el trabajo usando: asistir a una reunión, hacer una pregunta y discutir el presupuesto.
ejercicios.objetivo: attended a meeting / asked a question / discussed the budget (sin to, sin about)
ejercicios.ejemplo: Yesterday I attended a meeting with Honda. I asked a few questions about the timeline, and then we discussed the budget for Q4.
ejercicios.explica: Attend a meeting (sin to), ask a question (no make), discuss the budget (sin about).

ejercicios.consigna: Describe a dos personas de tu equipo: con quién está casada una, si el otro es sensible al feedback, y de qué depende que lleguen a tiempo a la oficina.
ejercicios.objetivo: married to / sensitive / depends on
ejercicios.ejemplo: Camila is married to a designer, and they have two kids. Andrés is very sensitive to feedback, so I'm careful with him. Whether they arrive on time depends on the traffic, of course.
ejercicios.explica: Married to (no with), sensitive (sensible en español; sensible en inglés es sensato) y depend on (no of).

ejercicios.consigna: Explica en qué trabajas actualmente en la agencia y qué hace la gente de tu equipo, sin usar «actually» ni «the people».
ejercicios.objetivo: currently / right now / people are
ejercicios.ejemplo: I'm currently leading the Honda account. People on my team are mostly planners and creatives. Right now we're working on a campaign for Q4.
ejercicios.explica: «Actualmente» es currently o right now (actually es «en realidad»); la gente en general es people, sin the, con verbo en plural.

temas.resumen: Comparar dos cosas o personas, destacar una entre todas y decir que dos son iguales.

teoria.paraQue: Para comparar dos personas, cosas u opciones (taller than, more expensive than), para destacar una entre todas (the best, the most creative) y para decir que dos son iguales o no lo son (as talkative as, not as expensive as).
teoria.llave: La llave vive en el adjetivo: si es corto, cambia por detrás (-er, the -est); si es largo, la llave va delante (more, the most). Nunca las dos a la vez: more longer ✗. Después del comparativo va than; con la igualdad no hay than, hay as…as.

formulas.formula: adjetivo + -er + than
formulas.ejemplo: This office is bigg((er)) than the old one.

formulas.formula: more + adjetivo + than
formulas.ejemplo: This proposal is ((more)) expensive than the first one.

formulas.formula: the + adjetivo + -est
formulas.ejemplo: Laura is ((the)) tall((est)) person on the team.

formulas.formula: the most + adjetivo
formulas.ejemplo: It's ((the most)) creative campaign of the year.

formulas.formula: as + adjetivo + as
formulas.ejemplo: I'm ((as)) talkative ((as)) my girlfriend.

formulas.formula: not as + adjetivo + as
formulas.ejemplo: He isn't ((as)) easy-going ((as)) his sister.

reglas: Una sílaba: -er / the -est (tall → taller → the tallest; cheap → cheaper → the cheapest).
Termina en -e: solo añade -r / -st (nice → nicer → the nicest; large → larger).
Consonante + vocal + consonante: dobla la última letra (big → bigger → the biggest; hot → hotter).
Dos sílabas terminadas en -y: la -y pasa a -ier / -iest (happy → happier, busy → the busiest, easy → easier).
Dos o más sílabas (sin -y): more / the most (modern, expensive, talkative, organized, hard-working).
Irregulares: good → better → the best · bad → worse → the worst · far → farther/further → the farthest/furthest.
Than solo va con el comparativo (-er / more). Con as…as nunca va than.
Nunca dos llaves juntas: more better ✗, more longer ✗, the most biggest ✗.
Para decir «menos»: less + adjetivo + than (less expensive than) o not as…as (not as expensive as).
El superlativo lleva the y suele cerrar con in (in the team, in Colombia) o of (of the year, of all).

usos.uso: Comparar a tu familia o a tus amigos
usos.ejemplo: My sister is ((more)) organized than me, but I'm funni((er)).

usos.uso: Elegir entre dos planes, restaurantes o ciudades
usos.ejemplo: Medellín is warm((er)) than Bogotá, and the food is ((as)) good ((as)) here.

usos.uso: Comparar propuestas, marcas o presupuestos con el cliente
usos.ejemplo: Option B is cheap((er)), but option A is ((more)) creative.

usos.uso: Destacar un resultado o una campaña
usos.ejemplo: This was ((the most)) successful campaign of the year.
Andrés is ((the most)) hard-working person on the team.

errores.bien: This meeting is longer than the last one.
errores.porque: Long tiene una sílaba: la llave va detrás (-er), no delante (more).

errores.mal: Mike is more better than me.

errores.bien: It's the biggest office in Bogotá.

errores.mal: My sister is taller that me.
errores.bien: My sister is taller than me.
errores.porque: El «que» de la comparación es than, no that.

errores.mal: She is as talkative than her mom.

errores.mal: This is the more expensive option.

errores.mal: It was the baddest meeting of the year.
errores.bien: It was the worst meeting of the year.
errores.porque: Bad es irregular: worse / the worst.

contraste.nota: Than marca diferencia; as…as marca igualdad.

contraste.a: This office is bigg((er)) than the old one.

contraste.nota: Comparativo = dos cosas; superlativo = una entre todas (lleva the).
