ejercicios.explica: Lee las señales de tiempo: six months ago → pasado (gave, signed, put, pointed); now / today → presente (works, gets, writes); he's → -ing (looking forward to).

ejercicios.texto: Laura is an account director at Brava, an advertising agency in Bogotá. On Mondays she wakes up at 5:30, works out for forty minutes and gets to the office at 8. The first thing she does is log in to her computer and go over the emails from the weekend. At 9 the team has a status meeting, where everyone brings up the problems of the week and Laura writes them down. Last Monday the client for a new coffee brand showed up without an appointment and asked the team to come up with a new slogan in two days. Laura didn't give up: she set up a brainstorming session for the afternoon, and by Wednesday they handed in five options. The client picked the second one.

preguntas.q: What is the first thing Laura does at the office?
opciones: She logs in and goes over her emails
She works out for forty minutes
She sets up a brainstorming session

preguntas.q: Why did the client show up last Monday?
opciones: To ask for a new slogan in two days

preguntas.q: What did the team hand in by Wednesday?
En «Laura writes them down», ¿por qué them va en medio?
opciones: Porque write down es separable y el pronombre va obligatoriamente en medio
Porque them siempre va antes de la partícula en cualquier phrasal verb
Porque es un error del texto; debería ser «writes down them»

ejercicios.explica: Wake up, work out, log in, go over, bring up, write down, show up, come up with, give up, set up, hand in: la rutina de una oficina contada en phrasal verbs. Con pronombre, los separables lo llevan en medio.

ejercicios.texto: Last month Mike flew from Bogotá to Mexico City for a conference. He got up at 3 am, and his brother dropped him off at the airport at 4. He had checked in online, so he went straight to security. The plane was supposed to take off at 6, but it didn't take off until 8 because of the weather. Mike ran out of battery while he was waiting, and he couldn't look up the hotel address. When he finally landed, he picked up his suitcase, found a taxi and figured out the address with the driver's phone. He checked in at the hotel at 1 pm, took off his shoes and slept for two hours before the first talk. In the end, everything worked out, but he says he will never put off charging his phone again.

preguntas.q: Who dropped Mike off at the airport?
Why couldn't Mike look up the hotel address?
opciones: Because his phone ran out of battery
Because the plane took off late
Because he didn't check in online

preguntas.q: What does «everything worked out» mean here?
opciones: Mike did a lot of exercise
Mike resolved the problem with the plane

preguntas.q: «Take off» aparece dos veces. ¿Con qué significados?

ejercicios.explica: Un mismo phrasal verb puede tener varios sentidos: take off (despegar / quitarse), check in (aeropuerto / hotel), work out (salir bien). El contexto decide.

ejercicios.titulo: La reunión que casi no pasa
ejercicios.texto: On Thursday the Brava team had a presentation with a bank, their biggest client. Andrés arrived early to set up the projector, but it didn't turn on. He called IT and they sorted it out in ten minutes. Then Camila found out that the client's marketing director couldn't make it, so a new manager was taking over the account. Nobody knew her. Laura quickly looked her up on LinkedIn and pointed out that she had worked in digital campaigns for years. When the manager showed up, the team dealt with the change calmly: they went over the strategy, brought up two digital ideas and asked for her feedback. She loved it. After the meeting, Andrés followed up with a thank-you email and set up a second call for the following week.

preguntas.q: What problem did Andrés have before the meeting?
Why did Laura look up the new manager?
opciones: Because nobody on the team knew her
Because she was taking over Laura's job

preguntas.q: What did Andrés do after the meeting?
opciones: He sent a follow-up email and set up another call

preguntas.q: En «they sorted it out» y «looked her up», ¿qué regla se cumple?
opciones: Son separables, y el pronombre va en medio
Son no separables, y por eso el pronombre va al final
Los pronombres van siempre antes del verbo

ejercicios.explica: Set up, turn on, sort out, find out, take over, look up, point out, show up, deal with, go over, bring up, follow up: una reunión completa en phrasal verbs. Con pronombre, los separables se partan: sorted it out, looked her up.

ejercicios.texto: Andrés works a lot during the week, so Saturdays are for his family. He doesn't get up early: he wakes up around 8 and makes breakfast. His daughter Valentina signed up for swimming classes in September, so at 10 he drops her off at the pool and goes to the supermarket. Last Saturday they ran out of almost everything, so he filled up two carts. He picks Valentina up at 11:30, and they usually end up eating empanadas on the way home. In the afternoon, he turns off his work phone and looks after the kids while his wife, Camila, goes to yoga. At night they put on a movie. Andrés says it's the only day he doesn't deal with clients or check his email, and he looks forward to it all week.

preguntas.q: What does Andrés do while Valentina is at the pool?
Why did he fill up two carts last Saturday?
opciones: Because they had run out of almost everything
Because Valentina signed up for swimming

preguntas.q: What does Andrés turn off in the afternoon?
«He picks Valentina up at 11:30»: ¿es correcto?
opciones: Sí: pick up es separable y el sustantivo puede ir en medio
No: el sustantivo siempre va después de la partícula
No: pick up no es separable

ejercicios.explica: Get up, wake up, sign up for, drop off, run out of, fill up, pick up, end up, turn off, look after, put on, deal with, look forward to. Con sustantivo, el separable admite las dos posiciones: picks up Valentina / picks Valentina up.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe tu rutina de un día normal, desde que te despiertas hasta que llegas a la oficina, usando al menos cinco phrasal verbs (wake up, get up, put on, turn on/off, drop off, pick up, log in, go over…).

requisitos.texto: Usa wake up o get up
Usa put on o take off con ropa
Usa turn on o turn off
Usa drop off, pick up, log in o go over

ejercicios.ejemplo: I wake up at 5:30 and get up ten minutes later. I put on my gym clothes and work out for an hour. Then I take a shower, turn on the news and have breakfast with my wife. At 7:15 I drop off my daughter at school and drive to the office. When I arrive, I log in to my computer and go over my emails before the status meeting.
ejercicios.explica: En presente simple con I, el verbo queda en base: wake up, put on, drop off. Las partículas no cambian nunca.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta cómo resolvió tu equipo un problema con un cliente la semana pasada, en pasado: qué pasó, qué averiguaron, qué idea propusieron, cómo lo resolvieron y qué seguimiento hicieron.

requisitos.texto: Usa find out o figure out en pasado
Usa come up with en pasado
Usa sort out, deal with o work out en pasado
Usa follow up o set up en pasado

ejercicios.ejemplo: Last week the client called because the campaign video had the wrong logo. First, we found out that the designer had used an old file. Then Camila came up with a quick solution: she sorted it out with the production team in two hours and we sent a new version the same afternoon. The client was happy. The next day I followed up with an email and set up a short call to go over the final files.
ejercicios.explica: En pasado cambia solo el verbo: found out, came up with, sorted it out, followed up, set up (set no cambia). Con pronombre, los separables lo llevan en medio: sorted it out.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe un email corto a un cliente después de una reunión: agradece, di de qué le vas a hacer seguimiento, organiza una próxima llamada, pide que te devuelva la llamada o te confirme, y cierra diciendo que esperas con ganas la próxima reunión.

requisitos.texto: Usa follow up
Usa set up (a call / a meeting)
Usa call back o get back
Cierra con look forward to + -ing

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Sarah, thank you for your time yesterday. I will follow up on the budget questions with our finance team and send you the numbers by Thursday. I would also like to set up a short call for next week to go over the final timeline. Could you call me back or confirm a time that works for you? I'm looking forward to seeing you again soon. Best regards, Andrés
ejercicios.explica: El email de seguimiento en inglés se arma con phrasal verbs: follow up on, set up a call, call me back y, de cierre, looking forward to + -ing (nunca «to see»).

temas.titulo: Preguntas: what, where, when, who, why, how
temas.resumen: Pedir información con las palabras interrogativas (what, where, when, who, why, how, which, whose, how much/many/long/often/far, what time, what kind of) en cada tiempo, preguntas de sujeto sin llave (Who called?), preposición al final (Who with?) y preguntas indirectas (Could you tell me where…?).

teoria.paraQue: Para pedir información y no solo sí o no: dónde trabajas, a qué hora empieza la reunión, cuánto cuesta, por qué no vino el cliente. Las preguntas Wh- son el motor de cualquier conversación: con ellas entrevistas, haces un brief, pides direcciones y conoces a alguien.
teoria.llave: La estructura siempre es la misma: Wh- + llave + sujeto + verbo. La palabra interrogativa va primero y después viene la pregunta normal del tiempo que estés usando: do/does (presente), did (pasado), am/is/are/was/were (be y continuos), will (futuro), have/has (perfecto). Cambia la llave, no el orden. Where DO you work? → Where DID you work? → Where WILL you work? → Where HAVE you worked?

formulas.formula: Wh- + do / does + sujeto + verbo base
formulas.ejemplo: Where [[do]] you {{work}}? · What time [[does]] the meeting {{start}}?

formulas.formula: Wh- + did + sujeto + verbo base
formulas.ejemplo: Where [[did]] you {{go}} last weekend? · Why [[did]] she {{leave}} early?

formulas.formula: Wh- + am / is / are / was / were + sujeto
formulas.ejemplo: Where [[are]] you? · How old [[is]] your son? · How [[was]] the meeting?

formulas.formula: Wh- + am / is / are / was / were + sujeto + verbo-ing
formulas.ejemplo: What [[are]] you {{do((ing))}}? · What [[were]] you {{do((ing))}} at 9?

formulas.formula: Wh- + will + sujeto + verbo base
formulas.ejemplo: What [[will]] you {{do}} after the launch? · When [[will]] the client {{answer}}?

formulas.formula: Wh- + have / has + sujeto + participio
formulas.ejemplo: Where [[have]] you {{been}}? · How long [[has]] she {{worked}} here?

formulas.formula: Who / What + verbo conjugado (+ objeto)
formulas.ejemplo: Who {{called}}? · Who {{work((s))}} with Laura? · What {{happened}}?

formulas.formula: Wh- + llave + sujeto + verbo + preposición
formulas.ejemplo: Who [[did]] you {{talk}} to? · Where [[are]] you from? · What [[is]] this for?

formulas.formula: Could you tell me / Do you know + wh- + sujeto + verbo (orden de afirmación, sin do/does/did)
formulas.ejemplo: Could you tell me where the meeting room [[is]]? · Do you know what time it {{start((s))}}?

reglas: Orden fijo: Wh- + llave + sujeto + verbo. La palabra interrogativa nunca va sola delante del sujeto: «Where you live?» es español con palabras inglesas; se dice Where do you live?

La llave es la del tiempo: do/does en presente, did en pasado, will en futuro, have/has en perfecto. Con be y con los continuos, el propio be es la llave y se adelanta: Where are you? What are you doing?
Después de do/does/did el verbo vuelve a la base: Where did you go? (no «did you went»), What does she do? (no «does she does»).
Pregunta de sujeto: si el Wh- es quien hace la acción (Who called? What happened?), no hay llave y el verbo se conjuga como en una afirmación: Who works here? Who called you?
Compara: Who called Laura? (¿quién llamó a Laura? → sujeto, sin llave) vs. Who did Laura call? (¿a quién llamó Laura? → objeto, con did).
La preposición va al final, no delante: Who did you talk to? Where are you from? What are you looking for? «To whom» existe, pero es muy formal.
What vs. which: what es abierto (What color do you want?); which es entre opciones conocidas (Which one, the red or the blue?).
How + adjetivo/adverbio crea nuevas preguntas: how old (edad), how long (duración), how often (frecuencia), how far (distancia), how much (incontables y precio), how many (contables).
Pregunta indirecta (Could you tell me…? Do you know…?): después del Wh- el orden es de afirmación y desaparece do/does/did: Could you tell me where she works? (no «where does she work»).
Respuesta corta a la pregunta Wh-: no repitas toda la frase. Where do you work? — At Brava. Why are you late? — Because of the traffic.

usos.ejemplo: Where [[are]] you from? What [[do]] you {{do}}? How long [[have]] you {{lived}} in Bogotá?
How far [[is]] the hotel? What time [[does]] the store {{close}}? How much [[is]] it?

usos.uso: Preguntar por el fin de semana
usos.ejemplo: What [[did]] you {{do}} on Saturday? Who [[did]] you {{go}} with? How [[was]] it?
When [[are]] you {{com((ing))}} back? What [[will]] we {{do}} on Sunday? How about Friday?

usos.uso: Hacer un brief con el cliente
usos.ejemplo: Who [[is]] the target? What kind of campaign [[do]] you {{need}}? When [[is]] the launch? How much [[is]] the budget?
Who [[is]] {{work((ing))}} on the video? Why [[did]] the client {{reject}} it? How long [[will]] it {{take}}?
Where [[did]] you {{work}} before? How many people [[did]] you {{manage}}? Why [[do]] you {{want}} this job?
Could you tell me when the files [[will]] {{be}} ready? Do you know who [[is]] in charge?

errores.mal: Where you work?
errores.porque: Falta la llave. En presente simple la pregunta necesita do/does después del Wh-.

errores.mal: Where did you went?
errores.porque: Did ya marca el pasado; el verbo vuelve a la base: did you go.

errores.mal: What does she does?
errores.porque: Does ya lleva la -s; el verbo queda en base: does she do.

errores.mal: Who did call you?
errores.porque: Who es el sujeto (quién llamó): pregunta de sujeto, sin did.

errores.mal: What are you looking?
errores.porque: La preposición del verbo no se pierde: look for → What are you looking for?

errores.mal: Could you tell me where is the bathroom?
errores.bien: Could you tell me where the bathroom is?
errores.porque: En la pregunta indirecta el orden es de afirmación: where the bathroom is.

errores.mal: How many years do you have?
errores.porque: La edad en inglés va con be: How old are you? I'm 38.

errores.mal: What time the meeting starts?
errores.bien: What time does the meeting start?
errores.porque: Falta does; y con does el verbo queda en base: start.

contraste.nota: A: quién llamó a Laura (who = sujeto, sin llave). B: a quién llamó Laura (who = objeto, con did).
Misma estructura, solo cambia la llave: do (presente) → did (pasado). El verbo queda en base en los dos.

contraste.b: Could you tell me where the meeting room [[is]]?
contraste.nota: Directa: be se adelanta. Indirecta: orden de afirmación, be al final.
A: a qué te dedicas (hábito, presente simple). B: qué estás haciendo ahora (continuo).
How much: precio e incontables. How many: cosas que se cuentan, en plural.

frases.en: What time does the meeting start?
Who is in charge of this account?
frases.es: ¿Quién está a cargo de esta cuenta?

frases.en: Why did the client reject the proposal?
frases.es: ¿Por qué el cliente rechazó la propuesta?

frases.en: Could you tell me when the files will be ready?
frases.es: ¿Me podrías decir cuándo estarán listos los archivos?

frases.en: What kind of campaign do you have in mind?
frases.es: ¿Qué tipo de campaña tienen en mente?

frases.en: How far is it from here?

teoria.tip: Arma la pregunta en dos pasos: primero la pregunta de sí/no (Do you work in Bogotá?) y luego pega el Wh- delante y quita la respuesta (Where do you work?). Si el Wh- es quien hace la acción (Who called?), no pegues nada: la frase ya es la pregunta.

palabras.ejemplo: What do you do? — I'm an account director.

hueco.frase: ___ do you do? — I'm an account director. (qué)

palabras.nota: La más general: cosas, acciones, información. What do you do? = ¿a qué te dedicas?

palabras.ejemplo: Where do you live? — In Chapinero.

hueco.frase: ___ do you live? — In Chapinero. (dónde)

palabras.nota: Lugar y destino. Where are you from? / Where are you going?

palabras.ejemplo: When is the deadline? — Next Friday.

hueco.frase: ___ is the deadline? — Next Friday. (cuándo)

palabras.nota: Momento general: día, mes, año. Para la hora exacta, what time.

palabras.ejemplo: Who is your account director? — Laura.

hueco.frase: ___ is your account director? — Laura. (quién)

palabras.nota: Personas. Si pregunta por el sujeto no lleva llave: Who called? (no «Who did call?»).

palabras.ejemplo: Why are you late? — Because of the traffic.

hueco.frase: ___ are you late? — Because of the traffic. (por qué)

palabras.nota: Razón. La respuesta empieza con because. Why don't we…? = ¿por qué no…? (propuesta).

palabras.ejemplo: How do you get to work? — By bike.

hueco.frase: ___ do you get to work? — By bike. (cómo)

palabras.nota: Manera y estado. How are you? / How was the meeting? / How do you spell it?

palabras.ejemplo: Which option do you prefer, A or B?

hueco.frase: ___ option do you prefer, A or B? (cuál de estas)

palabras.nota: Cuando hay un grupo cerrado de opciones. What color? (abierto) vs. Which color, red or blue? (cerrado).

palabras.ejemplo: Whose laptop is this? — It's Mike's.

hueco.frase: ___ laptop is this? — It's Mike's. (de quién)

palabras.nota: Posesión. Suena igual que who's (who is), pero se escribe distinto. Whose + sustantivo.

palabras.ejemplo: How much is the ticket? — 80,000 pesos.

hueco.frase: ___ is the ticket? — 80,000 pesos. (cuánto)

palabras.nota: Precio y cosas que no se cuentan: how much time, how much money, how much coffee.

palabras.ejemplo: How many people are on your team? — Six.

hueco.frase: ___ people are on your team? — Six. (cuántos)

palabras.nota: Cosas que se cuentan, en plural: how many people, how many meetings, how many days.

palabras.ejemplo: How long have you worked here? — For six years.

hueco.frase: ___ have you worked here? — For six years. (cuánto tiempo)

palabras.nota: Duración. Se responde con for o since. How long does it take? = ¿cuánto se demora?

palabras.ejemplo: How often do you go to the gym? — Three times a week.

hueco.frase: ___ do you go to the gym? — Three times a week. (cada cuánto)

palabras.nota: Frecuencia. Se responde con every day, once a week, twice a month.

palabras.es: a qué distancia, qué tan lejos
palabras.ejemplo: How far is the office from your house? — About 20 minutes.

hueco.frase: ___ is the office from your house? — About 20 minutes. (qué tan lejos)

palabras.nota: Distancia. How far is it to…? Se responde con kilómetros o minutos.

palabras.ejemplo: What time does the meeting start? — At 10.

hueco.frase: ___ does the meeting start? — At 10. (a qué hora)

palabras.nota: Hora exacta. When es más general. What time is it? = ¿qué hora es?

palabras.es: qué tipo de, qué clase de
palabras.ejemplo: What kind of music do you like?

hueco.frase: ___ music do you like? (qué tipo de)

palabras.nota: Tipo o categoría. What kind of clients do you work with? Variante: what type of.

palabras.ejemplo: How old is your daughter? — She's eight.

hueco.frase: ___ is your daughter? — She's eight. (cuántos años)

palabras.nota: Edad, siempre con be: How old are you? I'm 38. Nunca «how many years do you have».

palabras.ejemplo: I'm free on Thursday. How about you?

hueco.frase: I'm free on Thursday. ___ you? (¿y tú?)

palabras.nota: Para proponer o devolver la pregunta: How about Friday? How about you? Variante: what about.

palabras.ejemplo: What is this meeting for? — To approve the budget.

hueco.frase: What is this meeting ___? — To approve the budget. (para qué)

palabras.nota: Para qué: la preposición for va al final. What do you need it for? = ¿para qué lo necesitas?

palabras.ejemplo: Who did you go to the concert with?

hueco.frase: Who did you go to the concert ___? (con quién)

palabras.nota: La preposición va al final en el inglés hablado: Who with? Who are you talking to? Where are you from?

palabras.ejemplo: Could you tell me where the meeting room is?

hueco.frase: ___ where the meeting room is? (¿me podrías decir…?)

palabras.nota: Pregunta indirecta, más cortés. Después del wh-, orden de afirmación: where the room IS (no «where is the room»).

ejercicios.q: ___ do you live? — In Chapinero.
ejercicios.explica: La respuesta es un lugar, así que la pregunta es where. Después viene la llave do y el sujeto.

ejercicios.q: ___ time does the meeting start? — At 10.
ejercicios.explica: La hora exacta se pregunta con what time. Luego la llave does y el verbo en base: start.

ejercicios.q: ___ called this morning? — The client.
ejercicios.explica: Who es el sujeto (quién llamó): pregunta de sujeto, sin llave, verbo conjugado en pasado.

ejercicios.q: ___ are you late? — Because of the traffic.
ejercicios.explica: La respuesta empieza con because: la pregunta es why. Con be, la llave es el propio are.

ejercicios.q: Where ___ you work? — At Brava, an agency in Bogotá.
ejercicios.explica: Presente simple con you: la llave es do. Are es para be o continuos; does es para he/she/it.

ejercicios.q: What ___ you doing right now?
ejercicios.explica: Doing (-ing) y right now piden presente continuo: la llave es are, no do.

ejercicios.q: Where ___ you go last weekend? — To Villa de Leyva.
ejercicios.explica: Last weekend es pasado: la llave es did y el verbo queda en base (go).

ejercicios.q: ___ coffee do you drink a day? — Three cups.
ejercicios.explica: Coffee es incontable: how much. How many va con plurales (how many cups).

ejercicios.q: ___ do you live? — In Bogotá. (dónde)
ejercicios.explica: Lugar → where. Después, la llave do y el sujeto you.

ejercicios.q: ___ does the status call start? — At 9. (a qué hora)
ejercicios.explica: Hora exacta → what time (when también vale, es más general). La llave does va después.

ejercicios.q: Where ___ you work? (llave del presente simple)
ejercicios.explica: Wh- + llave + sujeto + verbo: Where DO you work? Sin la llave la pregunta queda en español.

ejercicios.q: What ___ you do yesterday? (llave del pasado)
ejercicios.explica: Yesterday → pasado → did. El verbo do queda en base porque did ya marca el tiempo.
Who (quién) y whose (de quién) se parecen: whose siempre va con un sustantivo (whose laptop).
How + adjetivo crea una pregunta nueva: often (frecuencia), long (duración), far (distancia), much/many (cantidad).

ejercicios.en: Where do you work?
ejercicios.explica: Wh- + do + you + verbo base. Works (con -s) y are son las trampas: la llave es do.

ejercicios.en: What time does the meeting start?
ejercicios.explica: Does lleva la -s; el verbo queda en base: start. Do no sirve con the meeting (it).

ejercicios.frase: Where you live?
correccion: Where do you live?
ejercicios.explica: Falta la llave: en presente simple la pregunta necesita do después del Wh-.

ejercicios.texto: What time do you usually get to the office?
respuestas: What time do you usually get to the office?
ejercicios.explica: What time + do + you + verbo. El do suena corto y débil entre time y you: afina el oído.

ejercicios.q: Where ___ you go on vacation last year? (llave)
ejercicios.explica: Last year → pasado → did. Después, el verbo en base: go.

ejercicios.q: What ___ you doing when I called you yesterday? (llave)
ejercicios.explica: Doing + pasado (when I called) → pasado continuo: were you doing.

ejercicios.q: How long ___ you worked at Brava? (llave)
ejercicios.explica: How long + participio (worked) → presente perfecto: have you worked.

ejercicios.q: Who ___ the meeting yesterday? — Laura did. (cancel)
ejercicios.explica: Who es el sujeto (quién canceló): sin did, el verbo va conjugado en pasado: Who canceled…?

ejercicios.q: ___ bag is this? — It's Mike's. (de quién)
ejercicios.explica: Posesión → whose + sustantivo. No confundir con who's (who is).

ejercicios.q: ___ sent this email? — Camila.
ejercicios.explica: Who es el sujeto (quién envió): pregunta de sujeto, sin llave: Who sent…?

ejercicios.q: Who ___ you talk to at the client's office?
ejercicios.explica: Aquí who es el objeto (con quién hablaste): necesita llave, y en pasado es did. La preposición to queda al final.

ejercicios.q: Could you tell me where ___?
ejercicios.explica: Pregunta indirecta: después de where el orden es de afirmación: the meeting room is.

ejercicios.frase: She works in Medellín.
ejercicios.instruccion: Pregunta por el lugar (Where…?).
ejercicios.explica: Wh- + does + she + verbo base: Where does she work? La -s pasa de works a does.

ejercicios.frase: They launched the campaign in October.
ejercicios.instruccion: Pregunta por el momento (When…?).
respuestas: When did they launch the campaign?
ejercicios.explica: Pasado → did + verbo base: did they launch. La -ed desaparece porque did ya marca el tiempo.

ejercicios.frase: Mike is talking to the client.
ejercicios.instruccion: Pregunta por la persona (Who… to?).
ejercicios.explica: Con el continuo, la llave es is y se adelanta: Who is Mike talking to? La preposición to va al final.

ejercicios.frase: We have three meetings today.
ejercicios.instruccion: Pregunta por la cantidad (How many…?).
respuestas: How many meetings do you have today?
How many meetings do we have today?
ejercicios.explica: How many + sustantivo plural + do + sujeto + verbo: How many meetings do you have today?

ejercicios.frase: Where is the bathroom?
ejercicios.instruccion: Hazla indirecta: Could you tell me…?
respuestas: Could you tell me where the bathroom is?
ejercicios.explica: En la indirecta, be vuelve al final: where the bathroom is. Nada de «where is the bathroom» después de tell me.

ejercicios.frase: Where did you went last night?
correccion: Where did you go last night?
ejercicios.explica: Did ya marca el pasado; el verbo vuelve a la base: did you go.

ejercicios.frase: What time does the presentation start?
ejercicios.explica: Correcta: what time + does + the presentation + start (verbo en base).

ejercicios.frase: Who did call you this morning?
correccion: Who called you this morning?
ejercicios.explica: Who es el sujeto (quién te llamó): pregunta de sujeto, sin did: Who called you?

ejercicios.en: Who did you go to the concert with?
ejercicios.explica: Did + verbo base (go), y la preposición with al final. «With whom» es muy formal.

ejercicios.en: How long have you worked here?
ejercicios.explica: How long + have + you + participio: presente perfecto. Do es la trampa del presente simple.

ejercicios.es: ¿Me podrías decir a qué hora cierra la tienda?
ejercicios.en: Could you tell me what time the store closes?
ejercicios.explica: Indirecta: sin does, y el verbo lleva la -s porque es afirmación: the store closes.

respuestas: Where did you have lunch today?
ejercicios.explica: Pasado → where + did + you + verbo base: have lunch / eat lunch.

respuestas: How many people are there on your team?
How many people are on your team?
How many people are there in your team?
How many people are in your team?
How many people do you have on your team?
How many people do you have in your team?
ejercicios.explica: People es plural: how many. Con there is/are, la llave es are: How many people are there…?

ejercicios.es: ¿Por qué no viniste a la reunión?
respuestas: Why didn't you come to the meeting?
Why didn't you go to the meeting?
Why didn't you attend the meeting?
ejercicios.explica: Pasado negativo: why + didn't + you + verbo base (come). Nunca «didn't came».

ejercicios.texto: How often do you go to the gym?
respuestas: How often do you go to the gym?
ejercicios.explica: How often + do + you + verbo: la frecuencia se pregunta así y se responde con twice a week, every day.

ejercicios.consigna: Imagina que entrevistas a una persona nueva para tu equipo. Hazle seis preguntas en voz alta: dónde trabajaba antes, cuánto tiempo estuvo allí, por qué quiere este trabajo, qué tipo de campañas ha hecho, cuántas personas ha manejado y a qué hora le gusta empezar el día.
ejercicios.objetivo: Wh- + llave + sujeto + verbo en distintos tiempos: Where did…? How long were…? Why do…? What kind of… have…? How many… did…? What time do…?
ejercicios.ejemplo: Where did you work before? How long were you there? Why do you want this job? What kind of campaigns have you worked on? How many people did you manage? What time do you like to start your day?
ejercicios.explica: La estructura no cambia; cambia la llave según el tiempo: did (pasado), do (presente), have (perfecto), were (be en pasado).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa cada pregunta con la llave correcta: do, does, did, are, were, have o will.
ejercicios.texto: Laura is interviewing a candidate for the creative team. «Thanks for coming, Sarah. Where {1} you work right now?» «At a small agency in Medellín.» «And how long {2} you worked there?» «For three years.» «Where {3} you work before that?» «In Cali, at a design studio.» «What {4} you doing there, exactly?» «I was designing packaging.» «Why {5} you want to change jobs?» «I want to work on bigger campaigns.» «What kind of clients {6} you like?» «Food and beverage brands.» «Okay. When {7} you be able to start?» «In two weeks.» «Perfect. One last question: who {8} the person who recommended you?»
ejercicios.explica: Lee las señales: right now → do; how long + worked → have; before that → did; doing + pasado → were; start en el futuro → will. La última es be: who is the person…?

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la palabra interrogativa correcta para cada pregunta del brief.
ejercicios.texto: Andrés has his first meeting with a new client, a coffee brand. He opens his notebook and asks: «{1} is your target consumer?» «Young professionals.» «{2} kind of campaign do you have in mind?» «Something digital.» «{3} is the launch?» «In March.» «{4} is the budget?» «Around 200 million pesos.» «{5} cities will the campaign run in?» «Bogotá and Medellín.» «{6} did you decide to change agencies?» «We wanted fresh ideas.» «{7} will be our main contact on your side?» «Me and the marketing manager.» «And {8} do you usually send feedback, by email or in meetings?»
ejercicios.explica: La respuesta te dice el Wh-: persona → who; tipo → what kind of; fecha → when; dinero → how much; opciones cerradas → which; razón → why; manera → how.

ejercicios.titulo: Preguntas con cortesía en el hotel
ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la versión correcta de cada pregunta indirecta.
ejercicios.texto: Mike arrives at a hotel in Cartagena for a conference. At the front desk he says: «Good afternoon. Could you tell me {1}?» «It's at 3 pm, sir.» «And do you know {2}?» «On the second floor, next to the pool.» «Great. Can you tell me {3}?» «From 6:30 to 10 am.» «One more thing: could you tell me {4}?» «About fifteen minutes by taxi.» «Do you know {5}?» «Around 20,000 pesos.» «Thank you. Oh, and could you tell me {6}?» «Yes, it's free for guests. The password is on your key card.»

opciones: how far the convention center is
how far is the convention center
how far does the convention center is
how much does a taxi cost

ejercicios.explica: Después de Could you tell me / Do you know, el orden es de afirmación: sujeto + verbo (check-in is, a taxi costs). Sin do/does y sin adelantar be. Para sí/no se usa if.

ejercicios.titulo: ¿Quién hizo qué? El lunes después del lanzamiento
ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la forma correcta. Si Who es el sujeto, el verbo va conjugado sin llave; si es el objeto, usa did + verbo base.
ejercicios.texto: The campaign launched on Friday and on Monday Laura wants to know everything. «Who {1} (approve) the final video?» «The client did, on Thursday.» «Who {2} (talk) to about the budget?» «I talked to Camila.» «Who {3} (post) the first ad on Instagram?» «Mike posted it at 8 am.» «And who {4} (call) when the website went down?» «I called IT immediately.» «Who {5} (fix) it?» «Andrés fixed it in twenty minutes.» «Who {6} (email) the results to?» «I emailed them to the whole client team.» «Great. Who {7} (write) the report?» «Camila wrote it.»
ejercicios.explica: Mira la respuesta: si contesta quién hizo la acción (The client did, Mike posted), who es sujeto → sin did. Si contesta a quién o con quién (I talked to Camila), who es objeto → did you + base.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa cada pregunta de la conversación con la llave correcta: do, does, did, are, were, is, was, have o will.
ejercicios.texto: Camila texts her friend Daniela on Sunday. «Hey! How {1} your weekend?» «Great! I went to Guatavita.» «Nice! Who {2} you go with?» «With my sister.» «What {3} you doing there, hiking?» «Yes, we hiked around the lake.» «How long {4} it take to get there?» «About two hours by car.» «And what {5} you doing now?» «Cooking lunch.» «What time {6} you usually have lunch on Sundays?» «Around 2.» «{7} you ever been to Villa de Leyva? I'm going next weekend.» «Yes, twice!» «Where {8} we stay, then? Any recommendations?»
ejercicios.explica: La llave sigue al tiempo: pasado (was, did, were), ahora (are), hábito (do), experiencia (have…ever), futuro (will). El Wh- va siempre primero y el orden no cambia.

ejercicios.titulo: La primera reunión con el cliente
ejercicios.texto: Last Tuesday Andrés had his first meeting with a new client, a Colombian sports brand. He prepared a list of questions the night before, because a good brief starts with good questions. First he asked, «Who is your target consumer?» The marketing director answered, «Men and women between 25 and 40 who run or go to the gym.» Then he asked, «What kind of campaign do you have in mind?» and «When is the launch?» They wanted a digital campaign for March. Andrés also asked how much the budget was and how many cities the campaign would run in. The hardest question was the last one: «Why did you leave your previous agency?» The director smiled and said, «Because they never asked us questions.» Andrés wrote that down. He knew the account was his.

preguntas.q: Why did Andrés prepare questions the night before?
opciones: Because a good brief starts with good questions
Because the client asked him to
Because he didn't know the brand

preguntas.q: Who is the brand's target consumer?
opciones: People between 25 and 40 who run or go to the gym

preguntas.q: Why did the client leave their previous agency?
opciones: Because the agency never asked them questions
Because the budget was too high

preguntas.q: En «Who is your target consumer?», ¿por qué no hay do/does?
opciones: Porque el verbo es be, y be es su propia llave: se adelanta

ejercicios.explica: Who is…? (be adelantado), What kind of… do you…? (do), When is…? (be), How much / How many…, Why did you…? (did + base). Un brief entero en preguntas Wh-.

ejercicios.texto: Mike arrived in Cartagena on Friday for a conference. At the airport he asked a taxi driver, «How far is the hotel from here?» The driver said twenty minutes, but it took almost an hour because of the traffic. When Mike got to the hotel, the receptionist asked him, «Where are you from?» and «How long are you staying?» He answered, «From Bogotá, for three nights.» Then Mike asked, «Could you tell me where the convention center is?» It was only two blocks away. On Saturday night he got lost in the old city, so he asked a woman, «Do you know what time the last bus leaves?» She laughed and said there were no buses in the walled city, only taxis. Mike asked her how much a taxi cost, and she said about 15,000 pesos. He thanked her and took one back to the hotel.

preguntas.q: How long did it take Mike to get to the hotel?
What did the receptionist want to know?
opciones: Where Mike was from and how long he was staying

preguntas.q: Why did the woman laugh?
opciones: Because there were no buses in the walled city

preguntas.q: «Could you tell me where the convention center is?»: ¿por qué «is» va al final?
opciones: Porque en la pregunta indirecta el orden es de afirmación
Porque where siempre va con is al final
Porque es un error del texto

ejercicios.explica: Directas: How far is…? Where are you from? How long are you staying? Indirectas: Could you tell me where … is? Do you know what time … leaves? En las indirectas, el verbo vuelve a su lugar.

ejercicios.texto: Every Monday at 9, Laura runs the status meeting at Brava, and the team calls it «the interrogation» because she asks a lot of questions. «Who is working on the coffee video?» Mike raises his hand. «How long will it take?» «Two more days.» «Why did the client reject the first version?» «Because the music was too slow.» Then she turns to Camila: «What did you send the bank on Friday?» «The media plan and the budget.» «When will they answer?» «They said by Wednesday.» «And who called this morning?» «The sports brand. They want a new slogan.» Laura smiles. «Okay. How many ideas do we have?» Silence. «That's what I thought. Brainstorming at 11. Who's bringing the coffee?» Everybody laughs. The meeting takes twenty minutes, and everybody leaves knowing exactly what to do.

preguntas.q: Why does the team call the meeting «the interrogation»?
opciones: Because Laura asks a lot of questions
Because it takes a long time

preguntas.q: Why did the client reject the first version of the video?
opciones: Because the music was too slow
Because it took two more days

preguntas.q: Who called this morning?
«Who called this morning?» y «What did you send…?»: ¿por qué una lleva did y la otra no?
opciones: En la primera who es el sujeto (sin llave); en la segunda what es el objeto (con did)
Porque who nunca lleva did y what siempre
Porque la primera es presente y la segunda pasado

ejercicios.explica: Who is working…? (continuo), How long will…? (futuro), Why did…? (pasado con did), Who called? (sujeto, sin llave), How many ideas do we have? (presente). Mismo orden, distinta llave.

ejercicios.texto: Camila's cousin Juliana went on a first date on Saturday, and on Sunday Camila wanted to know everything. «Where did you go?» «To a small Italian restaurant in Usaquén.» «Who paid?» «We split the bill.» «What does he do?» «He's an architect. He designs houses in Chía.» «How old is he?» «Thirty-four.» «What did you talk about?» «Travel, mostly. He has been to twelve countries.» «How long did you stay?» «Almost three hours.» «And how was it?» Juliana smiled. «Really nice. He's funny and he asks a lot of questions.» «What kind of questions?» «Where I grew up, why I became a nurse, what I do on weekends… Nobody had asked me so many things in years.» «So, when are you seeing him again?» «On Friday. He's cooking dinner.»

preguntas.q: What does Juliana's date do?
Why did Juliana like him?
opciones: Because he is funny and asks a lot of questions
Because he has a house in Chía

preguntas.q: When is Juliana seeing him again?
«Where I grew up, why I became a nurse»: ¿por qué no dicen «where did I grow up»?
opciones: Porque son preguntas indirectas (reportadas) y llevan orden de afirmación
Porque grew up es un phrasal verb
Porque el pasado nunca lleva did en preguntas

ejercicios.explica: Where did you go? Who paid? (sujeto) What does he do? How old is he? How long did you stay? When are you seeing him? Y las reportadas (where I grew up) sin llave: orden de afirmación.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe seis preguntas para entrevistar a un candidato para tu equipo: dónde trabajó antes, cuánto tiempo, por qué quiere el puesto, qué tipo de proyectos ha hecho, cuántas personas ha manejado y qué hará el primer mes.

requisitos.texto: Pregunta con where / why / what + do, does o did
Pregunta con how long, how many o how much
Pregunta en pasado con did
Pregunta sobre el futuro con will o are you going to

ejercicios.ejemplo: Where did you work before this? How long were you there? Why do you want to work at Brava? What kind of projects have you worked on? How many people did you manage in your last job? What will you do in your first month here? And one more: what time do you like to start your day?
ejercicios.explica: Cada pregunta sigue Wh- + llave + sujeto + verbo. La llave cambia con el tiempo: did (pasado), do (presente), have (perfecto), will (futuro).

ejercicios.consigna: Vas a tener la primera reunión con un cliente nuevo. Escribe seis preguntas para el brief: quién es el consumidor, qué tipo de campaña quiere, cuándo es el lanzamiento, cuánto es el presupuesto, en qué ciudades y una pregunta indirecta de cortesía (Could you tell me…?).

requisitos.texto: Pregunta con who + is / are
Pregunta con what kind of
Pregunta con how much o how many
Pregunta indirecta: Could you tell me + wh- (sin do/does)

ejercicios.ejemplo: Who is your target consumer? What kind of campaign do you have in mind, digital or TV? When is the launch? How much is the budget for this year? Which cities will the campaign run in? And finally, could you tell me who our main contact will be on your side? Thank you for your time.
ejercicios.explica: En el brief, who is / when is con be adelantado; what kind of … do you…? con do; y la indirecta con orden de afirmación: could you tell me who our contact will be.

ejercicios.consigna: Un amigo volvió de un viaje. Escríbele un mensaje con al menos cinco preguntas en pasado: adónde fue, con quién, cuánto tiempo se quedó, qué fue lo mejor, por qué eligió ese lugar y cuánto gastó.

requisitos.texto: Pregunta con where + did
Pregunta con how long, how much o how many
Pregunta con preposición al final (who … with?)
Pregunta con why + did o what was

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hey Andrés! Welcome back! Where did you go in the end? Who did you travel with? How long did you stay there? What was the best part of the trip? Why did you choose that place? And how much did you spend? Tell me everything on Friday. I want to see the photos too!
ejercicios.explica: Pasado: Wh- + did + you + verbo base (did you go, did you stay, did you spend). Con be, was se adelanta: what was the best part?

ejercicios.consigna: Llegas a un hotel en otra ciudad para un congreso. Escribe lo que le preguntas a la recepcionista con preguntas indirectas (Could you tell me…? Do you know…?): a qué hora es el desayuno, dónde está el gimnasio, qué tan lejos queda el centro de convenciones, cuánto cuesta un taxi y si el wifi es gratis.

requisitos.texto: Usa Could you tell me / Do you know + wh- al menos dos veces
Pregunta indirecta con what time + sujeto + verbo (sin do/does)
Pregunta indirecta con how far o how much
Pregunta indirecta de sí/no con if

ejercicios.ejemplo: Good afternoon. I have a reservation under Rodríguez. Could you tell me what time breakfast is? And do you know where the gym is? I also need to know how far the convention center is from here, and how much a taxi costs. One more thing: could you tell me if the Wi-Fi is free for guests? Thank you very much.
ejercicios.explica: En las indirectas el orden es de afirmación: what time breakfast is, where the gym is, how much a taxi costs. Sin do/does y con be en su lugar. Para sí/no, if.

temas.titulo: Preposiciones: in, on, at y compañía
temas.resumen: Decir cuándo (at 3 pm, on Monday, in October), dónde (at the office, in Bogotá, on the 5th floor), hacia dónde (to, into, from), cuánto tiempo (for, since, during, until, by) y qué preposición va pegada a cada verbo y adjetivo (depend on, good at).
temas.llave: at punto · on superficie/día · in dentro/periodo

teoria.paraQue: Para ubicar lo que dices en el tiempo y en el espacio sin calcos del español: la hora, el día, el mes, la ciudad, el piso, el destino y la fecha límite. Y para que los verbos y adjetivos lleven la preposición que el inglés exige (depend on, wait for, good at), que casi nunca es la que usarías en español.
teoria.llave: La llave es una imagen. *At* es un punto exacto: una hora (at 3 pm), un lugar puntual (at the office, at home). *On* es una superficie o una línea: un día (on Monday, on October 21st), un piso (on the 5th floor), la mesa (on the table). *In* es un contenedor: un periodo largo (in October, in 2026, in the morning) o un espacio con límites (in Bogotá, in the meeting room). Si dudas, pregúntate: ¿punto, superficie o contenedor?

formulas.formula: at + hora · on + día o fecha · in + mes, año, estación, parte del día
formulas.ejemplo: The call {{is}} at 3 pm on Monday; the launch {{is}} in October.

formulas.formula: at night · at noon · at the weekend (UK) / on the weekend, on weekends (US) · sin preposición con next, last, this, every
formulas.ejemplo: I {{read}} at night and I {{rest}} on weekends. See you next Monday.

formulas.formula: at + punto (at the office, at home, at the door) · on + superficie o piso (on the 5th floor, on the wall) · in + ciudad, país, cuarto, recipiente
formulas.ejemplo: She {{works}} at Brava, on the 5th floor, in Bogotá.

formulas.formula: to + destino · into + hacia dentro · from + origen
formulas.ejemplo: I {{drove}} from Bogotá to Chía and {{walked}} into the house.

formulas.formula: for + cantidad de tiempo · since + punto de inicio · during + evento · until + fin de una duración · by + fecha límite
formulas.ejemplo: I[['ve]] {{worked}} here for six years, since 2020. I[['ll]] {{send}} it by Friday.

formulas.formula: depend on · wait for · listen to · arrive at (lugar) / in (ciudad) · talk to … about · agree with · pay for · apply for · look for · ask for
formulas.ejemplo: It {{depends}} on the client. I[['m]] {{wait((ing))}} for the brief.

formulas.formula: good at · bad at · interested in · responsible for · married to · afraid of
formulas.ejemplo: Laura {{is}} good at presentations and responsible for two clients.

reglas: Tiempo: *at* para horas exactas (at 9, at noon, at midnight, at night), *on* para días y fechas completas (on Monday, on October 21st, on my birthday), *in* para periodos largos (in October, in 2026, in the summer, in the morning).
*In the morning / afternoon / evening*, pero *at night*. Es la excepción que más se oye.
Fin de semana: en inglés estadounidense *on the weekend* y *on weekends*; *at the weekend* es británico. Las dos son correctas, pero no las mezcles con *in*.
Con *next, last, this, every, tomorrow, yesterday* no va preposición: *next Monday*, *last week*, *every day* (nunca *on next Monday*).

Lugar: *at* es el punto donde estás o te encuentras con alguien (at the office, at home, at work, at the airport, at the door); *in* es el espacio que te contiene (in Bogotá, in Colombia, in the kitchen, in the car); *on* es una superficie o un piso (on the table, on the wall, on the 5th floor, on the bus).
Internet y pantallas van con *on*: *on Instagram, on the internet, on TV, on the phone, on the screen*.

Movimiento: *to* es el destino (go to the office), *into* es entrar (walk into the room), *from* es el origen (fly from Bogotá). *Arrive* no lleva *to*: *arrive at the office* (lugar) y *arrive in Bogotá* (ciudad o país).

*For* + cantidad (for two hours, for six years); *since* + punto de inicio (since 2020, since Monday); *during* + evento o periodo (during the meeting); *until* = hasta que termina algo (until 6 pm); *by* = a más tardar (by Friday).
Algunos verbos no llevan preposición aunque en español sí: *discuss the budget* (no *discuss about*), *call me* (no *call to me*), *enter the room* (no *enter to*).
La preposición de un verbo o adjetivo se aprende con la palabra, como si fuera una sola: *depend ON, wait FOR, listen TO, agree WITH, good AT, interested IN, responsible FOR, married TO*.

usos.ejemplo: Let's {{meet}} at the gym at 6 on Saturday.
I {{run}} in the morning and I {{read}} at night.
We {{flew}} from Bogotá to Cartagena and {{stayed}} there for four days.

usos.uso: Decir dónde vives y desde cuándo
usos.ejemplo: I[['ve]] {{lived}} in Chapinero since 2018.
The meeting {{is}} on Thursday at 10 at our office.
We {{need}} the final files by Friday.
I[['m]] responsible for three accounts and I {{report}} to the CEO.
The price {{depends}} on the number of pages.

errores.mal: It depends of the budget.
errores.porque: Depend va siempre con on. «Depender de» es la trampa.

errores.mal: We arrived to the office at 9.
errores.bien: We arrived at the office at 9.
errores.porque: Arrive no lleva to: at para lugares y in para ciudades.

errores.mal: I have a meeting in Monday.
errores.bien: I have a meeting on Monday.
errores.porque: Los días van con on. In es para meses y años.

errores.mal: She is married with an architect.
errores.bien: She is married to an architect.
errores.porque: Married to, aunque en español digamos «casada con».

errores.mal: Let's discuss about the budget.
errores.porque: Discuss ya incluye «sobre»: no lleva about. Si quieres about, usa talk about.

errores.mal: I work out in the night.
errores.porque: Night es la excepción: at night (pero in the morning).

errores.mal: I've lived here since five years.
errores.bien: I've lived here for five years.
errores.porque: Since marca el inicio (since 2021); for marca la cantidad (for five years).

errores.mal: I'm waiting the client.
errores.porque: Wait necesita for antes de la persona o la cosa.

contraste.b: I[['ll]] {{be}} in the office until Friday.
contraste.nota: By = a más tardar ese día (fecha límite). Until = hasta ese día, todo el tiempo (duración).
For + cuánto tiempo. Since + desde cuándo. Las dos responden a How long.

contraste.a: We {{arrived}} at the hotel at noon.
contraste.nota: Arrive at + edificio o punto; arrive in + ciudad o país. Nunca arrive to.

contraste.a: I {{go}} to the gym in the morning.
contraste.nota: Las partes del día llevan in the…, salvo night, que lleva at.

frases.es: Nos vemos el lunes a las 9.

frases.en: I'll be at the office until 6.
frases.es: Estaré en la oficina hasta las 6.

frases.en: I need it by Friday, please.
frases.es: Lo necesito para el viernes, por favor.

frases.en: I'm responsible for the media plan.
frases.es: Yo estoy a cargo del plan de medios.

frases.en: Can I talk to you about the budget?
We're waiting for the client's feedback.
frases.es: Estamos esperando la retroalimentación del cliente.

frases.en: I'm good at presentations, but bad at spreadsheets.
frases.es: Soy bueno para las presentaciones, pero malo para las hojas de cálculo.

frases.en: I live in Bogotá, on the 5th floor.
frases.es: Vivo en Bogotá, en el piso 5.

frases.en: I go to the gym in the morning.
frases.es: Voy al gimnasio en la mañana.

frases.en: We stayed at the beach for four days.
frases.es: Nos quedamos en la playa cuatro días.

teoria.tip: Piensa en una pirámide: in arriba (lo grande: años, meses, ciudades), on en el medio (días, fechas, pisos, superficies), at abajo (lo exacto: horas y puntos). Cuanto más pequeño y preciso, más cerca de at.

palabras.ejemplo: The status meeting starts at 9 am.

hueco.frase: The status meeting starts ___ 9 am. (a las)

palabras.nota: at 3 pm, at noon, at midnight, at lunchtime

palabras.ejemplo: We have our status call on Monday.

hueco.frase: We have our status call ___ Monday. (el)

palabras.nota: on Monday, on Fridays, on my birthday, on Christmas Day

palabras.ejemplo: The campaign launches on October 21st.

hueco.frase: The campaign launches ___ October 21st. (el)

palabras.nota: on October 21st, on the 5th of May, on January 1st

palabras.ejemplo: The client wants the first draft in October.

hueco.frase: The client wants the first draft ___ October. (en)

palabras.nota: in October, in December, in the first week of May

palabras.ejemplo: I started at Brava in 2019.

hueco.frase: I started at Brava ___ 2019. (en)

palabras.nota: in 2019, in the 90s, in the 21st century

palabras.es: en la mañana / tarde / noche temprana
palabras.ejemplo: I go to the gym in the morning.

hueco.frase: I go to the gym ___ the morning. (en)

palabras.nota: Pero at night. Y con días: on Monday morning (sin in).

palabras.ejemplo: I usually answer emails at night.

hueco.frase: I usually answer emails ___ night. (de)

palabras.nota: La excepción: in the evening pero at night. También at midnight.

palabras.es: el fin de semana / los fines de semana
palabras.ejemplo: We visit my parents on weekends.

hueco.frase: We visit my parents ___ weekends. (los)

palabras.nota: Estadounidense: on the weekend. Británico: at the weekend. Nunca in the weekend.

palabras.ejemplo: Our clients spend more in the summer.

hueco.frase: Our clients spend more ___ the summer. (en)

palabras.nota: in the summer, in winter, in the rainy season

palabras.en: next / last / this / every + tiempo (sin preposición)
palabras.es: el próximo / el pasado / este / cada (sin «el»)
palabras.ejemplo: See you next Monday.

hueco.frase: See you ___ Monday. (el próximo)

palabras.nota: next week, last month, this Friday, every day: cero preposición.

palabras.es: en (un punto: la oficina, la puerta, el aeropuerto)
palabras.ejemplo: I'll wait for you at the office.

hueco.frase: I'll wait for you ___ the office. (en)

palabras.nota: at the office, at the airport, at the door, at the bus stop, at Brava

palabras.ejemplo: Laura lives in Bogotá, but her family is in Cali.

hueco.frase: Laura lives ___ Bogotá. (en)

palabras.nota: in Bogotá, in Colombia, in Chapinero, in the north of the city

palabras.es: en, dentro de (un cuarto, un carro, una caja)
palabras.ejemplo: The team is in the meeting room.

hueco.frase: The team is ___ the meeting room. (en)

palabras.nota: in the kitchen, in the car, in my bag, in the box

palabras.ejemplo: Our office is on the 5th floor.

hueco.frase: Our office is ___ the 5th floor. (en)

palabras.nota: on the 5th floor, on the ground floor, on the top floor

palabras.ejemplo: The brief is on your desk.

hueco.frase: The brief is ___ your desk. (sobre)

palabras.nota: on the table, on the wall, on the screen, on the first page

palabras.ejemplo: I'm working at home today.

hueco.frase: I'm working ___ home today. (en)

palabras.nota: Sin the: at home, at work, at school. Y también: I work from home.

palabras.ejemplo: I read the brief on the plane.

hueco.frase: I read the brief ___ the plane. (en)

palabras.nota: Transporte grande: on the bus, on the plane. Pequeño: in a taxi, in the car.

palabras.es: en (Instagram, la web, la tele, el teléfono)
palabras.ejemplo: The campaign is on Instagram and on TV.

hueco.frase: The campaign is ___ Instagram and on TV. (en)

palabras.nota: on Instagram, on the internet, on TV, on the phone, on the website

palabras.ejemplo: I go to the office by bus.

hueco.frase: I go ___ the office by bus. (a)

palabras.nota: go to work, fly to Medellín, send it to the client. Excepción: go home (sin to).

palabras.ejemplo: She walked into the room and smiled.

hueco.frase: She walked ___ the room and smiled. (hacia dentro de)

palabras.nota: walk into the room, get into the car, put it into the box. Lo contrario: out of.

palabras.ejemplo: We flew from Bogotá to Cartagena.

hueco.frase: We flew ___ Bogotá to Cartagena. (desde)

palabras.nota: from Bogotá, from 9 to 5, an email from the client, I'm from Colombia

palabras.ejemplo: I usually go to work by bus.

hueco.frase: I usually go to work ___ bus. (en)

palabras.nota: by bus, by car, by plane, by bike, pero on foot.

palabras.ejemplo: I've worked at Brava for six years.

hueco.frase: I've worked at Brava ___ six years. (durante, cantidad)

palabras.nota: for two hours, for six years, for a long time. Cantidad, no punto de inicio.

palabras.ejemplo: I've lived in Chapinero since 2018.

hueco.frase: I've lived in Chapinero ___ 2018. (desde)

palabras.nota: since 2018, since Monday, since I was a kid. Va con presente perfecto.

palabras.ejemplo: My phone rang during the presentation.

hueco.frase: My phone rang ___ the presentation. (durante)

palabras.nota: during the meeting, during the summer, during the week. Nunca con cantidades: for two hours.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll be in the office until 6 pm.

hueco.frase: I'll be in the office ___ 6 pm. (hasta)

palabras.nota: Duración que termina: until Friday, until midnight. No es fecha límite (eso es by).

palabras.ejemplo: I need the final files by Friday.

hueco.frase: I need the final files ___ Friday. (a más tardar)

palabras.nota: by Friday, by noon, by the end of the month. «Para el viernes» es by, no for ni until.

palabras.ejemplo: The price depends on the number of pages.

hueco.frase: The price depends ___ the number of pages. (de)

palabras.nota: Nunca depend of. It depends on you / on the client / on the budget.

palabras.ejemplo: We're waiting for the client's feedback.

hueco.frase: We're waiting ___ the client's feedback. (esperar algo)

palabras.nota: wait for the bus, wait for me. Sin for solo cuando no dices qué esperas: Wait!

palabras.ejemplo: I listen to podcasts on the bus.

hueco.frase: I listen ___ podcasts on the bus. (escuchar algo)

palabras.nota: listen to music, listen to the client. Hear no lleva to: I heard a noise.

palabras.ejemplo: We arrived at the hotel at noon.

hueco.frase: We arrived ___ the hotel at noon. (llegar a un lugar puntual)

palabras.nota: arrive at the office / the airport; arrive in Bogotá / Colombia. Nunca arrive to. Y arrive home sin preposición.

palabras.ejemplo: I talked to the client about the deadline.

hueco.frase: I talked to the client ___ the deadline. (sobre)

palabras.nota: talk to someone (también talk with en EE. UU.). Pero discuss something, sin about.

palabras.ejemplo: I agree with Laura: the video is too long.

hueco.frase: I agree ___ Laura: the video is too long. (con)

palabras.nota: agree with a person. Con una idea: agree on the plan / agree to the proposal.

palabras.ejemplo: The client pays for the media, we pay for the production.

hueco.frase: The client pays ___ the media. (pagar algo)

palabras.nota: pay for the tickets, pay for lunch. Pero pay the bill, pay 50 dollars (sin for).

palabras.ejemplo: Mike applied for a job at a digital agency.

hueco.frase: Mike applied ___ a job at a digital agency. (postularse a)

palabras.nota: apply for a job / a visa / a loan. Y apply to a company / a university.

palabras.ejemplo: We're looking for a new account manager.

hueco.frase: We're looking ___ a new account manager. (buscar)

palabras.nota: look for = buscar; look at = mirar; look after = cuidar.

palabras.ejemplo: Can you ask the client for the final logo?

hueco.frase: Can you ask the client ___ the final logo? (pedir algo)

palabras.nota: ask for help, ask for the bill. Pero ask a question y ask someone (sin for).

palabras.ejemplo: Laura is really good at presentations.

hueco.frase: Laura is really good ___ presentations. (bueno para)

palabras.nota: good at numbers, bad at names, good at + -ing: good at negotiating.

hueco.frase: The client is interested ___ a TikTok campaign. (interesado en)

palabras.nota: interested in + sustantivo o -ing: interested in working with us.

palabras.ejemplo: Camila is responsible for the media plan.

ejercicios.q: We have the status call ___ Monday.
ejercicios.explica: Los días van con on. In es para meses y años.

ejercicios.q: The campaign launches ___ October.
ejercicios.explica: Los meses son periodos largos: in October.

ejercicios.q: I go to the gym ___ the morning.
ejercicios.explica: Las partes del día van con in the: in the morning, in the afternoon.

ejercicios.q: I usually read ___ night.
ejercicios.explica: Night es la excepción: at night, sin the.

ejercicios.q: Laura lives ___ Bogotá.
ejercicios.explica: Ciudades y países son contenedores: in Bogotá, in Colombia.

ejercicios.q: Our office is ___ the 5th floor.
ejercicios.explica: Los pisos son superficies: on the 5th floor.

ejercicios.q: I'm ___ home today, working on a proposal.
ejercicios.explica: At home, at work: punto donde estás, sin the.

ejercicios.q: Mike was born ___ 1990.
ejercicios.explica: Los años van con in: in 1990, in 2026.

ejercicios.q: See you ___ Friday!
ejercicios.explica: Días de la semana con on: on Friday.

ejercicios.q: Andrés is waiting ___ the client at the door.
ejercicios.explica: Wait necesita for antes de la persona: wait for the client.

ejercicios.q: It depends ___ the budget.
ejercicios.explica: Depend on, siempre. «Depender de» es la trampa.

ejercicios.q: I'm not very good ___ math.
ejercicios.explica: Good at / bad at + habilidad.

ejercicios.q: I go ___ the office by bus.
ejercicios.explica: El destino del movimiento va con to: go to the office.

ejercicios.es: La reunión es el lunes a las 10.
ejercicios.en: The meeting is on Monday at 10.
ejercicios.explica: On + día, at + hora. In es la trampa del español «en lunes».

ejercicios.es: Vivo en Bogotá con mi familia.
ejercicios.en: I live in Bogotá with my family.
ejercicios.explica: Las ciudades van con in.

ejercicios.frase: I have a meeting in Monday.
correccion: I have a meeting on Monday.
ejercicios.explica: Los días van con on, no con in.

ejercicios.frase: She arrived to the office at 9.
correccion: She arrived at the office at 9.
ejercicios.explica: Arrive no lleva to: arrive at + lugar puntual.
At para horas y night, on para días, in para meses y partes del día.

ejercicios.texto: I'll see you at the office on Monday.
respuestas: I'll see you at the office on Monday.
I will see you at the office on Monday.
ejercicios.explica: At the office (punto) y on Monday (día). Las preposiciones suenan cortas y débiles: afina el oído.

ejercicios.q: I've worked at Brava ___ 2021.
ejercicios.explica: 2021 es un punto de inicio: since 2021. For sería para una cantidad (for five years).

ejercicios.q: We've been in this meeting ___ two hours.

ejercicios.q: I need the report ___ Friday, please. (a más tardar)

ejercicios.q: Camila is responsible ___ the media plan.
ejercicios.explica: Responsible for. «Responsable de» tienta a decir of, pero no existe.

ejercicios.q: Sarah is married ___ a graphic designer.
ejercicios.explica: Married to, aunque en español digamos «casada con».

ejercicios.q: The phone rang ___ the presentation. (durante)
ejercicios.explica: During + evento: during the presentation. For sería para una cantidad de tiempo.

ejercicios.q: We'll stay at the beach ___ Sunday. (hasta)
ejercicios.explica: Until marca el final de una duración: hasta el domingo.

ejercicios.q: Are you interested ___ the new project?
ejercicios.explica: Interested in + sustantivo o -ing.

ejercicios.q: I applied ___ a job at a digital agency last year.
ejercicios.explica: Apply for a job / a visa. Apply to va con la empresa o la universidad.

ejercicios.q: Don't forget to pay ___ the tickets tonight.

ejercicios.es: Hablé con el cliente sobre la fecha de entrega.

ejercicios.explica: Arrive in + ciudad (at sería para un edificio). On Friday night, sin at ni in.

ejercicios.en: I have worked here since 2020.
ejercicios.explica: Since + punto de inicio (2020). For iría con una cantidad.
