Imperativo negativo: Don't be + adjetivo. 'Tan' = so.

ejercicios.frase: My new colleague is very sympathetic; everybody likes her.
correccion: My new colleague is very friendly; everybody likes her.
My new colleague is very nice; everybody likes her.
My new colleague is very kind; everybody likes her.
ejercicios.explica: Falso amigo: sympathetic = compasivo, que entiende tu dolor. 'Simpático' es friendly o nice.

ejercicios.frase: Laura is a very sensible person; she cries with every movie.
correccion: Laura is a very sensitive person; she cries with every movie.
ejercicios.explica: Falso amigo: sensible = sensato, razonable. 'Sensible' (que se afecta fácil) es sensitive.

ejercicios.frase: I'm boring in this meeting.
correccion: I'm bored in this meeting.
ejercicios.explica: Boring es lo que aburre; bored es cómo te sientes. 'I'm boring' significa que tú aburres a los demás.

ejercicios.frase: The client is very educated: he always says please and thank you.
correccion: The client is very polite: he always says please and thank you.
ejercicios.explica: Falso amigo: educated = con estudios, culto. 'Educado' (buenos modales) es polite.

ejercicios.frase: My boss is very strict about deadlines.
ejercicios.explica: Correcta. Strict about + sustantivo (strict about deadlines, strict about budgets).

ejercicios.frase: Mike is a very quite person; he almost never talks.
correccion: Mike is a very quiet person; he almost never talks.
ejercicios.explica: Quiet (callado) y quite (bastante) se confunden por la ortografía. Aquí describe a la persona: quiet.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe a un colega de tu equipo con tres adjetivos de personalidad y da un ejemplo concreto de cada uno.
ejercicios.objetivo: He's / She's very + adjetivo. He / She always… (ejemplo)
ejercicios.ejemplo: My colleague Laura is very organized: her files always have a name and a date. She's also talkative; she talks to everyone in the office. And she's a bit bossy, but she's reliable, so we love her.
ejercicios.explica: Describir a alguien = adjetivo + ejemplo concreto. Usa very / a bit para graduar y but para unir una virtud con un defecto.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe a tu cliente más difícil: cómo es (dos o tres adjetivos) y por qué dices eso.
ejercicios.objetivo: Our client is + adjetivo + because… / He's a bit + adjetivo negativo
ejercicios.ejemplo: Our most difficult client is very demanding because he wants three versions of everything. He's also impatient: he calls every day. But he's honest, and he pays on time.
ejercicios.explica: Adjetivo + because + razón. Los adjetivos para clientes difíciles: demanding, impatient, bossy, stubborn, moody; suavízalos con a bit.

ejercicios.consigna: Estás en una entrevista de trabajo. Descríbete con tres cualidades y un defecto, y usa al menos un antónimo ('I'm not…').
ejercicios.objetivo: I'm + adjetivo / I'm not very + adjetivo / Sometimes I'm a bit + adjetivo
ejercicios.ejemplo: I'm hard-working, creative and reliable: when I say Friday, it's Friday. I'm not very patient, so sometimes I'm a bit impatient with slow processes, but I'm working on it.
ejercicios.explica: En una entrevista: tres adjetivos positivos con un ejemplo y un defecto presentado con su antónimo (I'm not very patient) o suavizado (a bit impatient).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el adjetivo de carácter que corresponde a la pista.
ejercicios.texto: I lead a team of six people at Brava, and they are all different. Camila is the most {1} (trabajadora) person I know: she arrives early and never misses a deadline. Andrés is really {2} (gracioso); he makes everyone laugh, even on Monday mornings. Sarah is {3} (callada) in meetings, but her ideas are great. Daniel is {4} (confiable): if he says Friday, it's Friday. Laura is very {5} (organizada); every file has a name and a date. And me? I think I'm {6} (paciente) with the team, but a bit {7} (impaciente) with deadlines.
ejercicios.explica: Los adjetivos no cambian de género ni de número: Camila is hard-working, Daniel is reliable. Patient ↔ impatient se forma con el prefijo im-.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige el adjetivo que encaja con la explicación de cada frase.
ejercicios.texto: Our new client is not easy. He is very {1}: he wants three options by tomorrow and he never says thank you. He is also {2}; he calls five times a day and can't wait for an answer. In meetings he is a bit {3}: he tells everyone what to do, even our creative director. Yesterday he was {4} to the designer: he said her work was 'stupid'. Still, he is {5} about money: he always pays on time. And he is not {6}; when he likes an idea, he says it clearly.
ejercicios.explica: Cada adjetivo se confirma con la explicación que sigue a los dos puntos: demanding (quiere todo ya), impatient (no espera), bossy (manda), rude (grosero), honest (paga a tiempo), not negative (dice lo que le gusta).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el adjetivo en inglés. Ojo con -ing (la cosa) y -ed (cómo te sientes).
ejercicios.texto: Last week I had a very {1} (aburrida) meeting with the finance team: three hours of numbers. I was {2} (aburrido) after twenty minutes. Then the client called with an {3} (interesante) idea for the campaign, and suddenly everyone was {4} (interesado). On Friday, after a long week, I felt {5} (relajado) at the gym. My wife says I'm {6} (de humor cambiante) on Mondays, but {7} (alegre) on Fridays. She's right.
ejercicios.explica: -ing describe la cosa que produce el efecto (a boring meeting); -ed describe cómo se siente la persona (I was bored). Relaxed, moody y cheerful son estados de ánimo, no carácter.

ejercicios.texto: Yesterday Laura interviewed two candidates for the account manager position at Brava. The first one, Mike, was confident and talkative. He talked about his experience for twenty minutes and said he was ambitious and competitive. He also said he was 'not very patient with slow people'. The second candidate, Camila, was quiet and a bit shy at the beginning, but her answers were clear and honest. She said she was organized and reliable, and she gave an example: in her last job she never missed a deadline. She also said she was curious and liked to learn new things. Laura thinks Mike is smart, but a bit bossy. She prefers Camila because the team needs someone calm and thoughtful, not another extrovert.

preguntas.q: How was Mike in the interview?
What example did Camila give?
opciones: She never missed a deadline in her last job

preguntas.q: Why does Laura prefer Camila?
opciones: Because the team needs someone calm and thoughtful

preguntas.q: «Not very patient» es una forma suave de decir…

ejercicios.explica: Para describir carácter se juntan dos o tres adjetivos y un ejemplo (reliable: she never missed a deadline). 'Not very + adjetivo' suaviza el antónimo: not very patient = impatient.

ejercicios.texto: My family is small but very different. My dad is quiet and serious; he reads the newspaper every morning and never jokes. But he is also generous: he always pays for lunch when we go out. My mom is the opposite: she is cheerful and really talkative. She knows everybody in the neighborhood. My brother Andrés is funny and easy-going, but a bit lazy; on Sundays he stays in bed until noon. My sister Camila is the most hard-working person in the family. She is ambitious: she wants to be a director before she is 30. And my grandmother is the kindest person I know. She is patient with everyone, even with my brother. I think I'm a mix: serious at work, like my dad, and talkative with friends, like my mom.

preguntas.q: What is the father like?
Who wants to be a director before 30?
Why does the writer say the grandmother is patient?
opciones: Because she is patient even with the lazy brother
Because she stays in bed until noon

preguntas.q: ¿Por qué el texto dice «the kindest» y no «the most kind»?
opciones: Kind tiene una sílaba: el superlativo es kind + -est

ejercicios.explica: Adjetivos cortos → -er / -est (kind → the kindest); adjetivos largos → more / the most (the most hard-working). 'What is he like?' pregunta por el carácter.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe a tres personas de tu trabajo o tu familia: para cada una, da dos adjetivos de carácter y un ejemplo de lo que hace. Usa al menos un antónimo suave con 'not very…', un superlativo y un matizador (a bit, really, very).

requisitos.texto: Usa al menos tres adjetivos de carácter del tema
Usa not very + adjetivo
Usa un superlativo (the most … / the …est)
Usa a bit, really, very o quite delante de un adjetivo

ejercicios.ejemplo: My boss is organized and demanding, but she is not very patient: she wants everything today. My colleague Andrés is funny and really talkative; he makes jokes in every meeting. My wife is the most easy-going person I know. She is kind and a bit shy with new people, but she never complains about my plans.
ejercicios.explica: Tres adjetivos y un ejemplo por persona; el antónimo sale con 'not very…' y el superlativo con the most (largos) o -est (cortos).

temas.resumen: Reuniones, plazos, presupuesto, campañas y resultados: el vocabulario de tu día a día en la agencia, con los verbos que lo acompañan.

teoria.paraQue: Hablar de tu trabajo con naturalidad: qué haces en una reunión, qué le prometes a un cliente, cómo presentas un resultado y cómo pides una aprobación o un cambio de fecha.
teoria.llave: La llave es el verbo que acompaña a cada sustantivo. En español 'hacer' sirve para todo; en inglés cada cosa tiene su verbo: set up a meeting, meet a deadline, run a campaign, make a decision, take notes, attend a meeting, give feedback, approve a budget. Si aprendes el sustantivo solo, vas a decir 'make a meeting'.

formulas.formula: set up / schedule / reschedule / attend / cancel + a meeting
formulas.ejemplo: Can you set up a meeting with the client for Thursday?

formulas.formula: meet / miss + a deadline · the deadline is + día
formulas.ejemplo: We always meet our deadlines. The deadline is Friday.

formulas.formula: make a decision · take notes · write the minutes · give / get feedback
formulas.ejemplo: I took notes and sent the minutes after the meeting.

formulas.formula: run / launch / plan + a campaign · present the pitch · approve the budget
formulas.ejemplo: We're running a campaign for a new sneaker.

formulas.formula: follow up with + persona / on + tema
formulas.ejemplo: I'll follow up with the client on the budget tomorrow.

formulas.formula: What do you do? · Who do you work for? · What are you working on?
formulas.ejemplo: I'm working on a pitch for a bank.

reglas: Aprende cada sustantivo con su verbo: set up a meeting, meet a deadline, make a decision, take notes, give feedback, run a campaign. 'Make' y 'do' no sirven para todo.
Feedback es incontable: 'a lot of feedback', 'some feedback', nunca 'feedbacks' ni 'a feedback'. Igual que work, advice e information.

Falsos amigos de oficina: attend (asistir) no es assist (ayudar); meeting (reunión) no es reunion (reencuentro); commitment (compromiso) no es compromise (acuerdo a medias); currently (actualmente) no es actually (de hecho).
Agenda en inglés es el orden del día (la lista de temas); tu agenda de citas es your schedule o your calendar.
Minutes con -s es el acta de la reunión, no los minutos: 'Who's taking the minutes?'.
Muchas palabras son sustantivo y verbo a la vez: schedule / to schedule, launch / to launch, brief / to brief, pitch / to pitch, budget / to budget. Apréndelas en los dos usos.
Las siglas se leen letra por letra: KPI /keɪ piː aɪ/, CEO, ROI. En plural llevan s: KPIs.

usos.ejemplo: meeting · agenda · minutes · take notes · set up / attend / reschedule / cancel a meeting · follow up
deadline · schedule · meet / miss a deadline · deliverable · on time · reschedule
budget · quote · invoice · proposal · approve the budget · overtime
brief · pitch · campaign · launch · target audience · insight · KPI · reach · engagement · run a campaign
client · account · stakeholder · team · colleague · boss · hire
'I had three meetings today.' · 'I have a deadline tomorrow, so I can't go to the gym.' · 'My boss approved my vacation!'
'We're launching a campaign for a beer brand.' · 'We won the pitch!' · 'The client gave us great feedback.'

errores.mal: I can't assist to the meeting.
errores.porque: Assist = ayudar. Asistir a una reunión es attend (sin 'to') o go to.

errores.mal: The client gave us a lot of feedbacks.
errores.bien: The client gave us a lot of feedback.
errores.porque: Feedback es incontable: no tiene plural.

errores.mal: We have a reunion with the client at 4.
errores.bien: We have a meeting with the client at 4.
errores.porque: Reunion es un reencuentro (de excompañeros, de familia). La reunión de trabajo es meeting.

errores.mal: Let's make a meeting on Monday.
errores.bien: Let's set up a meeting on Monday. / Let's have a meeting on Monday.
errores.porque: Las reuniones se organizan (set up, schedule) o se tienen (have); no se 'hacen'.

errores.mal: We need to take a decision today.
errores.bien: We need to make a decision today.
errores.porque: En inglés estadounidense la decisión se 'hace': make a decision.

errores.mal: The agency has a strong compromise with the client.
errores.bien: The agency has a strong commitment to the client.
errores.porque: Compromise es un acuerdo donde cada parte cede algo. Compromiso (en el sentido de dedicación) es commitment.

errores.mal: Actually I'm working on a campaign for a bank.
errores.bien: Currently I'm working on a campaign for a bank. / I'm currently working on…
errores.porque: Actually significa 'de hecho, en realidad'. Actualmente es currently o right now.

errores.mal: Send me your agenda for next week so we can find a time.
errores.bien: Send me your schedule for next week so we can find a time.
errores.porque: Agenda en inglés es la lista de temas de una reunión. Tu agenda de citas es schedule o calendar.

contraste.a: I'll send the agenda before the meeting.
contraste.b: I'll send the minutes after the meeting.
contraste.nota: Agenda = antes (temas) · minutes = después (acta).
meet = cumplir · miss = incumplir.

contraste.a: The campaign had a reach of 2 million.
contraste.b: The campaign had high engagement: 50,000 comments.
contraste.nota: Reach = cuántos lo vieron · engagement = cuántos reaccionaron.

contraste.b: I assisted the client with the brief.
contraste.nota: attend = asistir a · assist = ayudar.

ejercicios.explica: Las cinco palabras de todos los días en la agencia. Campaign se pronuncia /kæmˈpeɪn/, la g es muda.
Brief, pitch, launch y schedule son sustantivos y verbos a la vez: to brief, to pitch, to launch, to schedule.
Agenda = lista de temas (antes de la reunión); minutes = acta (después). Ninguna significa 'agenda de citas' ni 'minutos'.
Vocabulario de resultados. Account en una agencia es el cliente que manejas, no una cuenta bancaria.
Verbos clave. Attend ya incluye el 'a': attend the meeting, sin 'to'.
Colocaciones verbo + sustantivo. Meet a deadline (cumplir), take notes (tomar), set up a meeting (convocar), give feedback (dar), make a decision (tomar).
Papeles y dinero. Quote es la cotización (lo que va a costar); invoice es la factura (lo que ya debes pagar).
La gente del trabajo. Colleague se pronuncia /ˈkɑːliːɡ/, con acento en la primera sílaba.
Más colocaciones. Meet the client = reunirse con el cliente; meet a deadline = cumplir un plazo. El verbo es el mismo, el sentido cambia.

ejercicios.q: We have a ___ with the client at 10 a.m. to present the campaign.

ejercicios.explica: Deadline = fecha límite. 'We can't be late' es la pista.

ejercicios.q: The client only has $20,000 for the campaign. It's a very small ___.
ejercicios.explica: Budget = presupuesto, el dinero disponible para el proyecto.

ejercicios.q: The client gave us ___ on the designs: 25 comments!
ejercicios.explica: Feedback es incontable: a lot of feedback, some feedback. Nunca lleva -s ni 'a'.

ejercicios.q: Can you ___ a meeting with the media team for Thursday?
ejercicios.explica: Set up a meeting = convocar una reunión. 'Make a meeting' es calco del español.

ejercicios.q: Sorry, I can't ___ the meeting tomorrow; I'm traveling.
ejercicios.explica: Attend the meeting = asistir a la reunión. Assist es ayudar, y 'go' necesitaría 'to'.

ejercicios.q: Laura, can you ___ during the meeting? We need a summary later.
ejercicios.explica: Take notes = tomar notas. Es una colocación fija.

ejercicios.q: The client isn't available on Monday. We have to ___ the meeting.
ejercicios.explica: Reschedule = reprogramar, cambiar la fecha. Re- + schedule.

ejercicios.q: Before the meeting, I'll send you the ___ with the three topics we need to discuss.
ejercicios.explica: Agenda = lista de temas, se manda antes. Minutes = acta, se manda después. Schedule son horarios.

ejercicios.q: The campaign had great ___: two million people saw the video.
ejercicios.explica: Reach = alcance, cuánta gente vio el contenido. Engagement sería comentarios, likes y shares.

ejercicios.q: The ___ for this campaign is women between 25 and 40 in Bogotá.
ejercicios.explica: Target audience = público objetivo, la gente a la que le hablas. El client es quien paga.

ejercicios.q: After the meeting, I'll ___ with the client by email to confirm the next steps.
ejercicios.explica: Follow up with + persona = hacer seguimiento. Sin 'up', follow es seguir a alguien.

ejercicios.q: The ___ (presupuesto) for the campaign is $50,000.
ejercicios.explica: Presupuesto = budget. Se pronuncia /ˈbʌdʒɪt/.

ejercicios.q: We have a ___ (reunión) with the client at 3 p.m.
ejercicios.explica: Reunión = meeting. Nunca reunion.

ejercicios.q: The ___ (fecha límite) is next Monday.
ejercicios.explica: Fecha límite = deadline, una sola palabra.

ejercicios.q: The client needs to ___ (aprobar) the designs before Friday.
ejercicios.explica: Aprobar = approve. Ojo: en inglés lleva doble p y termina en -ve.

ejercicios.q: I always ___ (tomo notas) in meetings so I don't forget anything.
ejercicios.explica: Tomar notas = take notes. No make ni do.

ejercicios.q: Who is going to ___ (asistir a) the kick-off meeting?
ejercicios.explica: Asistir a = attend, sin preposición. Assist es ayudar.

ejercicios.q: After the ___ (lanzamiento), we'll measure reach and engagement.
ejercicios.explica: Lanzamiento = launch. También es verbo: to launch a campaign.

ejercicios.q: Please write the ___ (acta) of the meeting and send them to everyone.
ejercicios.explica: Acta de la reunión = minutes (siempre en plural). Por eso dice 'send them'.

ejercicios.q: We need an ___ (hallazgo, insight) about the consumer to build the idea.
ejercicios.explica: Insight = hallazgo sobre el consumidor. Se pronuncia /ˈɪnsaɪt/, como in + sight.

correccion: The client gave us a lot of feedback.
ejercicios.explica: Feedback es incontable: nunca lleva -s.

ejercicios.frase: We have a reunion with the client at 4.
correccion: We have a meeting with the client at 4.
ejercicios.explica: Reunion es un reencuentro (de excompañeros, de familia). La reunión de trabajo es meeting.

ejercicios.frase: We need to meet the deadline on Friday.
ejercicios.explica: Correcta. Meet the deadline = cumplir el plazo.

ejercicios.frase: The agency has a strong compromise with the client.
correccion: The agency has a strong commitment to the client.
The agency is strongly committed to the client.
The agency is very committed to the client.
ejercicios.explica: Falso amigo: compromise es un acuerdo a medias. Compromiso (dedicación) es commitment to.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe una semana típica en la agencia: cuántas reuniones tienes, qué entregables hay esta semana y cuál es la fecha límite más cercana.
ejercicios.objetivo: I have / attend … meetings a week · the deliverables are… · the deadline is… · the client / my team
ejercicios.ejemplo: I attend about ten meetings a week. This week the deliverables are a pitch for a bank and three videos for Honda. The closest deadline is Thursday, and the client wants feedback on the designs by Friday.
ejercicios.explica: Usa attend / have … meetings, the deliverables are…, the deadline is… y feedback sin -s. Meeting, no reunion.

ejercicios.consigna: Cierra una reunión con el cliente: resume los próximos pasos (quién aprueba qué, cuál es la fecha límite y cómo vas a hacer seguimiento).
ejercicios.objetivo: next steps · you approve the budget by… · the deadline is… · I'll follow up with… · I'll send the minutes
ejercicios.ejemplo: So, next steps: you approve the budget by Wednesday, we send the first draft on Friday, and I'll follow up with you on Monday. I'll send the minutes this afternoon.
ejercicios.explica: Cerrar una reunión: next steps + approve + deadline + follow up with + send the minutes. Las colocaciones completas, no 'make the follow'.

ejercicios.consigna: Presenta al cliente los resultados de una campaña: el público objetivo, el alcance, el engagement, el KPI principal y un insight.
ejercicios.objetivo: target audience · reach of… · engagement · our main KPI is… · the insight is that…
ejercicios.ejemplo: Our target audience was young riders in Bogotá. The campaign had a reach of two million people and high engagement: 50,000 comments. Our main KPI was test rides, and we got 3,000. The insight is that young riders buy on credit, not with cash.
ejercicios.explica: Vocabulario de resultados: target audience, a reach of + número, high / low engagement, our main KPI is…, the insight is that… Reach cuenta personas; engagement cuenta reacciones.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la palabra de trabajo que corresponde a la pista.
ejercicios.texto: Monday was a long day at Brava. At 9 we had a {1} (reunión) with the client about the new {2} (campaña). There were three items on the {3} (orden del día): the {4} (presupuesto), the {5} (cronograma) and the KPIs. I took notes, and after the meeting I wrote the {6} (acta) and sent them to everyone. The client gave us a lot of {7} (retroalimentación) on the designs, so the team worked overtime. The {8} (fecha límite) for the first draft is Friday, and we never miss our deadlines.
ejercicios.explica: Agenda = orden del día, minutes = acta, schedule = cronograma, feedback es incontable (a lot of feedback). Cada sustantivo va con su verbo: take notes, write the minutes, give feedback, miss a deadline.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige el verbo que acompaña a cada sustantivo.
ejercicios.texto: Can you {1} a meeting with the media team for Thursday? We need to {2} a decision about the budget before Friday. Please {3} notes and send the minutes. Also, the client wants to {4} the campaign on March 15, so we can't {5} the deadline. I'll {6} up with the designer on the new logo, and Laura will {7} the kick-off meeting with the stakeholders.
ejercicios.explica: En inglés cada sustantivo tiene su verbo: set up a meeting, make a decision, take notes, launch a campaign, miss a deadline, follow up, attend a meeting (assist = ayudar).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa el correo con la palabra en inglés.
ejercicios.texto: Dear Mike, thanks for your email. We received the {1} (brief, encargo) on Monday and the team is working on the {2} (propuesta). Attached you'll find the {3} (cotización) for the video: the total is $12,000. Our main {4} (hallazgo) is that young riders buy on credit, so the {5} (público objetivo) is men between 18 and 25. The {6} (entregables) are three videos and ten posts. Could you {7} (aprobar) the budget by Friday? If you need to {8} (reprogramar) Thursday's call, just let me know. Best, Laura
ejercicios.explica: Vocabulario de un correo de cuenta: brief, proposal, quote (cotización), insight, target audience, deliverables, approve the budget, reschedule the call.

ejercicios.texto: Last month Brava won the pitch for a new sneaker brand. The brief arrived on a Monday: the client wanted a campaign for Gen Z with a budget of $80,000. Laura, the account manager, set up a kick-off meeting with the whole team. Twelve people attended. The planner presented the insight: young people don't buy sneakers, they buy status. The creative team worked overtime for two weeks and the deadline was tight, but they met it. On the day of the pitch, Andrés presented the idea in twenty minutes. The client gave a lot of positive feedback and approved the proposal the next day. Now the team is running the campaign: the launch is on November 10, and the main KPI is sales, not likes. Laura is already following up with the client on the next deliverables.

preguntas.q: What did the client want?
opciones: A campaign for Gen Z with a budget of $80,000
A new logo for a bank

preguntas.q: What was the insight?
opciones: Young people buy status, not sneakers

preguntas.q: What is the main KPI?
¿Por qué el texto dice «a lot of feedback» y no «many feedbacks»?
opciones: Feedback es incontable: no lleva plural

ejercicios.explica: El ciclo de una cuenta: brief → kick-off meeting → insight → meet the deadline → pitch → feedback → approve the proposal → run the campaign → launch → KPI → follow up.

ejercicios.texto: Yesterday was a bad day for Camila. She missed the deadline for the monthly report because the data team sent the numbers late. Her boss was not happy. Then the client called to reschedule the status meeting: not Tuesday, but Monday at 8 a.m. Camila had to cancel her gym class. In the afternoon she found a mistake in the invoice: the agency charged the client for ten posts, but the deliverables were twelve. She fixed it and sent a new invoice. At 6 p.m. the stakeholders asked for a new quote for the launch event. Camila worked overtime until 9. 'The good news,' she told her colleagues, 'is that we are still on schedule for the launch, and the client said our engagement numbers are the best of the year.'

preguntas.q: Why did Camila miss the deadline?
opciones: Because the data team sent the numbers late
Because she went to the gym
Because the client cancelled the meeting

preguntas.q: What was wrong with the invoice?
opciones: It charged for ten posts, but the deliverables were twelve
It was sent to the wrong client

preguntas.q: What is the good news?
opciones: They are still on schedule and engagement is the best of the year
The client approved a bigger budget
Camila doesn't have to work on Monday

preguntas.q: «Reschedule the meeting» significa…
opciones: Cambiar la fecha o la hora de la reunión

ejercicios.explica: miss a deadline, reschedule a meeting, cancel, invoice, deliverables, quote, work overtime, on schedule, engagement: el vocabulario del día a día con sus verbos.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe tu semana de trabajo en Brava: una reunión, un plazo, algo del dinero (presupuesto, cotización o factura) y qué le prometiste al cliente. Usa los verbos que acompañan a cada sustantivo.

requisitos.texto: Usa una colocación de reuniones: set up / attend / reschedule a meeting
Usa meet o miss + deadline
Nombra algo del dinero: budget, quote, invoice o proposal
Usa give / get feedback, make a decision o follow up

ejercicios.ejemplo: On Monday I set up a meeting with the client about the new campaign. We made a decision about the budget: $50,000 for three months. The client gave us a lot of feedback on the first draft, so we worked late on Tuesday and Wednesday, but we met the deadline on Friday. I also sent the quote for the video and I'll follow up with the client next week.
ejercicios.explica: Sustantivo + su verbo: set up a meeting, make a decision, give feedback, meet the deadline, send the quote, follow up with the client. 'Make a meeting' o 'take a decision' son calcos.

temas.resumen: Aeropuerto, hotel, restaurante y transporte: las palabras y las colocaciones para moverte en un viaje de trabajo o de vacaciones.

teoria.paraQue: Sobrevivir a un viaje en inglés: hacer el check-in, pedir una habitación, entender un retraso, pedir la cuenta y moverte en metro o taxi sin traducir palabra por palabra.
teoria.llave: La llave es la colocación: verbo + sustantivo que siempre van juntos. No aprendas 'room'; aprende 'book a room'. No aprendas 'tip'; aprende 'leave a tip'. Las más importantes: book a room / a flight, check in, check out, board the plane, miss the flight, pay the check, leave a tip, rent a car, go sightseeing, take the subway.

formulas.formula: I'd like + sustantivo / I'd like to + verbo
formulas.ejemplo: I'd like a double room for two nights. · I'd like to check in, please.

formulas.formula: Can / Could I have + sustantivo, please?
formulas.ejemplo: Could I have the check, please?

formulas.formula: Is + sustantivo + included?
formulas.ejemplo: Is breakfast included? · Is the tip included?

formulas.formula: What time is + check-in / check-out / boarding / the flight?
formulas.ejemplo: What time is check-out?

formulas.formula: book a room · check in at… · check out before… · have a reservation under the name…
formulas.ejemplo: I have a reservation under the name Gómez.

formulas.formula: go through security / customs · board the plane · miss / catch the flight · the flight takes off / lands
formulas.ejemplo: We boarded the plane at gate 12.

reglas: Aprende cada sustantivo con su verbo: book a room, leave a tip, miss the flight, rent a car, take the subway, go sightseeing. Así no inventas verbos (nunca 'do the check-in').
Luggage y baggage son incontables: 'my luggage is heavy', nunca 'two luggages'. Si quieres contar, usa suitcases, bags o pieces of luggage.
En Estados Unidos la cuenta del restaurante es the check; the bill se entiende y se usa para servicios (the phone bill, the hotel bill). 'The account' nunca es la cuenta del restaurante.
Check in / check out son verbos de dos palabras (I check in at 3). Con guion, check-in / check-out, son sustantivos: 'What time is check-out?'.
Falsos amigos de viaje: receipt es recibo (recipe es receta de cocina); reservate no existe (reserve o book); carpet es alfombra (folder es carpeta); exit es salida (success es éxito).
Medios de transporte con by: by bus, by plane, by subway, by car; pero on foot. Y 'take' con el medio: take a cab, take the subway.
Round trip = ida y vuelta (US). One-way = solo ida. En hotel: single room (una persona) / double room (dos).

usos.ejemplo: flight · boarding pass · gate · security · customs · delay / delayed · layover · departure · arrival · aisle seat / window seat · carry-on · take off / land · board · miss the flight
reservation · book a room · single / double room · front desk · check in / check out · key card · room service · breakfast included · voucher · available
menu · waiter · order · the check · tip · receipt · buffet · a table for two
subway · cab / taxi · bus stop · platform · fare · rent a car · take the subway · by bus
business trip · itinerary · round trip · one-way ticket · expense report · receipt · 'I'm here for a conference.'
My flight is delayed. · They lost my luggage. · The room isn't ready. · I missed my connection. · The key card doesn't work.

errores.mal: I have two luggages.
errores.bien: I have two suitcases. / I have two pieces of luggage.
errores.porque: Luggage es incontable: no tiene plural ni va con números.

errores.mal: Can you bring us the account, please?
errores.bien: Can you bring us the check, please?
errores.porque: La cuenta del restaurante es the check (US) o the bill (UK). Account es cuenta bancaria o cuenta de cliente.

errores.mal: Keep the recipe for the expense report.
errores.bien: Keep the receipt for the expense report.
errores.porque: Receipt /rɪˈsiːt/ = recibo. Recipe /ˈresəpi/ = receta de cocina.

errores.mal: I want to reservate a room.
errores.bien: I want to book a room. / I want to reserve a room.
errores.porque: 'Reservate' no existe. El verbo es book (el más natural) o reserve; el sustantivo es reservation.

errores.mal: We did the check-in at 3 p.m.
errores.porque: Check in ya es el verbo. No necesita 'do' ni 'make'.

errores.mal: I travel in bus to the office.
errores.bien: I travel by bus to the office.
errores.porque: Medios de transporte con by: by bus, by plane, by car. Solo 'on foot' es distinto.

errores.mal: Where is the exit? I need to go to the door 23.
errores.porque: La puerta de embarque es gate, no door. Y los números van sin 'the': gate 23, platform 4, room 310.

errores.mal: I want a ticket of going and coming back.
errores.bien: I want a round trip ticket.
errores.porque: Ida y vuelta = round trip (US). Solo ida = one-way.

contraste.b: What time can I check in?
contraste.nota: Con guion es sustantivo; sin guion es verbo.

contraste.a: Could I have the check, please?
contraste.b: Could I have the receipt, please?
contraste.nota: Check = lo que pagas; receipt = el papel que te dan después de pagar.

contraste.a: I have a lot of luggage.
contraste.nota: Luggage no se cuenta; suitcases sí.
Single es para la habitación (una persona); para el tiquete de solo ida, en US se dice one-way.

I booked a room near the client's office.

frases.es: asiento de pasillo · asiento de ventana
frases.ejemplo: Can I have an aisle seat, please?

teoria.tip: Antes de un viaje, repite en voz alta las cinco frases que seguro vas a decir: 'I have a reservation under…', 'Is breakfast included?', 'An aisle seat, please', 'Could I have the check?' y 'Can I have a receipt?'.

ejercicios.explica: Vocabulario básico de aeropuerto. Gate es la puerta de embarque, nunca door.
Vocabulario de hotel. La recepción es the front desk (o reception); la persona es the receptionist.
Vocabulario de restaurante. En US la cuenta es the check; the bill también se entiende.
Tipos de tiquete y momentos del vuelo. Layover es la escala entre dos vuelos.
Colocaciones verbo + sustantivo. Apréndelas juntas: book a room, pack your suitcase, miss the bus, board the plane, leave a tip.
Aisle se pronuncia /aɪl/, la s es muda. Customs (aduana) siempre lleva s; custom sin s es costumbre.
Receipt /rɪˈsiːt/: la p es muda. No confundir con recipe (receta de cocina).
Hacer turismo = go sightseeing. Viaje de trabajo = business trip (no 'work travel').
Transporte en US: subway (metro), cab (taxi). Fare es lo que pagas por el pasaje; price se usa para cosas, fare para transporte.
Verbos del vuelo. Book es reservar (un vuelo, una habitación, una mesa); 'reservate' no existe.

pares: the time you wait between two flights
the document you need to get on the plane
a ticket to go and come back
extra money you leave for the waiter
ejercicios.explica: Empareja cada palabra con su definición en inglés para fijarla sin pasar por el español.

pares: the place where you check in at a hotel
the place where you board the plane
where they check what you bring into the country
a paper or code you exchange for a service
when the flight leaves later than planned
ejercicios.explica: Definiciones en inglés. Fíjate en la diferencia: front desk es del hotel y gate del aeropuerto.

ejercicios.q: Excuse me, where is ___ 23? My flight leaves in 20 minutes.
ejercicios.explica: Gate = puerta de embarque. Platform es el andén del tren; front desk es la recepción del hotel.

ejercicios.q: I'd like to ___ a double room for two nights, please.
ejercicios.explica: Book a room = reservar una habitación. También se dice reserve a room, pero nunca 'do' o 'buy'.

ejercicios.q: Can we have ___, please? We're ready to leave the restaurant.
ejercicios.explica: La cuenta del restaurante es the check (US). The account es un calco del español; the receipt es el recibo que te dan después de pagar.

ejercicios.q: Our flight is ___ by two hours because of the rain.
ejercicios.explica: Delayed = retrasado. Si fuera cancelled no habría 'by two hours'.

ejercicios.q: I only have a ___, so I don't need to wait for my suitcase.
ejercicios.explica: Carry-on = equipaje de mano, el que llevas contigo en el avión.

ejercicios.q: We have to ___ before 12, so let's pack now.
ejercicios.explica: Check out = dejar la habitación y pagar. Check in es al llegar.

ejercicios.q: Do you want an aisle seat or a ___ seat?
ejercicios.explica: En el avión eliges aisle seat (pasillo) o window seat (ventana). Single y double son para habitaciones.

ejercicios.q: The service was great, so we left a 15% ___.
ejercicios.explica: Tip = propina, y la colocación es leave a tip.

ejercicios.q: I need a ___ ticket: Bogotá to Miami and back.
ejercicios.explica: Round trip = ida y vuelta. One-way = solo ida.

ejercicios.q: Your room isn't ready yet. You can leave your ___ at the front desk.
ejercicios.explica: Luggage es incontable: nunca lleva -s. Lo mismo pasa con baggage.

ejercicios.q: Our flight isn't direct: we have a three-hour ___ in Panama City.
ejercicios.explica: Layover = escala. Un delay es un retraso, no una parada planeada.

ejercicios.q: Good evening. I have a ___ (reserva) for tonight under the name Gómez.
ejercicios.explica: Reserva = reservation (o booking). El verbo es book o reserve.

ejercicios.q: Please show your ___ (pasabordo) and your passport.
ejercicios.explica: Boarding pass = pasabordo. Viene de board (abordar).

ejercicios.q: Is breakfast ___ (incluido) in the price?
ejercicios.explica: Included = incluido. Pregunta clave en cualquier hotel.

ejercicios.q: You can ___ (registrarse) at the hotel after 3 p.m.
ejercicios.explica: Check in = registrarse en el hotel o hacer el check-in del vuelo. Sin guion cuando es verbo.

ejercicios.q: I ordered a sandwich from ___ (servicio a la habitación) at midnight.
ejercicios.explica: Room service = servicio a la habitación. Se pide 'from room service'.

ejercicios.q: The ___ (propina) is not included in the price.
ejercicios.explica: Tip = propina. En US suele ser del 15 al 20 %.

ejercicios.q: I'd like an ___ (asiento de pasillo), please. I don't like the window.
ejercicios.explica: Aisle seat = asiento de pasillo. Aisle se pronuncia /aɪl/.

ejercicios.q: Tomorrow we're going ___ (a hacer turismo) in Cartagena.
ejercicios.explica: Hacer turismo = go sightseeing. No se dice 'do tourism'.

ejercicios.texto: boarding pass
ejercicios.explica: Boarding pass = pasabordo.

ejercicios.texto: I have a reservation.
ejercicios.explica: La frase que abre todo check-in. Reservation con -tion, no 'reserve'.

ejercicios.texto: Can I have the check, please?
respuestas: Can I have the check, please
Can I have the check please
ejercicios.explica: Pedir la cuenta en US: the check.

ejercicios.texto: The flight is delayed.
ejercicios.explica: Delayed = retrasado. Se oye en todos los aeropuertos.

ejercicios.texto: What time is check-out?
ejercicios.explica: Check-out como sustantivo (la hora de salida). Se escribe con guion o junto.

respuestas: I want to book a double room
I'd like to book a double room
I would like to book a double room
I want to reserve a double room
I'd like to reserve a double room
I would like to reserve a double room
ejercicios.explica: Reservar = book o reserve. 'I'd like to' es más cortés que 'I want to'.
Puerta de embarque = gate. Nunca door.

respuestas: Can I have the check, please
Can we have the check, please
Could I have the check, please
Could we have the check, please
Can I have the bill, please
Can we have the bill, please
Could we have the bill, please
ejercicios.explica: La cuenta = the check (US) o the bill. Nunca 'the account'.

ejercicios.es: Mi vuelo tiene un retraso de dos horas.
respuestas: My flight is delayed two hours
My flight is delayed by two hours
My flight is two hours late
My flight has a two-hour delay
My flight has a two hour delay
My flight is delayed for two hours
There is a two-hour delay on my flight
ejercicios.explica: Lo más natural: 'My flight is delayed (by) two hours'. Delay es el sustantivo; delayed el adjetivo.
Breakfast normalmente va sin artículo: Is breakfast included?

ejercicios.es: Necesito un tiquete de ida y vuelta a Medellín.
respuestas: I need a round trip ticket to Medellín
I need a round-trip ticket to Medellín
I need a round trip ticket to Medellin
I need a round-trip ticket to Medellin
I need a round trip to Medellín
I need a round trip to Medellin
ejercicios.explica: Ida y vuelta = round trip (US). El orden es round trip ticket, no 'ticket round trip'.

ejercicios.frase: I have two luggages.
correccion: I have two suitcases.
I have two bags.
I have two pieces of luggage.
ejercicios.explica: Luggage es incontable. Para contar usa suitcases, bags o pieces of luggage.

ejercicios.frase: Can you bring us the account, please?
correccion: Can you bring us the check, please?
Can you bring us the bill, please?
ejercicios.explica: Calco del español. La cuenta del restaurante es the check (US) o the bill.

ejercicios.frase: Keep the recipe; you need it for your expense report.
correccion: Keep the receipt; you need it for your expense report.
ejercicios.explica: Falso amigo: recipe es receta de cocina. El recibo es receipt /rɪˈsiːt/.

ejercicios.frase: You have to check out before noon.
ejercicios.explica: Correcta. Check out (verbo, sin guion) = dejar la habitación. Noon = las 12 del día.

ejercicios.frase: I want to reservate a table for four.
correccion: I want to reserve a table for four.
I want to book a table for four.
I'd like to reserve a table for four.
I'd like to book a table for four.
ejercicios.explica: 'Reservate' no existe. El verbo es book o reserve; reservation es el sustantivo.

ejercicios.consigna: Estás en la recepción de un hotel en Miami. Haz el check-in: di que tienes una reserva, el tipo de habitación, cuántas noches y pregunta si el desayuno está incluido.
ejercicios.objetivo: I have a reservation under the name… / a single / double room for … nights / Is breakfast included? / What time is check-out?
ejercicios.ejemplo: Good evening. I have a reservation under the name Gómez: a single room for three nights. Is breakfast included? And what time is check-out?
ejercicios.explica: El guion del check-in: I have a reservation under the name… + tipo de habitación + for … nights + Is breakfast included? Reservation, no 'reserve'.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuéntale a un colega cómo fue tu último viaje de trabajo: el vuelo (¿hubo retraso?), el hotel y si tuviste tiempo para hacer turismo.
ejercicios.objetivo: business trip · flight / delayed / layover · hotel / room service · go sightseeing
ejercicios.ejemplo: Last month I went on a business trip to Mexico City. The flight was delayed two hours, so I arrived late. The hotel was nice, and I ordered room service the first night. On Saturday I went sightseeing downtown.
ejercicios.explica: Usa las colocaciones: go on a business trip, the flight was delayed, order room service, go sightseeing. Nunca 'do tourism' ni 'make the check-in'.

ejercicios.consigna: Termina una cena de trabajo en un restaurante: pide la cuenta, pregunta si la propina está incluida y pide el recibo para tu informe de gastos.
ejercicios.objetivo: Could we have the check, please? / Is the tip included? / Could I have a receipt?
ejercicios.ejemplo: Excuse me, could we have the check, please? Is the tip included? And could I have a receipt? I need it for my expense report.
ejercicios.explica: La cuenta es the check (nunca the account), la propina es the tip y el recibo es the receipt (no recipe). Pide con Could I / we have…, please?

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la palabra de viaje que corresponde a la pista.
ejercicios.texto: My {1} (vuelo) to Miami leaves at 7 a.m., so I'm at the airport at 5. I check in online, so I only need to print my {2} (pasabordo). I have a {3} (equipaje de mano) and one big suitcase. The line at {4} (control de seguridad) is very long, but I have time. Then I see the screen: the flight is {5} (retrasado) two hours. I go to {6} (puerta de embarque) 23, buy a coffee and wait. Finally we {7} (abordar) the plane at 9:30 and the plane {8} (despega) at 10.
ejercicios.explica: Vocabulario de aeropuerto en orden real: flight, boarding pass, carry-on, security, delayed, gate, board the plane, take off. 'Delayed' es adjetivo: the flight is delayed.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la palabra que encaja en cada hueco.
ejercicios.texto: Good evening. I have a {1} under the name Rodríguez: a {2} for three nights. Is breakfast {3}? Great, and what time does the buffet open? 6:30, perfect. And what time is {4}? Noon, that's fine. One more thing: my {5} doesn't work; can you fix it, please? Also, tomorrow after I check out I'd like to leave my {6} at the {7} for a few hours, because my flight is at night.
ejercicios.explica: Colocaciones de hotel: a reservation under the name…, a single room for three nights, Is breakfast included?, What time is check-out?, leave my luggage at the front desk.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la palabra en inglés. Los verbos van en pasado.
ejercicios.texto: After the conference, Mike and I took the {1} (metro) to the old city. We went {2} (hacer turismo) for two hours and then found a small restaurant. The {3} (mesero) brought the {4} (carta) and we {5} (pedimos) fish and two beers. When we finished, I asked for the {6} (cuenta) and left a 20% {7} (propina). I also asked for a {8} (recibo) for my expense report. We took a cab back to the hotel because it was late.
ejercicios.explica: take the subway · go sightseeing · the waiter brings the menu · order (pedir) · ask for the check · leave a tip · a receipt (recibo, no 'recipe').

ejercicios.texto: Last month Laura went to São Paulo on a business trip. The agency sent her the itinerary two days before: a round trip ticket, a single room for three nights and a meeting with the client on Tuesday at 9. The problems started at the airport. Her flight was delayed three hours, so she missed her connection in Panama City. The airline gave her a meal voucher and a seat on the next flight, but she arrived in São Paulo at midnight. At the hotel, the front desk had no reservation under her name! Finally they found a double room available, with breakfast included. The next morning she took a cab to the client's office and arrived on time. 'The trip was terrible, but the meeting was great,' she said.

preguntas.q: What did the itinerary include?
opciones: A round trip ticket, a single room and a meeting on Tuesday
A one-way ticket and a rental car
Two nights in a double room

preguntas.q: Why did Laura miss her connection?
opciones: Because her first flight was delayed three hours
Because she lost her boarding pass
Because the line at security was long

preguntas.q: What happened at the hotel?
opciones: They had no reservation under her name

preguntas.q: «A meal voucher» es…

ejercicios.explica: Secuencia de un viaje de trabajo: itinerary, round trip, delayed, miss the connection, voucher, reservation under the name, room available, breakfast included, take a cab.

ejercicios.texto: Andrés and Camila went to Cartagena for the weekend. They bought one-way tickets because they wanted to come back by bus. They only had carry-ons, so they didn't wait for luggage at arrivals. They booked a double room in the old city, and when they checked in, the woman at the front desk gave them two key cards and a map. On Saturday they went sightseeing all morning and had lunch at a small restaurant near the wall. The waiter was friendly, so they left a good tip. On Sunday they rented bikes and rode along the beach. The bus back to Bogotá left at 8 p.m. from platform 6. It was a long trip, but the fare was cheap and they slept most of the way.

preguntas.q: Why did they buy one-way tickets?
opciones: Because they wanted to come back by bus
Because round trips were more expensive

preguntas.q: Why didn't they wait at arrivals?
What did they do on Sunday?
opciones: They rented bikes and rode along the beach
They went sightseeing in the old city
They took a cab to the airport

preguntas.q: ¿Por qué el texto dice «luggage» y no «luggages»?
opciones: Luggage es incontable; para contar se dice suitcases o bags

ejercicios.explica: one-way vs. round trip; carry-on (contable) vs. luggage (incontable); book a room, check in, key card, go sightseeing, leave a tip, rent bikes, platform, fare.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta tu último viaje (o uno imaginario): cómo llegaste, dónde te quedaste, qué pasó en el hotel y en un restaurante, y cómo te moviste por la ciudad. Usa las colocaciones del tema.

requisitos.texto: Usa una colocación de hotel: book a room, check in, check out o front desk
Nombra algo del aeropuerto o del vuelo: flight, gate, boarding pass, delayed, luggage, carry-on
Usa vocabulario de restaurante: the check, a tip, the waiter, the menu, order
Usa un medio de transporte: take a cab / the subway, rent a car, by bus

ejercicios.ejemplo: Last month I went to Miami on a business trip. My flight was delayed two hours, so I arrived at the hotel at midnight. I checked in, left my luggage in the room and went to sleep. The next day I had lunch near the office; the waiter was friendly and I left a 20% tip. I took the subway to the client's office because a cab was too expensive. On Friday I checked out at noon and went to the airport by bus.
ejercicios.explica: Cada sustantivo con su verbo: book a room, check in / out, leave a tip, take the subway / a cab, rent a car. Luggage es incontable y los medios de transporte van con by.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Cada hueco esconde un calco típico del español: agree, explain to, attend, discuss, depend on, realize, tell, ask.
ejercicios.texto: Hi Sarah, I {1} with your comments on the deck. I didn't understand slide 6, though. Could you explain it {2}? Yesterday I {3} the meeting with the media team, and we {4} the budget for an hour. The final number {5} the results of the test. Also, I {6} that slide 9 has the wrong date; I'll fix it today. Laura {7} me that you prefer the second route. One more thing: can I {8} a question about the logo? Best, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: I agree (sin am). Explain it to me (la cosa y luego to + persona). Attend a meeting (assist es ayudar). Discuss sin about. Depend on. Realize = darse cuenta. Tell me / said that (nunca said me). Ask a question (no make).

ejercicios.instruccion: Escribe la forma natural en inglés de lo que dice la pista. No traduzcas palabra por palabra: piensa en la pieza fija.
ejercicios.texto: {1} (tener / 38) and I've worked in advertising for fifteen years, but I still make classic mistakes. This morning I said 'I am agree' in a meeting; the correct form is 'I {2} (estar de acuerdo)'. Then I didn't understand the brief, so I asked Mike: 'Could you explain it {3} (a mí)?' He said: 'Sure, {4} (preguntar) me anything.' At lunch I told Camila the meeting was very {5} (aburrida). Later I {6} (darse cuenta, pasado) that I wrote 'sensible' instead of 'sensitive' in an email. Luckily, people {7} (be) patient with me. {8} (en realidad), I'm improving every week.
ejercicios.explica: I'm 38 (la edad con be). I agree (verbo). Explain it to me; ask me (sin to). Boring describe la reunión; bored, cómo te sientes. Realize = darse cuenta. People es plural: people are. Actually = en realidad, no «actualmente».

ejercicios.instruccion: Escribe la forma correcta. Fíjate en las preposiciones fijas (married to, arrive in, listen to, depend on) y en los verbos que van en pareja (take a photo, make a decision).
ejercicios.texto: My brother is {1} (casado con) a woman from Cali, and last weekend we visited them. We {2} (arrive, pasado) in Cali on Friday night. On Saturday we went to a salsa bar and {3} (tomar, pasado) a lot of photos. My brother's wife likes to {4} (escuchar) old salsa music all day. On Sunday we had to {5} (tomar) a decision: stay one more day or fly back. It {6} (depend, pasado) on the price of the tickets, so I checked online. {7} (la gente) in Cali are very friendly, and the food was amazing. On Monday I was {8} (cansado), but happy.
ejercicios.explica: Married to (no with), arrive in + ciudad, listen to + cosa, depend on (no of). Take a photo pero make a decision. People es plural (people are). Tired: -ed para cómo te sientes.

ejercicios.texto: When Andrés started at Brava, he made a funny mistake. In his first meeting with a client from Texas, he said, 'Actually, I work on three accounts.' The client thought he was correcting something. Andrés wanted to say 'currently'. A week later, he asked a colleague to put the files in his 'carpet'. She looked at the floor. 'You mean your folder?' she said. His favorite one was in an email: 'The client is very sensible about prices.' He wanted to say 'sensitive'. Now Andrés keeps a list of false friends on his desk, and he checks it before important emails. 'I realized that my English was good,' he says, 'but my Spanish was in the way.'

preguntas.q: Why did the client from Texas get confused?
What does Andrés do now before important emails?
opciones: He checks his list of false friends

preguntas.q: ¿Qué significa carpet?
«The client is very sensitive about prices»: ¿qué significa sensitive?

ejercicios.explica: Falsos amigos: actually = en realidad (actualmente = currently), carpet = alfombra (carpeta = folder), sensible = sensato (sensible = sensitive), realize = darse cuenta.

ejercicios.texto: After my first month working with clients in the U.S., my boss gave me some feedback. 'Your English is clear,' she said, 'but there are five phrases you translate from Spanish.' First, I said 'I have 38 years' at a team dinner; it's 'I'm 38'. Second, I wrote 'Explain me the brief' in a message; it's 'Explain the brief to me'. Third, I said 'We need to make a question'; it's 'ask a question'. Fourth, I said 'I assisted the meeting'; it's 'I attended the meeting'. And fifth, I wrote 'We discussed about the budget', but discuss doesn't need about. She told me: 'Fix these five and you'll sound much more natural.'

preguntas.q: Who gave him feedback?
How many phrases did he translate from Spanish?
¿Qué verbo va con meeting cuando significa «asistir»?
¿Cuál es la correcta?

ejercicios.explica: Cinco calcos y su pieza fija: I'm 38 (no I have 38 years), explain it to me (no explain me), ask a question (no make), attend a meeting (no assist), discuss the budget (sin about).

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe un email corto a una clienta después de una reunión. Cuéntale qué discutieron, si estás de acuerdo con su idea, de qué depende la fecha final y pídele que te explique algo que no entendiste.

requisitos.texto: Usa agree como verbo (I agree / I don't agree)
Usa discuss sin about
Usa explain + cosa + to + persona
Usa depend on

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Sarah, thanks for the meeting today. We discussed the budget and the timeline, and I agree with your idea of a smaller first phase. The final date depends on the production company, so I'll confirm it on Friday. Could you explain the new approval process to me? I don't want to make a mistake with the legal team. Best regards, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Cuatro calcos que delatan en un email: I am agree → I agree; discuss about → discuss; explain me → explain it to me; depend of → depend on. Son piezas fijas: apréndelas enteras.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la forma correcta del adjetivo: comparativo (-er / more … than), superlativo (the -est / the most) o igualdad (as … as) cuando la pista lo pide.
ejercicios.texto: The client received two proposals for the new website: ours and one from Studio Norte. Studio Norte is {1} (cheap) than Brava, but their timeline is {2} (long): twelve weeks instead of eight. Our team is {3} (small) than theirs, but in my opinion our ideas are {4} (creative). Their case studies are {5} (impressive) of all the agencies, I have to admit. Still, our price is not {6} (as / high) theirs; it's only 5% more. Yesterday the client said our presentation was {7} (good) one of the week, and theirs was {8} (bad) than last year's.
ejercicios.explica: Adjetivo corto → -er / the -est (cheaper, longer, smaller). Largo → more / the most (more creative, the most impressive). Irregulares: good → the best, bad → worse. Para igualar: as high as, sin than.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Es una conversación del equipo para escoger dónde hacer una sesión de fotos.
ejercicios.texto: — So, Medellín or Cartagena for the shoot? — Cartagena is {1}, but it's also {2} in July: 35 degrees every day. — And Medellín is {3} for the crew; it's only a 40-minute flight. — True. Hotels in Medellín are {4} than in Cartagena, too. — But the light in Cartagena is {5} light I know for this kind of photo. — I agree, it's beautiful. Still, Medellín isn't {6} Cartagena, and the budget is {7} problem we have this year. — OK, let's go with Medellín. It's {8} than spending all the money in Cartagena.
ejercicios.explica: Largo → more beautiful. Corto con consonante-vocal-consonante → dobla: hotter, the biggest. -y → -ier: easier. Irregulares: the best, better. Nunca dos llaves (more better ✗) y as…as nunca lleva than.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con comparativo, superlativo o as … as (cuando la pista lo pide). Ojo con la ortografía: -y → -ier / -iest.
ejercicios.texto: Let me tell you about my team. Camila is {1} (organized) person in the office; she never forgets a deadline. Andrés is {2} (funny) than everyone else, and his jokes save our long meetings. Laura is not {3} (as / talkative) Andrés, but her ideas are often {4} (good) than ours. Mike, our planner in Miami, works {5} (hard) than anyone I know. This year was {6} (busy) year in the agency's history, and the team was {7} (strong) than ever. I'm not {8} (as / patient) Camila, but I'm learning.
ejercicios.explica: Organized es largo → the most organized. Funny y busy terminan en -y → funnier, the busiest. Good → better. Hard y strong son cortos → harder, stronger. Para comparar sin ganador: not as talkative as.

ejercicios.texto: Hi Jonathan, thanks for the two options. Here are my thoughts. Option A is cheaper than Option B, and it's faster: we can launch in four weeks. But Option B is more creative, and in my opinion it's the strongest idea you showed us this year. The problem is the budget. Option B is 30% more expensive, and our budget is smaller than last year's. Option A isn't as exciting as B, but it's safer. My boss thinks the safest choice is the best choice right now. Personally, I prefer B. Could we find a cheaper version of B? Maybe with fewer videos and more photos? Best, Sarah

preguntas.q: Which option is faster?
What does Sarah's boss prefer?
«Option A isn't as exciting as B»: ¿qué significa?
opciones: A es menos emocionante que B
A es igual de emocionante que B
A es más emocionante que B

preguntas.q: ¿Por qué se dice «more expensive» y no «expensiver»?
opciones: Porque expensive es largo: lleva more delante
Porque es irregular, como good → better

ejercicios.explica: Un email de cliente es casi todo comparación: cheaper / faster (cortos), more creative / more expensive (largos), the strongest / the safest / the best (superlativos) y not as exciting as para decir «menos» sin sonar negativo.

ejercicios.texto: My girlfriend got a job offer in Medellín, so we're comparing the two cities. Medellín is warmer than Bogotá, and people say it's friendlier. Rent is also cheaper: a two-bedroom apartment costs about 20% less. But for my work, Bogotá is better. Most of our clients are here, and our office is the biggest one in the country. The traffic in Bogotá is the worst part of my day; Medellín's traffic isn't as bad, but it's not perfect either. My mom lives in Bogotá, and she's the most important reason to stay. We haven't decided yet. Maybe the easiest solution is to try it for six months.

preguntas.q: Which city is cheaper?
Why is Bogotá better for his work?
opciones: Most of his clients are there

preguntas.q: «Medellín's traffic isn't as bad»: ¿qué significa?
opciones: El tráfico de Medellín es menos malo
El tráfico de Medellín es peor
Los dos son igual de malos

preguntas.q: «the worst part of my day»: ¿de qué adjetivo viene worst?
opciones: De worse, que es un adjetivo normal

ejercicios.explica: Warmer, cheaper, the biggest, the easiest: adjetivos cortos o en -y. The most important: largo. Better / the worst: irregulares. Isn't as bad as: comparación de igualdad en negativa.

ejercicios.consigna: Tu jefa te pide comparar dos productoras para un video (inventa los nombres y los datos). Escríbele un mensaje corto con la comparación y tu recomendación.

requisitos.texto: Usa un comparativo corto con -er + than
Usa un comparativo largo con more + adjetivo + than
Usa un superlativo (the -est / the most / the best)
Usa as … as o not as … as

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Laura, I reviewed the two production companies for the video. Lumen is cheaper than Casa Roja, and their team is bigger. Casa Roja is more expensive than Lumen, but their reel is more creative and their director has the best portfolio I saw this year. Lumen is not as experienced as Casa Roja with food brands. My recommendation is Casa Roja: it's the safest option for a launch this important. Best, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Para comparar propuestas: corto + -er + than (cheaper than), largo con more … than (more expensive than), superlativo con the (the best, the safest) y not as … as para matizar sin atacar. Nunca more cheaper ni as … than.

ejercicios.instruccion: Escribe el conector que traduce la pista: but, although, because, so, also, too o though.
ejercicios.texto: The meeting with the client was hard, {1} (pero) it ended well. They didn't like the first idea {2} (porque) it was too serious for a young audience. {3} (aunque) I didn't agree, I listened carefully. We had a second idea, {4} (así que) Laura presented it. The client loved it, and the CEO liked it {5} (también, al final). The budget is tight, {6} (así que) we need to simplify the production. I {7} (también, antes del verbo) want to test the idea with real users. It wasn't a perfect meeting. We have a new direction, {8} (eso sí, al final).
ejercicios.explica: But y although marcan el choque (although abre la frase, nunca con but). Because da la causa; so, la consecuencia. Too va al final y also antes del verbo. Though al final significa «eso sí».

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige el conector correcto. Es un email para responder a los comentarios de un cliente sin sonar brusco.
ejercicios.texto: Hi Mike, thanks for the feedback on the storyboard. I see your point, {1} I think the ending needs to stay. {2} the video is long, the ending is the moment people remember. We tested it with ten users, {3} we have data, not only opinions. Eight people liked it {4} it was emotional. Two people didn't understand it, {5}. Laura {6} thinks we can shorten the middle part, {7} the total stays under 30 seconds. Changing the ending is possible, {8} it means a new music track. Let me know what you think. Best, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Desacuerdo suave: I see your point, but… Although abre el contraste. So = resultado (so we have data, so the total stays…), because = causa (because it was emotional). Though al final matiza; also va antes del verbo.

ejercicios.instruccion: Escribe el conector que traduce la pista. Piensa en la relación entre las dos ideas: ¿choca, explica, resulta o suma?
ejercicios.texto: I started English classes again this year {1} (porque) my job needs it. I can read emails well, {2} (pero) calls are still difficult for me. {3} (aunque) I understand most of the conversation, I get nervous when I have to speak. My boss noticed it, {4} (así que) she suggested a course. I study every morning {5} (porque) my mind is fresh before work. My girlfriend speaks English {6} (también, al final), {7} (así que) we practice at dinner on Tuesdays. It's not easy. I'm getting better, {8} (eso sí, al final).
ejercicios.explica: Because responde a «why?» (because my job needs it); so cuenta el resultado (so she suggested a course). But y although chocan dos ideas; too cierra la frase y though al final suaviza: I'm getting better, though.

ejercicios.texto: In my first year as a director, I said 'No, that's wrong' a lot. People stopped sharing ideas because they felt attacked. So I changed my style. Now, when I don't agree, I start with what is good: 'I see your point, but the budget is tight.' Although I still disagree sometimes, people listen more. Last week Andrés proposed a TikTok series for a bank. I thought it was risky because the brand is very traditional. I didn't say no, though. I said: 'It's a strong idea, and it's also risky. Let's test one video first.' We tested it, and it worked, so now the series is in the plan.

preguntas.q: Why did people stop sharing ideas?
What happened with Andrés's idea?
opciones: They tested one video and it worked

preguntas.q: «I didn't say no, though»: ¿qué significa though aquí?
opciones: «Eso sí / sin embargo», al final de la frase

preguntas.q: «…and it worked, so now the series is in the plan»: ¿qué introduce so?

ejercicios.explica: Los conectores son la herramienta para disentir sin pelear: I see your point, but… / Although I disagree… Because explica (because they felt attacked), so concluye (so now the series is in the plan), also suma.

ejercicios.texto: We planned a team picnic in Parque Simón Bolívar on Saturday, but the weather forecast said rain all day. Although some people wanted to cancel, Camila had a better idea. 'We can go bowling in Salitre,' she said, 'because it's indoors and near the park.' Everybody agreed, so we changed the plan on Friday night. The bowling place was expensive, though. We spent more than we planned because we also ordered pizza. Was it worth it? Yes. Andrés won two games, and Laura won the third one, although she says it was her first time. Next time we'll check the weather earlier.

preguntas.q: Why did they change the plan?
Why did they spend more money?
«Although some people wanted to cancel, Camila had a better idea»: ¿se puede añadir but?
opciones: No: nunca although y but en la misma frase

preguntas.q: «because it's indoors»: ¿qué introduce because?

ejercicios.explica: Although va al principio o en medio y nunca se junta con but. Because + frase completa da la causa; because of + sustantivo (because of the rain). So da el resultado y though al final añade un «eso sí».

ejercicios.consigna: Un cliente quiere cambiar el color principal de la campaña y tú no estás de acuerdo. Escríbele un mensaje con un desacuerdo suave: reconoce su punto, da tus razones y di qué pasaría si se cambia.

requisitos.texto: Muestra contraste con but
Usa although / though / even though
Da una razón con because
Di una consecuencia con «…, so + resultado»

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Sarah, thanks for your comments on the campaign. I see your point about the colors, but I think we should keep the yellow. Although it's a strong color, it's the one people remember because it's in all the brand's stores. We tested two versions with users, so we have real data. Changing it now is possible, though it will delay the launch one week. Let me know what you think. Best, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Desacuerdo en cuatro piezas: but para el choque (I see your point, but…), although para conceder, because para la razón y so para la consecuencia. Nunca although + but ni because + so en la misma frase.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige entre pasado simple (hechos, interrupciones) y pasado continuo (lo que estaba en marcha).
ejercicios.texto: Last Tuesday at ten we {1} the new campaign to a big client. Everything {2} well: Laura {3} the first video and the client {4} at every joke. Suddenly, the fire alarm {5}. We all {6} down eight floors to the street. While we {7} outside, the client {8} me three questions about the budget. It was the strangest meeting of my life.
ejercicios.explica: At ten + la escena en marcha → continuo (were presenting, was going, was showing, was laughing). Lo que interrumpe o avanza la historia → simple (went off, walked). While trae la acción larga (were waiting); three questions es un hecho contado y terminado → asked.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con pasado simple o continuo. Pregúntate: ¿acción larga de fondo o acción corta?
ejercicios.texto: Last month I {1} (walk) to a meeting in the rain when my phone {2} (ring). I {3} (try) to answer it with one hand while I {4} (hold) my umbrella with the other. Of course, the phone {5} (fall) into a puddle. A man who {6} (sell) empanadas on the corner {7} (pick) it up and {8} (give) it back to me. It never worked again, but the empanadas were great.
ejercicios.explica: Acción larga + when + acción corta: I was walking when my phone rang. While trae la acción larga (while I was holding). Los hechos en secuencia van en simple: tried, fell, picked it up, gave it back.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Hay fondo (continuo), acciones en secuencia (simple) y algunas trampas de forma.
ejercicios.texto: I remember my first day at Brava very well. When I {1}, the receptionist {2} on the phone, so I waited. The office was full: some people {3} at their desks and others {4} coffee in the kitchen. Then Laura {5} out of a meeting, {6} my hand and {7} me to my desk. While we {8}, she told me the secret of the agency: 'Never order the coffee from the machine.'
ejercicios.explica: When I arrived (acción corta) + lo que ya estaba pasando (was talking, were working, were drinking). Laura came, shook, took: tres acciones seguidas → simple. While + acción larga: while we were walking.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa la conversación con la policía. Mezcla preguntas y respuestas en pasado simple y continuo.
ejercicios.texto: Yesterday someone stole my wallet at a café. The police officer asked me some questions. 'What {1} (you / do) when it happened?' 'I {2} (work) on my laptop.' '{3} (you / see) the person?' 'No, I {4} (not / see) anybody. I {5} (look) at the screen.' 'When {6} (you / notice) the problem?' 'When I {7} (try) to pay. I {8} (put) my hand in my bag and the wallet wasn't there.'
ejercicios.explica: ¿Qué estabas haciendo en ese momento? → What were you doing? / I was working. ¿Pasó o no pasó? → Did you see…? / I didn't see. Cada tiempo tiene su llave: were para el continuo, did para el simple.

ejercicios.titulo: A wedding in Villa de Leyva
ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con pasado simple o continuo según la historia.
ejercicios.texto: Two years ago my cousin got married in Villa de Leyva. The ceremony was beautiful. While the couple {1} (say) their vows, a dog {2} (run) into the church and {3} (sit) next to the priest. Everybody {4} (start) to laugh. At the party, the band {5} (play) a salsa song when the lights {6} (go) out. For a few minutes we {7} (dance) in the dark. Nobody {8} (want) to go home that night.
ejercicios.explica: While + acción larga (were saying, was playing) y la interrupción en simple (ran, sat, went out). Want es verbo de estado: siempre simple (wanted). For a few minutes acepta los dos: we danced / we were dancing.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta para contar qué pasó en la videollamada.
ejercicios.texto: Last week I {1} a video call with a client about the new website when my internet {2}. While I {3} to reconnect, my boss {4} the call from his phone. When I finally {5} back, he {6} the client a new deadline at that exact moment. The client {7} very happy, but I wasn't. That deadline is impossible! Now the whole team is working on Saturdays because of him.
ejercicios.explica: Acción en marcha (was having, was trying, was giving at that exact moment) frente a lo que pasó de golpe (died, joined, came back). Look como «parecer» es estado: the client looked happy.

ejercicios.texto: In 2019 I was working at a small agency and I wasn't happy. One afternoon I was waiting for a bus on Carrera Séptima when it started to rain hard. I ran into a café and sat at the only free table. A woman was sitting at the next table, and she was reading a marketing book. I made a comment about the book, and we started talking. She asked me a lot of questions about my work. When I left, she gave me her card. It said: Laura Méndez, Creative Director, Brava. Two weeks later, I was working for her.

preguntas.q: Why did he go into the café?
What was the woman doing?
«I was waiting for a bus… when it started to rain»: ¿qué acción interrumpe a la otra?
opciones: I was waiting interrumpe a it started
it started to rain interrumpe a I was waiting

preguntas.q: «Two weeks later, I was working for her»: ¿qué sugiere el continuo?
opciones: Que ya estaba en ese trabajo en ese momento
Que es un hábito de hoy

ejercicios.explica: Dos planos: el fondo en continuo (was working, was waiting, was sitting, was reading) y los hechos en simple (started, ran, sat, made, gave). When trae la acción corta que interrumpe.

ejercicios.texto: Yesterday's meeting with the juice client didn't start well. When we arrived, the marketing team was arguing about the launch date. Nobody was paying attention to us. Laura waited for five minutes, then she stood up and drew a calendar on the whiteboard. While she was drawing, the room went quiet. She marked two possible dates and asked one question: 'Which one gives you more time in stores?' The client team discussed it for ten minutes and chose the second date. When we left, they were still talking about Laura's calendar.

preguntas.q: What was the marketing team doing when they arrived?
What did Laura do after five minutes?
«While she was drawing, the room went quiet»: ¿en qué tiempo va la acción larga?
«they were still talking»: ¿qué significa?

ejercicios.explica: Cuando llegaste, lo que ya estaba pasando → continuo (was arguing, was paying attention). Lo que Laura hizo, paso a paso → simple (waited, stood up, drew, marked, asked).

ejercicios.texto: When I was ten, my dad taught me to ride a bike in a park in Manizales. It was a cold Sunday morning. Other kids were playing soccer and a man was selling ice cream near the gate. My dad was holding the back of the seat and running next to me. 'Don't stop pedaling!' he shouted. I was pedaling as fast as I could. After a few minutes I looked back and saw him. He was standing far away, waving at me. He wasn't holding the bike anymore. I fell immediately, of course. But the next day I rode alone.

preguntas.q: Where did he learn to ride a bike?
What was the man near the gate doing?
«He wasn't holding the bike anymore»: ¿qué descubre el niño?
opciones: Que su papá se había caído

preguntas.q: «I looked back and saw him»: ¿por qué pasado simple?
opciones: Es el fondo de la escena

ejercicios.explica: La escena del parque se pinta en continuo (were playing, was selling, was holding, was running). El momento clave avanza en simple: looked back, saw, fell, rode.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta una anécdota de viaje: qué estabas haciendo cuando pasó algo inesperado y qué hiciste después.

requisitos.texto: Usa was / were + -ing para el fondo
Usa un verbo irregular en pasado simple (went, lost, ran, bought…)
Conecta con when
Ordena lo que hiciste después con then / after that

ejercicios.ejemplo: Three years ago I was traveling to Mexico City for a pitch. I was waiting at the gate and I was reading the presentation one last time when a woman next to me spilled her coffee on my laptop. The screen went black. I ran to a store in the airport and bought a cheap USB drive. Then I found the file in my email and copied it. We won the pitch, and the woman sent me an apology card.
ejercicios.explica: Fondo en continuo (was traveling, was waiting, was reading) + when + la interrupción en simple (spilled). Después, la secuencia de lo que hiciste en simple: ran, bought, found, copied.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuéntale a tu jefe cómo salió una reunión con un cliente: qué estaba pasando cuando llegaste, qué pasó durante la reunión y cómo terminó. Usa while al menos una vez.

requisitos.texto: Usa was / were + -ing
Usa while + was / were + -ing
Usa un verbo regular en pasado simple (-ed)

ejercicios.ejemplo: The meeting went well, but it started late. When I arrived, the client was finishing another call and his assistant was looking for a projector cable. We started at 10:20. While Sarah was showing the media plan, the client asked a lot of questions about the budget. I explained the numbers and he agreed to test the plan for one month. At the end, he invited us for lunch.
ejercicios.explica: While + acción larga en continuo (while Sarah was showing) y lo que pasó en medio en simple (the client asked). Al llegar, lo que estaba en marcha: was finishing, was looking.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe sobre un momento importante de tu vida (una oferta de trabajo, una noticia, un partido) y lo que estabas haciendo cuando te enteraste.

requisitos.texto: Usa was / were + -ing
Usa when + una acción corta en pasado simple
Di cuándo fue (ago, last year, in 2016…)

ejercicios.ejemplo: In 2016 I was living with two friends in a small apartment in Teusaquillo. One Friday night I was cooking pasta and my friends were watching a soccer game when my phone rang. It was a director from an agency. She offered me my first real job in advertising. I burned the pasta, but I didn't care. That night we celebrated with pizza.
ejercicios.explica: Lo que estabas haciendo cuando llegó la noticia → continuo (was cooking, were watching). La noticia → when + simple (when my phone rang). Lo que pasó después sigue en simple: offered, burned, celebrated.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige entre presente simple (lo general, la rutina) y presente continuo (ahora, temporal). Cuidado con los verbos de estado.
ejercicios.texto: Normally, I {1} the week with a team meeting at nine. We {2} the calendar and everybody {3} what they plan to do. But this Monday is different: the CEO {4} the agency, so the meeting is at eight and everybody {5} a jacket. Right now Laura {6} her slides for the third time, and Mike {7} anything because he's nervous. I {8} why. The CEO is a nice guy.
ejercicios.explica: Normally, every week → simple (I start, we review, everybody explains). This Monday, right now → continuo (is visiting, is wearing, is checking, isn't eating). Understand es de estado: I don't understand, nunca I'm not understanding.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con presente simple o continuo según la pista: ¿es su rutina o es algo de este mes?
ejercicios.texto: My sister Natalia {1} (work) as a nurse in Pereira. She usually {2} (start) at six in the morning, but this month she {3} (do) night shifts at the hospital, so she {4} (sleep) during the day. She {5} (not / like) the night shifts at all. When I call her, she always {6} (say) the same thing: 'I can't talk, I {7} (try) to sleep!' Next month her schedule goes back to normal, thank God.
ejercicios.explica: Su profesión y su horario normal son hechos → simple con -s (works, starts, says). This month → continuo (is doing, is sleeping). Like es de estado: doesn't like. Y lo que dice cuando la llamas ocurre en ese momento: I'm trying to sleep.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa las preguntas y respuestas. Decide: ¿pregunta por lo general (do/does) o por lo de ahora (am/is/are + -ing)?
ejercicios.texto: Before I write a brief, I ask the client some questions. 'What {1} (your company / sell) exactly? Who {2} (usually / buy) your products? And this year, what {3} (your competitors / do) on social media? {4} (you / run) any campaigns at the moment?' Today's client {5} (know) her business very well, and she answers fast: 'We {6} (not / advertise) right now, because we {7} (change) our logo this month.'
ejercicios.explica: Lo que la empresa vende y quién compra siempre son hechos → does your company sell; con who como sujeto no hay does: Who usually buys? This year, at the moment, right now → continuo. Know es de estado: she knows.

ejercicios.titulo: A message from a new colleague
ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Pregúntate si el verbo es una acción en progreso o un estado (gustos, saber, necesitar, entender).
ejercicios.texto: Hi Jonathan, I {1} the new office! It's beautiful. I {2} at the desk next to the window, and right now I {3} at the plants on the terrace.
