I {4} you're busy today, so no rush, but I {5} a password for the shared drive. Also, I {6} what 'the war room' means. Is it a meeting room? I {7} for your answer. Thanks!
ejercicios.explica: Acciones que están pasando (sitting, looking, waiting) → continuo. Love, know, need y understand son verbos de estado: van en simple aunque se refieran a ahora mismo.

ejercicios.texto: Laura is the creative director at Brava. She usually rides her bike to the office; it takes her twenty-five minutes. But this month she's driving because it's raining every afternoon. She writes all her ideas in a small black notebook; she doesn't trust apps. At the moment she's leading two big projects: a campaign for a bank and a launch for a juice brand. She isn't sleeping much these days, but she says she's enjoying the pressure. 'I love this job,' she always says, 'even when it's killing me.'

preguntas.q: How does Laura usually get to the office?
Why is she driving this month?
«She writes all her ideas in a small black notebook»: ¿por qué presente simple?
«I love this job»: ¿por qué love no va en -ing?
opciones: Porque love es un verbo de estado

ejercicios.explica: Usually, always, lo que alguien es o hace siempre → simple (rides, writes, doesn't trust). This month, at the moment, these days → continuo (is driving, is leading, isn't sleeping). Love es estado: I love this job.

ejercicios.texto: Felipe and I studied together, but our lives are very different now. I work at an agency, I live in Bogotá and I take the same bus every day. Felipe doesn't have an office; he's a photographer and he travels all the time. This month he's working in the Amazon for a documentary. He's sleeping in a hammock and he isn't using his phone much. I'm sitting at my desk right now, reading his message: 'The river is amazing. Come here!' I don't know. I like my bed too much.

preguntas.q: What does Felipe do?
Where is Felipe this month?
«Felipe doesn't have an office»: ¿por qué doesn't y no isn't?
opciones: Porque have (tener) es un hecho, no algo en progreso

preguntas.q: «I'm sitting at my desk right now»: ¿por qué continuo?
opciones: Porque es un verbo de estado

ejercicios.explica: Lo que cada uno es y hace en general → simple (I work, he travels, doesn't have). Lo de este mes o de ahora → continuo (he's working, he's sleeping, I'm sitting). Have como «tener» es estado: doesn't have.

ejercicios.consigna: Compara tu semana típica con esta semana: qué haces normalmente en el trabajo y qué estás haciendo distinto estos días.

requisitos.texto: Usa presente simple con una expresión de frecuencia (usually, normally, every day…)
Usa am / is / are + -ing para lo temporal
Marca lo temporal (this week, these days, at the moment…)

ejercicios.ejemplo: I usually get to the office at eight and I have a team meeting at nine. I normally spend the afternoon with clients and I go home at six. But this week is different. We're preparing a big pitch, so I'm staying at the office until ten every night. I'm not going to the gym and I'm eating pizza at my desk. My girlfriend isn't happy about it, but the pitch is on Friday.
ejercicios.explica: La comparación pide los dos tiempos: lo de siempre en simple (I usually get, I normally spend) y lo de esta semana en continuo (we're preparing, I'm staying, I'm not going).

ejercicios.consigna: Un cliente te pregunta cómo va el proyecto. Respóndele: qué está haciendo el equipo ahora y qué opinas, con al menos dos verbos de estado (think, know, need, want, prefer…) en simple.

requisitos.texto: Usa dos verbos de estado (think, know, need, want, like, prefer…)
Usa am / is / are + -ing para lo que pasa ahora
Termina con una pregunta

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Patricia, good news. The team is working on the second version of the storyboard right now, and the designers are adjusting the colors you mentioned. I think the new version is much stronger. We know the launch date is close, so we're moving fast. We need your feedback on the music by Thursday. Do you prefer the first option or the second?
ejercicios.explica: El avance del trabajo va en continuo (is working, are adjusting, we're moving). Opiniones, conocimiento y necesidades van en simple aunque sean de hoy: I think, we know, we need, do you prefer.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el cuantificador que traduce la pista: much / many / a lot of / a few / a little / some / any / how much / how many. Pregúntate primero: ¿se puede contar?
ejercicios.texto: Laura, a few questions about the workshop on Friday. {1} (cuántas) people are coming? I need to order lunch. We don't have {2} (mucho) space in the room, so the group is small. Is there {3} (algo de) budget for printed materials? I think we need {4} (unos pocos) posters and {5} (un poco de) time for questions at the end. We don't have {6} (ningún) markers in the office, so I'll buy some. And {7} (cuánto) money can we spend on the venue? Last year there were {8} (muchos) problems with the sound, so let's test it the day before.
ejercicios.explica: People y posters se cuentan → how many, a few. Space, time y money no → much, a little, how much. Any en negativas y preguntas (Is there any budget? We don't have any markers). En afirmativa, a lot of sirve para todo.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Es un email interno con los resultados de la semana: contable o incontable decide.
ejercicios.texto: Hi team, quick update on the campaign. We got {1} comments on Instagram this week, more than 3,000! Unfortunately, we didn't get {2} sales from the website: only 40. The client has {3} questions about the numbers, so I need {4} information before the call. How {5} people clicked on the link? And how {6} money did we spend on ads in total? We have {7} time before the meeting, about an hour, so please send me the data now. The news {8} good, but we need to explain it well.
ejercicios.explica: Comments, sales, questions, people → contables (a lot of, many, a few, how many). Information, money, time → incontables (some, how much, a little). News es incontable y va en singular: The news is good.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige entre las dos opciones de la pista y escribe la correcta. Some en afirmativa y ofrecimientos; any en negativa y pregunta.
ejercicios.texto: It's my turn to buy breakfast for the team. Is there {1} (some / any) milk in the fridge? No, there isn't {2} (some / any). We have {3} (much / a lot of) bread, but we don't have {4} (much / many) eggs: only three. I'll buy {5} (a few / a little) bananas too, because Camila doesn't eat bread. How {6} (much / many) cups of coffee do we need? There are twelve people on the team, so twelve. Would you like {7} (some / any) juice, Andrés? He says no, just coffee. I don't have {8} (much / many) cash, so I'll pay by card.
ejercicios.explica: Any en pregunta y negativa; some en el ofrecimiento (Would you like some juice?). A lot of en afirmativa (much ahí suena raro). Eggs, bananas y cups son contables → many, a few; cash es incontable → much.

ejercicios.texto: October is always a busy month at Brava. We have a lot of work and not much time. This year there are three new clients, and each one wants a lot of meetings. I get about eighty emails a day, and I don't have much time to answer them, so I answer a few in the morning and a few after lunch. Our creative team needs more people, but there isn't much money for new hires. My boss gave me a piece of advice: 'Don't say yes to every request. Ask how much time it needs first.' It was good advice. Now, before a meeting, I ask: how many people need to be there? Usually, fewer than we think.

preguntas.q: Why doesn't Jonathan answer all his emails at once?
Why can't the team hire more people?
«a piece of advice»: ¿por qué se dice así?
opciones: Advice es incontable: para contarlo se usa a piece of
Es un error: debería ser an advice

preguntas.q: «how many people need to be there?»: ¿por qué many y no much?
opciones: Porque people es contable y plural

ejercicios.explica: Work, time, money y advice son incontables (a lot of work, not much time, a piece of advice). Emails, meetings y people se cuentan (a lot of meetings, a few emails, how many people).

ejercicios.texto: On Saturday my girlfriend and I had dinner at home with six friends. On Friday night I checked the kitchen: there was some rice, a little cheese and a few tomatoes, but there wasn't any meat and we didn't have much wine. So on Saturday morning we went to the market. 'How much chicken do we need?' I asked. 'For eight people? About two kilos,' she said. 'And how many bottles of wine?' 'Four is enough. Not many of our friends drink.' At the end of the night, there was a lot of food left, but there wasn't any wine. Next time, more wine and less chicken.

preguntas.q: What didn't they have on Friday night?
How many people were at the dinner in total?
«How much chicken…?» y «How many bottles…?»: ¿por qué cambia?
opciones: Chicken (carne) es incontable; bottles es contable y plural
Es lo mismo, se pueden cambiar
Many es para comida y much para bebida

preguntas.q: «there wasn't any wine»: ¿por qué any y no some?

ejercicios.explica: Rice, cheese, meat, wine y chicken (como comida) son incontables: a little, much, how much. Tomatoes, bottles y friends se cuentan: a few, many, how many. Some en afirmativa, any en negativa.

ejercicios.consigna: Estás preparando el presupuesto de un evento para un cliente. Escribe un mensaje a tu equipo pidiendo la información que te falta: cuántas personas, cuánto dinero, qué hay y qué no hay.

requisitos.texto: Pregunta con How much…? o How many…?
Usa much o many en una negativa
Usa a few o a little
Usa some o any

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi team, I'm preparing the budget for the client event in November and I need some information. How many people are coming from their side? We don't have much money this year, so we need to be careful. I'd like a few options for the venue and a little time on Thursday to review them together. Do we have any photos from last year's event? Thanks, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Cada sustantivo decide su cuantificador: people y options se cuentan (how many, a few); money, time e information no (much, a little, some). Much y many suenan naturales en negativa y pregunta; any en preguntas.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa el email con las piezas fijas: motivo, adjunto, pedido, seguimiento y cierre. No traduzcas del español: usa las fórmulas.
ejercicios.texto: Hi Mike, I'm {1} (write) to confirm our meeting on Thursday at 10 a.m. {2} (adjunto) the agenda and the latest version of the proposal. {3} (could / you / review) it before the meeting? I'd also like {4} (you / invite) Sarah, because she knows the budget. I'm also {5} (follow) up on the contract: did your legal team sign it? Let me know if you have any {6} (preguntas). Looking forward to {7} (see) you on Thursday. {8} (cierre formal), Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Un email son piezas: I'm writing to… (motivo, en continuo), Please find attached… (adjunto), Could you + verbo? (pedido), I'd like you to + verbo (no «I want that you»), I'm following up on…, Looking forward to + -ing y Best regards.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Es un email para mover una llamada; fíjate en las fórmulas fijas.
ejercicios.texto: {1} Sarah, Sorry for the {2} reply; this week was crazy. I'm writing {3} our call on Friday. Unfortunately, I have a conflict at 3 p.m. Could we {4} it to Monday? Would 10 a.m. {5} for you? I've also {6} the new version of the deck, with the changes from Tuesday. {7} you have any questions before the call, let me know. Looking forward to {8} from you. Best regards, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Hi + nombre (Estimated es un calco). Sorry for the late reply. I'm writing about… Could we move it…? Would 10 a.m. work for you? (verbo base tras would). I've attached. Looking forward to hearing: -ing después de to.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa el email de seguimiento. Recuerda: I'm following / looking forward to + -ing, Could you + verbo base, I'd like you to + verbo.
ejercicios.texto: Hi Mike, I'm {1} (follow) up on the proposal I sent last week. I know you have {2} (mucho) work this month, so here is a short summary. We need {3} (unos pocos) days to prepare the production, so we'd like to start on the 15th. {4} (could / you / confirm) the budget by Friday? If you prefer, we can {5} (programar) a 15-minute call. I'd like {6} (you / send) us the logo files too. Thanks for your help, and sorry {7} (por) the delay on our side last month. {8} (look forward / hear) from you. Best, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Seguimiento: I'm following up on… Work es incontable (a lot of work) y days contable (a few days). Pedidos: Could you confirm…?, I'd like you to send… Disculpa: sorry for the delay. Cierre: Looking forward to hearing from you.

ejercicios.texto: Hi Jonathan, Thanks for the proposal. I'm writing to share some feedback from our team. In general, we love the creative idea, especially the videos with real customers. However, the budget is a bit higher than we expected. Could you send us a version with fewer videos and more photos? We'd also like to move the launch from May 3 to May 17, because our new stores open that week. Please find attached the store calendar. Would Tuesday at 4 p.m. work for a quick call? Sorry for the short notice. Looking forward to hearing from you. Kind regards, Sarah

preguntas.q: What does Sarah want to change?
opciones: The budget and the launch date

preguntas.q: Why does she want to move the launch?
opciones: The new stores open that week

preguntas.q: «Would Tuesday at 4 p.m. work for a quick call?»: ¿qué hace Sarah?
«Looking forward to hearing from you»: ¿por qué hearing con -ing?
opciones: Porque después de looking forward to va -ing
Es opcional: también vale to hear

ejercicios.explica: Un email de cliente nativo usa las mismas piezas que tú debes usar: I'm writing to share…, Could you send us…?, We'd like to…, Please find attached…, Would + hora + work…?, Looking forward to hearing from you.

ejercicios.texto: When I started writing emails in English, I translated from Spanish. My emails looked like this: 'Estimated Mike: I write you to send you attached the proposal. I want that you review it. Attentively, Jonathan.' Mike was polite, but my boss laughed. She showed me how to write with fixed pieces: 'Hi Mike, I'm writing to share the proposal. Please find it attached. Could you review it by Friday? Let me know if you have any questions. Best regards, Jonathan.' Now I have a list of these pieces on my desk. I don't translate anymore; I build my emails like Lego.

preguntas.q: What was the problem with his first emails?
What does he have on his desk now?
¿Cómo se dice bien «Quiero que lo revises»?
opciones: I want that you review it.

preguntas.q: ¿Qué cierre NO se usa en un email en inglés?

ejercicios.explica: Estimated, I write you to, I want that you y Attentively son calcos. Sus piezas en inglés: Hi + nombre, I'm writing to…, Please find attached…, Could you…?, Best regards.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe un email a un cliente para enviarle la propuesta de una campaña (adjunta) y proponerle una llamada para revisarla.

requisitos.texto: Abre con I'm writing to + verbo
Menciona el adjunto (Please find attached / I've attached)
requisitos.patron: \b(please find attached|i've attached|i have attached|attached is)\b

requisitos.texto: Pide con Could you…? o propone con Would … work for you?
Cierra con Looking forward to + -ing

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Mike, I'm writing to share our proposal for the summer campaign. Please find attached the deck with the two creative routes and the budget. Could you review it with your team before next week? I'd like to schedule a 30-minute call to answer your questions. Would Tuesday at 10 a.m. work for you? Let me know if you need anything else. Looking forward to hearing from you. Best regards, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Un email que no suena traducido usa la secuencia fija: I'm writing to… → Please find attached… → Could you…? / Would … work for you? → Looking forward to hearing from you → Best regards. Después de looking forward to, siempre -ing.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige el futuro correcto: will (decisión u ofrecimiento en el momento, opinión), going to (plan o evidencia) o presente continuo (cita ya organizada).
ejercicios.texto: Laura: 'The client wants the deck by tomorrow.' Me: 'No problem, I {1} it tonight.' Mike: 'Sorry, I can't help. I {2} my sister at the airport at eight; she booked the flight weeks ago.' Laura: 'OK. Look at the sky. It {3} rain. Who has an umbrella?' Sarah: 'Don't worry, I {4} you mine.' Laura: 'Thanks. And good news: next year we {5} a bigger team; we already have the budget.' Me: 'Great. And I think the client {6} the new idea.'
ejercicios.explica: Decides u ofreces en el momento → will (I'll finish it, I'll lend you mine). Cita con hora y persona → continuo (I'm picking up my sister at eight). Evidencia que ves → going to (It's going to rain). Plan ya decidido → going to. Opinión (I think…) → will.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con un futuro adecuado. Cita con día u hora → presente continuo; plan → going to; predicción u opinión → will. Hay varias respuestas válidas.
ejercicios.texto: Next week is going to be intense. On Monday I {1} (meet) the new client at nine; it's already in my calendar. On Tuesday the team {2} (present) the first ideas, and I'm sure the client {3} (ask) a lot of questions. On Wednesday I {4} (not / go) to the office because I {5} (fly) to Medellín for a shoot. I {6} (try) to rest on the plane, but I know I {7} (answer) emails the whole flight.
ejercicios.explica: Lo que está en tu calendario (on Monday at nine, a flight) → presente continuo: I'm meeting, I'm flying. Intenciones → going to: I'm going to try. Lo que crees que pasará (I'm sure, I know) → will: the client will ask, I'll answer.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con will / won't + verbo base. Son promesas, ofrecimientos y decisiones del momento.
ejercicios.texto: A message to my team after a hard week: 'Thanks for your work, everybody. I know it was a crazy week. I promise next month {1} (be) calmer. I {2} (not / accept) more projects without talking to you first. Camila, don't worry about the report; I {3} (do) it myself. Andrés, {4} (you / send) me the files tonight? Then I {5} (review) them tomorrow morning. And on Friday the pizza is on me. I {6} (order) it at one, so don't bring lunch.'
ejercicios.explica: Promesas (I promise… will be, I won't accept), ofrecimientos (I'll do it myself) y peticiones (Will you send me…?) → will. Después de will el verbo va siempre en base; la negativa es won't.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta: plan ya decidido, cita organizada, decisión del momento u opinión.
ejercicios.texto: My girlfriend and I already have plans for December. We {1} to Cartagena; we bought the tickets last month. We {2} on the 20th and come back on the 28th. On the 19th we {3} dinner with her parents in Chía. My dad is alone in Manizales, so I'm worried. Maybe I {4} him and invite him to Cartagena. But I think he {5} no; he hates the heat. Wait, I have an idea: I {6} him the photos of the hotel pool. That {7} him!
ejercicios.explica: Plan ya decidido (tickets comprados) → going to. Fechas organizadas → continuo (are leaving, are having). Maybe, I think, una idea que surge ahora → will (I'll call, he'll say, I'll send, that will convince him).

ejercicios.texto: Brava is going to move to a new office in January. The building is in Chicó, and it has a terrace with a view of the mountains. The management team is going to divide the space into open areas and small rooms for calls. 'People will love the terrace,' says Laura. Not everybody agrees. Mike lives in the south, so he's going to spend more time in traffic. 'I'll probably work from home more,' he says. The move is happening on the second weekend of January, and the agency is closing on that Friday so everybody can pack.

preguntas.q: When is Brava going to move?
Why isn't Mike happy?
opciones: He'll spend more time in traffic

preguntas.q: «The move is happening on the second weekend of January»: ¿por qué presente continuo?
opciones: Es un plan con fecha ya organizado

preguntas.q: «People will love the terrace»: ¿qué expresa will aquí?

ejercicios.explica: Planes decididos → going to (is going to move, is going to divide). Fechas ya organizadas → continuo (is happening, is closing). Opiniones y probabilidades → will (people will love, I'll probably work).

ejercicios.texto: In the elevator, I met Sarah. She was carrying two big boxes. 'Are you moving?' I asked. 'No, I'm going to sell these old cameras online,' she said. 'I'm buying a new one next week.' 'Do you need help? I'll take one box.' 'Thanks! Are you coming to Camila's party on Saturday?' 'I don't think so. I'm visiting my dad in Manizales this weekend. But I'll send her a gift.' 'Good idea. She's going to be thirty, so she'll probably cry a little.' We both laughed. The elevator stopped at the fifth floor and the doors opened.

preguntas.q: What is Sarah going to do with the old cameras?
Why isn't he going to the party?
«I'll take one box»: ¿por qué will?
opciones: Es un ofrecimiento decidido en el momento

preguntas.q: «I'm visiting my dad in Manizales this weekend»: ¿qué tipo de futuro es?

ejercicios.explica: Ofrecimientos en el momento → will (I'll take one box, I'll send her a gift). Planes → going to (I'm going to sell). Citas y viajes organizados → continuo (I'm buying, I'm visiting).

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe a tu equipo el plan de la próxima semana: qué ya está organizado (con día u hora), qué vas a hacer y una predicción sobre el cliente.

requisitos.texto: Usa going to + verbo base
Usa will / 'll + verbo base para una predicción
Usa presente continuo con un día o una hora

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi team, here is the plan for next week. We're meeting the bank's marketing team on Monday at ten, and Laura is presenting the new storyboard at 2 p.m. on Wednesday. On Tuesday I'm going to review all the slides with Camila, so please send me your parts before Monday night. I think the client will like the idea, but they'll probably ask for a cheaper version. Let's prepare one just in case.
ejercicios.explica: Tres futuros en un mismo correo: citas con fecha en continuo (we're meeting, Laura is presenting), tu plan con going to (I'm going to review) y la predicción con will (the client will like, they'll ask).

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe tus propósitos para el próximo año (personales y de trabajo): dos planes con going to, una promesa con will y algo que no vas a hacer.

requisitos.texto: Usa going to + verbo base
Usa will / 'll para una promesa
Incluye una negativa (won't / not going to)
Usa next year

ejercicios.ejemplo: Next year is going to be important for me. I'm going to take an English course in the mornings, and I'm going to travel with my girlfriend to Mexico. At work, I'm going to delegate more to my team. I promise I'll leave the office before seven at least three days a week. And I won't answer emails on Sundays. That's the hardest one.
ejercicios.explica: Propósitos ya decididos → going to (I'm going to take, I'm going to travel). Promesas → will / won't (I'll leave, I won't answer). Después de will y de going to el verbo va en base.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa la llamada. Para pedir: Could you…? Para tomar el control: Let me + verbo base. Oír es hear, y en silencio es on mute.
ejercicios.texto: — Hi everyone, can you {1} (oír) me? — Yes, but I think Laura is {2} (en silencio). — Sorry! Can you hear me now? — Yes. OK, {3} (let / me / share) my screen. {4} (can / you / see) it? — Yes, we can. — Great. Sorry, Mike, {5} (could / you / repeat) that? The audio cut out. — Sure. I said the client called this morning. — Thanks. Could you speak more {6} (despacio)? The connection is bad. — No problem. — I think Andrés {7} (freeze, pasado). — Let me {8} (check) the chat. He says he's coming back.
ejercicios.explica: En una llamada: Can you hear me? (no listen), You're on mute (no in mute), Could you repeat that? (that, no me), more slowly (no more slow), I think you froze. Let me share / Let me check: verbo base, sin to.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Es la apertura de una presentación de resultados con su estructura fija.
ejercicios.texto: Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining. {1} to talk about the results of the summer campaign. {2}, I'll show you the numbers. Then, we'll look at what worked, and {3}, our recommendations for next year. Let me share my screen. As you can {4} on this {5}, sales went {6} 18% in July, and July was our best month. {7}, the campaign worked, and it worked fast. That's all from me. Any {8}?
ejercicios.explica: La estructura fija: Today I'm going to talk about… → First… Then… Finally… → As you can see on this chart (chart = gráfico de datos) → sales went up → To sum up → Any questions? (plural; doubts es un calco).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa la ronda de preguntas. Agradece la pregunta, explica con Let me…, y si no sabes, promete volver con la respuesta.
ejercicios.texto: — Thank you, Jonathan. I have a question about the budget. — That's a good {1} (pregunta). — Why did we spend more in July? — {2} (let / me / explain). We had {3} (más) people at the events, so we needed more staff. — How {4} (much / many) people came? — About 5,000. — And did sales go {5} (subir)? — Yes, 18%. — Interesting. What about the TikTok results? — I don't have the numbers here. {6} (dejarme / responderte luego) on that by Friday. {7} (does / that / answer) your question? — Yes, thanks. — Great. That's all {8} (de mi parte).

respuestas: Let me get back to you

ejercicios.explica: Para las preguntas: That's a good question → Let me explain → Let me get back to you on that (si no sabes) → Does that answer your question? → That's all from me. People es contable: how many. Sales go up / down.

ejercicios.texto: Last week I presented the quarterly results to our client in Miami, in English, for the first time. I practiced the structure five times: 'Today I'm going to talk about the results. First, the numbers. Then, what worked. Finally, next steps.' At the beginning, there was a problem: Sarah couldn't hear me. 'Jonathan, I think you're on mute,' she said. I fixed it and started again. When I showed the main chart, I said, 'As you can see, sales went up 18%.' At the end, Mike asked a difficult question about costs. I didn't know the answer, so I said, 'Let me get back to you on that.' It worked.

preguntas.q: How many times did he practice?
What was the problem at the beginning?
«Let me get back to you on that»: ¿para qué sirve?
opciones: Para responder después cuando no sabes la respuesta

preguntas.q: ¿Por qué dice chart y no graphic?
opciones: Chart es un gráfico de datos; graphic es una pieza de diseño

ejercicios.explica: Una presentación segura es una estructura ensayada (Today I'm going to… First… Then… Finally…) más tres salvavidas: You're on mute, As you can see… y Let me get back to you on that.

ejercicios.texto: At Brava we have a lot of video calls with clients in the U.S., so we wrote some simple rules. First, join two minutes early and check your camera and microphone. Second, stay on mute when you're not speaking, especially in a noisy office. Third, if you don't understand something, don't stay quiet: say 'Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you repeat that?' Nobody will think your English is bad. Fourth, if you're presenting, say what you're going to talk about first. Finally, at the end of the call, summarize the next steps and ask, 'Any questions?' Clients notice the difference.

preguntas.q: When should you join a call?
What should you do if you don't understand something?
¿Cuál es la forma INCORRECTA de pedir que repitan?
«stay on mute»: ¿qué preposición lleva mute?

ejercicios.explica: Las reglas de la llamada son frases fijas: on mute (no in mute), Sorry, I didn't catch that, Could you repeat that? (that, no me), y Any questions? en plural para cerrar.

ejercicios.consigna: Mañana presentas los resultados de una campaña a un cliente en inglés. Escribe el guion de los primeros 30 segundos: saluda, comparte pantalla, di de qué vas a hablar, da la estructura y señala un dato.

requisitos.texto: Abre con Today I'm going to talk about / show / present
Guía con First… y Then… / Finally…
Señala un dato con As you can see…
Usa Let me + verbo base (sin to)

ejercicios.ejemplo: Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining. Let me share my screen. Today I'm going to talk about the results of the back-to-school campaign. First, I'll show you the main numbers. Then, we'll look at what worked on each channel, and finally, I'll share our recommendations for next year. As you can see on this chart, sales went up 22% in August. Let me explain why.
ejercicios.explica: La apertura que nunca falla: Let me share my screen → Today I'm going to talk about… → First… Then… Finally… → As you can see on this chart… Let me va con verbo base: let me explain, nunca let me to explain.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el modal y el verbo entre paréntesis. Después del modal el verbo va en forma base: sin to, sin -s, sin do. En las preguntas, el modal pasa delante del sujeto.
ejercicios.texto: Hi team, quick note before tomorrow's call. I {1} (will / send) the agenda tonight, so please read it before 9. Laura {2} (can / not / join) us because she has a dentist appointment, but she {3} (will / share) her comments by email. {4} (could / you / print) three copies of the deck, Andrés? The client {5} (may / ask) about the budget again, so I {6} (will / prepare) a short answer. One more thing: {7} (can / we / start) five minutes early? Their CEO is always on time.
ejercicios.explica: El modal es la llave: recibe el not (can't join), pasa delante del sujeto en la pregunta (Could you print? Can we start?) y el verbo queda desnudo (will send, may ask). Nada de «will to send» ni «Do you can».

ejercicios.titulo: Checking in at a hotel in Miami
ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta en cada hueco. Es un diálogo en la recepción: pedir con cortesía, permiso y promesas.
ejercicios.texto: Good evening. I {1} a room for two nights, please. — Of course. {2} I see your passport? — Sure, here you are. {3} pay by card? — Yes, you can. Breakfast is from 6 to 10. — Great. One more question: {4} I have a late check-out on Friday? My flight is at 6 pm. — I'm afraid we {5} do that on Fridays; the hotel is full. But you {6} leave your bags at the front desk. — Perfect. And {7} you call me a taxi tomorrow at 8? — Don't worry, I {8} take care of it.
ejercicios.explica: I'd like + sustantivo (sin to). May I / Could I para permiso y peticiones corteses; Can I…? con el modal delante, nunca «Do I can». La negativa es can't (no «don't can») y la promesa del momento es I'll + verbo base.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el modal y el verbo. Fíjate en el tiempo: could también es can en pasado (habilidad), y en las preguntas el modal va primero.
ejercicios.texto: When I started at Brava, I {1} (could / not / speak) English on calls, so I stayed quiet. Now things are different. Yesterday the client asked for the campaign in two weeks and I said: 'I'm afraid we {2} (can / not / deliver) everything by the 20th, but we {3} (can / send) the key visual first. {4} (could / we / move) the final deadline to the 27th? I {5} (will / confirm) the plan with my team today.' She said yes. Then I asked: '{6} (may / I / share) my screen to show you the timeline?' Small victory.
ejercicios.explica: Couldn't speak = no podía (habilidad en pasado). Can't deliver / can send para lo que puedes o no puedes hacer; Could we move…? pide con cortesía; I'll confirm es el compromiso del momento; May I share…? pide permiso formal. Siempre modal + verbo base.

ejercicios.texto: Last Tuesday, Camila had her first call alone with a client in Miami. Before the call, she was nervous: 'What if I can't understand them?' she asked me. I told her two things: 'You can always ask them to repeat, and you don't have to answer everything on the spot. Just say: I'll get back to you.' The call went well. The client asked for a discount, and Camila said, 'I can't decide that today, but I'll talk to Jonathan and I will send you an answer by Thursday.' Then they asked if the campaign could launch in May. She said, 'May I check the production calendar first?' Professional and calm. When she was a kid, she couldn't even order food in English. Now she negotiates deadlines.

preguntas.q: What did Camila promise to do?
Why does she say «I can't decide that today»?
opciones: She doesn't have the power to decide alone

preguntas.q: «May I check the production calendar first?»: ¿qué hace Camila con may?
«She couldn't even order food in English»: ¿qué expresa couldn't aquí?
opciones: Habilidad en el pasado, en negativa

ejercicios.explica: Cada modal tiene su trabajo: can't = no puedo (habilidad o posibilidad), I'll = promesa del momento, may I = permiso formal, couldn't = no podía (can en pasado). Todos van con el verbo en base.

ejercicios.titulo: A weekend in Villa de Leyva
ejercicios.texto: My girlfriend and I are planning a weekend in Villa de Leyva. I can drive, but I don't like the road at night, so we'll leave early on Saturday. She can't take Friday off because her boss is traveling, which means we can't stay three nights. I'd like a hotel with a pool, but she says a small guesthouse will be cheaper and nicer. 'Could you book it tonight?' she asked me. 'Sure, I'll do it after dinner,' I said. There is one problem: my mom wants to come with us. She can't walk long distances anymore, so we will need a place near the main square. And one promise I made: this time I won't check my work email.

preguntas.q: When will they leave?
What is the problem with his mom?
«I'd like a hotel with a pool»: ¿qué es I'd like?
opciones: La forma cortés de I want

preguntas.q: «I won't check my work email»: ¿qué es won't?
opciones: will + not: una promesa o decisión

ejercicios.explica: Can / can't para habilidad y posibilidad (I can drive, she can't take Friday off), could you para pedir, I'll / won't para prometer y decidir, I'd like como el I want cortés. Después de todos ellos, verbo base.

ejercicios.consigna: Responde por escrito a un cliente que pide adelantar la entrega: di qué puedes y qué no puedes hacer (can / can't), pídele algo con cortesía (Could you…?), comprométete con una fecha (I'll … by …) y pide permiso para algo (May I…? / Can I…?).

requisitos.texto: Di qué no puedes hacer con can't / cannot
Pide algo con Could you…?
Comprométete con I'll / I will + verbo … by + fecha
Pide permiso con May I…? / Can I…?

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Sarah, thanks for your message. I understand the launch date changed. We can deliver the key visual and the three social posts next week, but we can't finish the video by the 15th; production needs ten more days. Could you confirm which pieces are the priority for the launch? I'll send you a new timeline by Thursday morning, and I will call you after that to go over it. May I share this change with the media team today? Best regards, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: En una negociación los modales hacen todo el trabajo: can / can't para lo posible, Could you…? para pedir sin sonar brusco, I'll … by … para comprometerte con fecha y May I…? para pedir permiso. El verbo siempre va en base después del modal.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el pasado continuo (was / were + -ing). Estás describiendo el fondo de la escena.
ejercicios.texto: Last Saturday my girlfriend and I went to a new restaurant in La Macarena. It was a busy night. A man {1} (play) the guitar near the door and a group of friends {2} (celebrate) a birthday at the big table. Two waiters {3} (run) from table to table. Next to us, an old couple {4} (not / talk); they {5} (look) at their phones. My girlfriend {6} (tell) me a story about her boss, but I {7} (not / listen). I {8} (think) about the pitch on Monday.
ejercicios.explica: Para pintar la escena (lo que estaba pasando alrededor) → was/were + -ing. Was con I, he, she, a man, my girlfriend; were con we, they, a group of friends, two waiters, an old couple. Negativa: wasn't/weren't + -ing.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la llave correcta: was, were (o sus negativas). Mira bien el sujeto.
ejercicios.texto: Yesterday at ten we had the weekly status meeting, and nobody was paying attention. Laura {1} drawing in her notebook. Mike and Sarah {2} sending messages under the table. The client {3} looking at his watch every two minutes. Andrés {4} reading his emails. {5} I listening? Not really: I {6} thinking about lunch. When the client asked 'Any questions?', we {7} even looking at him.
ejercicios.explica: La llave del pasado continuo es be: was (I, he, she, Laura, the client) y were (we, you, they, Mike and Sarah). Did nunca va con -ing. En la pregunta, was/were pasa delante: Was I listening?

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa las preguntas y respuestas en pasado continuo. Pregunta: (Wh-) + was / were + sujeto + -ing.
ejercicios.texto: On Monday my boss had some questions. 'I called you three times last night. What {1} (you / do)?' 'Sorry, I {2} (drive) back from Chía with my girlfriend.' '{3} (she / drive) at any point?' 'No, she {4} (sleep) in the passenger seat.' 'OK. And who {5} (you / talk) to at eleven? Your line was busy.' 'My dad. He {6} (watch) a soccer game and he {7} (complain) about the referee.' My boss smiled: 'I {8} (shout) at the same referee!'
ejercicios.explica: Para preguntar qué estaba haciendo alguien en un momento: What were you doing?, Was she driving? Con who, la llave también va delante del sujeto: who were you… to? La respuesta repite la llave: I was driving, she was sleeping.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el pasado continuo. Hay varias negativas: wasn't / weren't + -ing.
ejercicios.texto: After the presentation, the client asked: 'Did your team see my email at nine?' The honest answer was no. At nine we {1} (not / check) emails. Camila {2} (not / work) yet; she {3} (have) breakfast with her kids. Andrés and Mike {4} (not / sit) at their desks; they {5} (fix) the printer downstairs. And I {6} (not / look) at my phone because I {7} (practice) the presentation in the meeting room. So I said: 'Sorry, we {8} (prepare) everything for you.'
ejercicios.explica: Explicar qué estaba haciendo cada uno a una hora concreta (at nine) → pasado continuo. La negativa lleva el not en la llave: wasn't working, weren't sitting; el -ing se queda.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Las trampas: falta el -ing, falta la llave o la llave no concuerda.
ejercicios.texto: When I was a kid in Manizales, Sunday mornings were always the same. At nine my dad {1} the radio in the kitchen and my mom {2} arepas. My brother and I {3} cartoons in the living room. Outside, our neighbor {4} his car, like every Sunday. One Sunday the power went off. My mom still asks me: 'What {5} when the lights went off?' The answer: I {6} a glass of hot chocolate in front of the TV. And the TV {7} anymore.
ejercicios.explica: Las dos piezas van juntas: was/were + verbo-ing. Sin -ing (was make) o sin llave (washing) no hay continuo. Did no entra: What were you doing?, the TV wasn't working.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el pasado continuo para contar qué estaba haciendo cada persona cuando todo se apagó.
ejercicios.texto: It happened last October. It was five in the afternoon and the whole team {1} (finish) the presentation for the bank. Sarah {2} (edit) the video, Andrés {3} (export) the final slides and I {4} (write) the email to the client. Suddenly, the screens went black. For a second nobody said anything. Then everybody started shouting at the same time. 'What {5} (you / do)?' Andrés asked Sarah. 'Nothing! I {6} (just / save) the file!' Luckily, the IT guy {7} (still / work) in the basement, and he had a backup.
ejercicios.explica: En una anécdota, lo que estaba en marcha cuando pasó algo va en pasado continuo (was finishing, was editing); el golpe de la historia va en simple (the screens went black). Just y still van entre la llave y el -ing.

ejercicios.texto: Last Thursday at 3:15 there was a small earthquake in Bogotá. I was sitting in a meeting with the client from the bank on the eighth floor. Laura was presenting the new campaign and the client was taking notes. Suddenly, the glass of water on the table started to move. At first we thought it was a truck outside. Then the lamps started to swing. Mike was standing next to the window, and he was the first to run to the stairs. Five minutes later we were all in the street, and the client was still holding her notebook. 'Great presentation,' she said. 'Let's finish it on Monday.'

preguntas.q: Where was he when the earthquake started?
opciones: In a meeting on the eighth floor

preguntas.q: Who was presenting the campaign?
«Laura was presenting… Suddenly, the glass started to move»: ¿qué parte es el fondo de la historia?
«the client was still holding her notebook»: ¿qué expresa?
opciones: Que lo soltó antes del temblor
Que lo agarró una sola vez
Que seguía sosteniéndolo en ese momento

ejercicios.explica: Was/were + -ing pinta lo que estaba en marcha (was sitting, was presenting, was standing) y el pasado simple trae los hechos (started, thought, said). Still + continuo: la acción seguía en curso.

ejercicios.texto: Last night my phone rang at 2 a.m. I was sleeping, of course. It was my friend Felipe. 'Were you sleeping?' he asked. 'No, I was dancing salsa,' I said. 'Of course I was sleeping! Where are you?' He was calling from the airport in Lima. His flight was delayed, his phone was dying, and he was looking for a hotel. 'Can you book me something? My card isn't working.' Ten minutes later, I was sitting on the bed with my laptop, half asleep, looking for hotels in a city I don't know. My girlfriend wasn't sleeping anymore, and she wasn't happy.

preguntas.q: Where was Felipe calling from?
What was Felipe looking for?
«Were you sleeping?»: ¿cómo se forma esta pregunta?
«My girlfriend wasn't sleeping anymore»: ¿qué significa?

ejercicios.explica: Preguntar por lo que alguien estaba haciendo: Were you sleeping? (were + sujeto + -ing). Para describir la situación de alguien en ese momento: he was calling, his phone was dying, he was looking for a hotel.

ejercicios.texto: When I arrived at 9:30, the facilitator was explaining the rules and the client team was sitting on one side of the room. Our team was standing on the other side, drinking coffee. By eleven, everybody was working together: two groups were writing ideas on sticky notes and another group was drawing the customer journey on the wall. At lunch the client's CEO was smiling and asking questions, which was a good sign. At four we were still discussing prices. Nobody was looking at their phones. For me, that was the real success of the day.

preguntas.q: What were the groups doing at eleven?
opciones: Writing ideas and drawing a journey

preguntas.q: What was the good sign at lunch?
opciones: The CEO was smiling and asking questions

preguntas.q: «Nobody was looking at their phones»: ¿por qué was y no were?
«At four we were still discussing prices»: ¿qué tipo de acción es?
opciones: Una acción en progreso a una hora concreta

ejercicios.explica: Un resumen de reunión usa mucho el pasado continuo para decir qué estaba pasando a cada hora (at 9:30, by eleven, at four). Nobody, everybody y the team llevan was; we, two groups llevan were.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta una anécdota: describe qué estaba pasando a tu alrededor (dónde estabas, qué estaban haciendo otras personas) justo antes de que pasara algo inesperado.

requisitos.texto: Usa was + -ing
Usa were + -ing con un sujeto plural (we, they, my friends…)
Usa when o while
Marca el giro con suddenly / then

ejercicios.ejemplo: Last December I was having dinner with my team at a restaurant in Usaquén. We were celebrating the end of the year. Andrés was telling a long story about a client, Camila was laughing and two designers were taking photos of the food. While the waiter was bringing the desserts, suddenly the music stopped and the lights went out. For a minute nobody moved. Then someone started singing happy birthday in the dark.
ejercicios.explica: El fondo de la anécdota va en continuo: I was having, we were celebrating, Andrés was telling. El hecho inesperado entra en simple: the music stopped, the lights went out.

ejercicios.consigna: Tu jefe te pregunta qué estaba haciendo el equipo ayer a las 3 p. m., cuando el cliente llamó y nadie contestó. Explica dónde estaba cada uno, qué estaban haciendo y qué no estaban haciendo.

requisitos.texto: Usa was / were + -ing
Incluye una negativa: wasn't / weren't + -ing
Menciona la hora (at 3, at 3 p.m.…)

ejercicios.ejemplo: I understand the problem, but nobody was ignoring the client. At 3 p.m. Camila and Andrés were presenting a proposal to another client in Chapinero. Sarah was editing a video with headphones on. Mike wasn't working; he was having a late lunch. And I was driving back from a shoot in Chía. I'm sorry. I'm calling the client myself right now.
ejercicios.explica: Para dar explicaciones sobre un momento concreto (at 3 p.m.) → was/were + -ing para cada persona. La negativa wasn't/weren't + -ing dice lo que no estaba pasando.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe el resumen de una reunión reciente para alguien que no fue: qué estaban discutiendo cuando llegaste, qué estaba haciendo el cliente y termina con una pregunta con Was / Were.

requisitos.texto: Usa was / were + -ing
Usa when
Haz una pregunta con was / were + sujeto + -ing

ejercicios.ejemplo: When I arrived at the meeting, the client and Laura were discussing the budget. The client was looking at the numbers and shaking his head. Mike was taking notes, and Sarah was showing the media plan on the screen. After twenty minutes, they agreed on a smaller budget for the first month. One thing I didn't understand: were you working on a new version of the plan last night?
ejercicios.explica: Al llegar a una reunión ya empezada, lo que estaba pasando va en continuo (were discussing, was looking, was taking notes). Pregunta: were you working…? — were delante del sujeto y el verbo con -ing.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el pasado simple. Casi todos los verbos son irregulares: no llevan -ed.
ejercicios.texto: Last Monday was a disaster. I {1} (wake) up late because my phone {2} (die) during the night. I {3} (take) a quick shower, {4} (put) on the first shirt I {5} (find) and {6} (run) to the corner. Of course, there {7} (be) no taxis. I {8} (get) to the office at ten, sweaty and angry, and the meeting was already over. My boss just looked at me and smiled.
ejercicios.explica: Una secuencia de acciones terminadas → pasado simple. Irregulares: wake → woke, take → took, put → put, find → found, run → ran, get → got. There + plural → there were.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa la conversación. En preguntas y negativas aparece did y el verbo vuelve a la base.
ejercicios.texto: Monday morning, in the kitchen. Camila: 'Hey! What {1} (you / do) on the weekend?' Me: 'Not much. I {2} (not / go) out on Saturday because I was tired. On Sunday we {3} (visit) my girlfriend's parents in Chía.' Camila: '{4} (you / eat) a lot?' Me: 'Too much! Gloria {5} (cook) for ten people again.' Camila: 'And {6} (you / see) the game?' Me: 'No, I {7} (not / see) it. Who {8} (win)?'
ejercicios.explica: Did se lleva la marca de pasado: did you do, didn't go, did you see (nunca did you saw). En la afirmativa did se esconde y deja su marca: visited, cooked. Con who como sujeto no hay did: Who won?

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Recuerda: una sola marca de pasado por frase.
ejercicios.texto: Last year we {1} for a big account. We {2} three weeks on the idea and we {3} a beautiful film. On the day of the pitch, the client {4} once. They {5} questions about the budget and they {6} our film twice. Two days later, they {7} us with the news: we didn't win. Why {8} we lose? The price. Another agency was cheaper. We still talk about that film.
ejercicios.explica: La marca de pasado aparece una sola vez: o en el verbo (spent, made, asked) o en did (didn't smile, Why did we lose?). Did + verbo con -ed es doble marca: did watched es un error.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el pasado simple. Ojo: be va con was / were y no usa did.
ejercicios.texto: In March I {1} (be) in Cartagena for a shoot. The weather {2} (be) terrible: it {3} (rain) for three days. The actors {4} (not / be) happy, and the director {5} (not / want) to shoot in the rain. On the fourth day the sun {6} (come) out and we {7} (finish) everything in one afternoon. {8} (it / be) stressful? Yes. But the final video looks great. We celebrated with fried fish on the beach that night.
ejercicios.explica: Be tiene su propia llave: was/were, wasn't/weren't, Was it…? Los demás verbos usan did: didn't want. Afirmativa: rained, finished (regulares) y came (irregular).

ejercicios.texto: I met my girlfriend five years ago at a friend's birthday party in Chapinero. I almost didn't go because I felt tired after a long week. I arrived late, around eleven, and I didn't know anybody except my friend. Then she came into the kitchen and asked me for a glass of water. We started talking about music and we didn't stop for three hours. I took her phone number, but I didn't call her the next day. I sent her a message two days later. She replied with one word: 'Finally.'

preguntas.q: Why did he almost stay home?
What did she ask him for?
«I didn't know anybody»: ¿por qué know y no knew?
opciones: Porque didn't ya lleva el pasado y el verbo vuelve a la base

preguntas.q: «She replied»: replied es…

ejercicios.explica: Una historia terminada se cuenta en pasado simple: met, felt, arrived, came, took, sent. Con didn't el verbo vuelve a la base (didn't know, didn't call). Reply → replied: la y pasa a i.

ejercicios.texto: My first job was at a small agency in Medellín. I was twenty-two and I didn't have any experience. On my first day, my boss gave me a brief for a supermarket and said: 'You have until five.' I didn't understand half of the words in the brief, but I didn't ask any questions because I felt embarrassed. I wrote three ideas and presented them at five. My boss read them in silence. Then he said: 'The third one is good. Did you write it alone?' I said yes. It was the first idea I ever sold.

preguntas.q: How old was he?
Why didn't he ask questions?
«Did you write it alone?»: ¿por qué write y no wrote?
opciones: Porque did ya lleva la marca de pasado

preguntas.q: ¿Cuál es el pasado de give en el texto?

ejercicios.explica: Hechos terminados → pasado simple (gave, said, wrote, read). En la pregunta y la negativa did sale a la luz y el verbo queda en base: Did you write…?, I didn't understand.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta qué hiciste el fin de semana pasado: al menos tres acciones en orden, algo que no hiciste y una pregunta para tu interlocutor.

requisitos.texto: Usa un verbo irregular en pasado (went, had, saw, slept…)
Ordena con first / then / after that / finally
Incluye una negativa con didn't + verbo base
Haz una pregunta con did you…?

ejercicios.ejemplo: Last weekend was quiet. On Saturday I slept until nine, then I went to the gym and after that I had lunch with my girlfriend in Usaquén. In the afternoon we watched a movie at home. On Sunday we drove to Chía and ate at her parents' house. I didn't work at all, and I didn't check my email once. What did you do on the weekend?
ejercicios.explica: Narrar el fin de semana es una cadena de pasados simples: slept, went, had, watched, drove, ate. Negativa: didn't + base (didn't work, didn't check). Pregunta: What did you do…?

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta la última presentación importante que hiciste a un cliente: cuándo fue, qué pasó, qué dijo el cliente y cómo terminó.

requisitos.texto: Di cuándo fue (yesterday, last week, two weeks ago…)
Cuenta lo que dijo el cliente con said o told
Usa was o were
Usa un verbo irregular en pasado

ejercicios.ejemplo: Two weeks ago we presented a new campaign to the bank. The meeting was at their office and there were eight people in the room. Laura showed the storyboard and I explained the media plan. At first the client didn't say anything, and I felt nervous. Then the marketing director smiled and said: 'This is exactly what we needed.' We left the building at noon and celebrated with a big lunch.
ejercicios.explica: Hechos terminados con un momento claro (two weeks ago) → pasado simple. Be usa was/were; say → said, feel → felt, leave → left. La negativa con did: didn't say.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa la presentación. Con be no hay llave extra (I'm, Are you…?); con los demás verbos, presente simple. La preposición de in charge … es fija.
ejercicios.texto: Hi everyone, {1} (I / be) Jonathan. {2} (I / work) as an account director at Brava, an advertising agency in Bogotá. {3} (I / be) in charge {4} (preposición) the digital team, and {5} (there / be) eight of us on my team. We {6} (help) brands grow on social media and in search. My colleague Laura {7} (lead) the creative side, and she's here with me today. And you, Sarah? {8} (you / be) based in Miami? — Yes, but I travel to Bogotá every month.
ejercicios.explica: Nombre y cargo con be (I'm Jonathan, I'm in charge of); trabajo con work as. Cuántos son: there are eight of us (no «we are eight»). Laura leads: -s de he/she. Pregunta con be: Are you based…?, sin do.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Son los dos minutos de charla antes de empezar una llamada con un cliente.
ejercicios.texto: — Hi Mike! How {1} your weekend? — It {2} great, thanks. I went to the beach with my kids. And you? — Pretty quiet. I {3} 38 now, so I need more rest! — Ha! By the way, where {4} you based? Bogotá? — Yes, I live {5} Bogotá and I work {6} Brava, near the park. — Nice. What exactly {7}? — I'm responsible {8} our clients in the U.S., so I talk to people like you every day.
ejercicios.explica: El fin de semana va en pasado: How was…? It was… La edad con be: I'm 38. Based va con be: Where are you based? La ciudad con in, la empresa con at. What do you do? pregunta el trabajo. Responsible for, no of.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el presente simple del verbo. Brava, our team y cada persona son he/she/it: llevan -s en afirmativa y does / doesn't en preguntas y negativas.
ejercicios.texto: Brava {1} (be) an independent agency with sixty people in Bogotá and Medellín. We {2} (work) with brands in food, banking and retail. Our team {3} (create) campaigns for social media, and our data area {4} (measure) the results every week. Camila {5} (manage) the community team, and Andrés {6} (not / work) on Fridays because he teaches at a university. Tell me about you: {7} (your company / have) an in-house team, or {8} (you / work) only with agencies?
ejercicios.explica: Para presentar la agencia: Brava is, our team creates, Camila manages (-s con he/she/it). Negativa con doesn't + verbo base (doesn't work). Preguntas con does / do delante: Does your company have…? Do you work…?

ejercicios.texto: Last month I had a kickoff call with a new client in Mexico City. I was nervous, so I prepared my introduction the night before. 'Hi, I'm Jonathan. I'm the account director at Brava. I'm in charge of the digital team, and there are eight of us. We help brands grow on social media.' Then I asked questions: 'Where are you based? How long have you worked on the brand?' The client, Mariana, was very friendly. She asked me, 'How's the weather in Bogotá?' 'Cold and rainy, as always,' I said, and everybody laughed. After five minutes, I didn't feel nervous anymore.

preguntas.q: Why did he prepare his introduction?
How many people are on his team?
«I'm in charge of the digital team»: ¿cuál es la preposición fija?
¿Cuál de estas frases NO es natural en inglés?

ejercicios.explica: Una presentación de trabajo son piezas fijas: I'm + nombre / cargo, I'm in charge of…, There are eight of us, We help brands + verbo. Y el small talk abre la puerta: Where are you based? How's the weather?

ejercicios.texto: Sarah Collins is the marketing manager of a coffee brand in Miami. She's 41 and she's originally from Chicago, but she lives in Florida now. She works with three agencies: one in New York, one in São Paulo and Brava in Bogotá. She's responsible for the brand in Latin America, so she travels a lot. Every month she visits Bogotá for two days. She doesn't speak much Spanish, but she understands it. In meetings, she likes short presentations and clear numbers. On Fridays she doesn't take calls after 3 p.m. because she picks up her kids from school.

preguntas.q: Where does Sarah live?
Why doesn't she take calls on Friday afternoons?
opciones: She has meetings with New York

preguntas.q: «She's 41»: ¿por qué no se dice «She has 41 years»?
opciones: Porque la edad va con be en inglés

preguntas.q: «She doesn't speak much Spanish»: ¿por qué speak no lleva -s?
opciones: Porque doesn't ya lleva la marca de he/she

ejercicios.explica: Para describir a alguien: be para edad, origen y cargo (She's 41, she's responsible for…) y presente simple con -s para lo que hace (works, travels, likes). Con doesn't, el verbo vuelve a la base.

ejercicios.consigna: Vas a tener la primera reunión con una clienta nueva. Escríbele un email corto para presentarte: quién eres, tu cargo, de qué te encargas, tu equipo, y termina con una pregunta.

requisitos.texto: Di quién eres con I'm + nombre o cargo
Explica tu responsabilidad con in charge of / responsible for
Habla de tu equipo: I lead a team of… / There are … of us
requisitos.patron: \b(lead|manage) a team of\b|\bthere are \w+ of us\b

requisitos.texto: Haz una pregunta con do / does / are / is

ejercicios.ejemplo: Dear Ms. Collins, I'm Jonathan, the account director at Brava, and I'm writing to introduce myself before our meeting on Monday. I'm in charge of the digital team, and I lead a team of eight people in Bogotá. We help food and retail brands grow on social media and in search. Do you prefer to start with a short presentation or with your questions? Looking forward to meeting you. Best regards, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Presentarte es armar piezas: I'm + cargo, I'm in charge of / responsible for (preposición fija), I lead a team of… y una pregunta con do o be para abrir la conversación. Nunca «I am work» ni «responsible of».

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el presente continuo (am / is / are + -ing). Todo pasa ahora o en estos días.
ejercicios.texto: This week is crazy at Brava. We {1} (prepare) a pitch for a new airline client, so nobody {2} (go) home before nine. Right now, Laura {3} (sketch) ideas on the whiteboard and two designers {4} (test) different logos. I {5} (not / sleep) much these days, and my girlfriend {6} (complain) about it. She says I {7} (live) at the office this month. She's right, but it's only for two more weeks.
ejercicios.explica: Lo que pasa ahora (right now) o en este periodo (this week, these days, this month) → am/is/are + -ing. Nobody funciona como singular: nobody is going. En la negativa, el not va pegado a la llave: I'm not sleeping.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Ojo: los verbos de estado (understand, agree, see como «ver», know) no van en -ing aunque sea ahora.
ejercicios.texto: Sorry, can you hear me? I {1} from home today because the building {2} the elevator, and it's really noisy. Right now a man {3} the wall next to my apartment. I {4} what you mean about the budget, and I {5} with you: we need more money for video. Can you share your screen? I {6} it yet. OK, now I {7} it. Wait a second, my dog {8} at the door.
ejercicios.explica: Acciones en progreso (working, repairing, drilling, barking) → be + -ing. Understand, agree y see (percibir) son verbos de estado: van en simple aunque hables de este momento (I understand, I don't see it, now I see it).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa las preguntas y frases en presente continuo. En la pregunta, am / is / are va delante del sujeto.
ejercicios.texto: Hi, Dad! No, I'm not busy. Well, a little. What {1} (you / do)? {2} (you / listen) to the radio again? I can hear it from here. Me? I {3} (walk) to a meeting near the park. Why {4} (you / call) so early? Oh, {5} (my aunt / visit) you this week? That's great. {6} (she / stay) at your house? OK, I have to go. The client {7} (wait) for me at the door. Love you!
ejercicios.explica: Pregunta en continuo: (Wh-) + am/is/are + sujeto + -ing: What are you doing?, Is she staying? Nunca do/does: What do you doing es imposible. La llave be cambia con el sujeto: are you, is my aunt.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el presente continuo. Aquí habla de planes ya organizados, con día, hora o personas.
ejercicios.texto: Our Friday is full. In the morning we {1} (meet) the bank team at their office in Chapinero. After that, Andrés and I {2} (have) lunch with a production company. At four, the client {3} (visit) Brava to see the first edits. I {4} (not / go) to the gym that day, obviously. In the evening my girlfriend and I {5} (fly) to Santa Marta for a long weekend. {6} (you / do) anything special this weekend? We {7} (come) back on Monday night.
ejercicios.explica: Planes con fecha y ya acordados con otras personas → presente continuo, aunque sean futuros: We're meeting the bank team on Friday. Es la agenda: algo ya está reservado o confirmado.

ejercicios.texto: It's eleven in the morning and the office is busy. Andrés is standing in front of a big screen and he's showing the new storyboard to three designers. They aren't saying much; they're taking notes. In the kitchen, Mike is making coffee and talking on the phone with a client in Miami. Laura isn't here today because she's working from home. Next to the window, two interns are eating empanadas and laughing at something on a laptop. And me? I'm writing this short note while I wait for a call. The call is late, as always.

preguntas.q: What is Andrés doing?
Why isn't Laura in the office?
«They aren't saying much»: ¿cuál es la llave de esta negativa?
«Mike is making coffee and talking on the phone»: ¿por qué talking no lleva su propio is?
opciones: Porque el is de making sirve para los dos verbos

ejercicios.explica: Describir lo que pasa ahora mismo → am/is/are + -ing. Cuando el mismo sujeto hace dos cosas, la llave se dice una vez: Mike is making coffee and talking on the phone.

ejercicios.texto: My routine is different this month. Usually I drive to work, but my car is at the mechanic, so I'm taking the bus. I'm also getting up earlier because the bus is slow. My girlfriend is traveling for work; she's visiting clients in Lima and Quito, so I'm cooking for myself. I don't like cooking, but I'm learning. This week I'm trying a new recipe every night. The pasta last night was terrible, but tonight's soup smells good. I think I'm getting better. I want my girlfriend to come back soon, and my car too.

preguntas.q: How does he usually go to work?
Where is his girlfriend this month?
«I don't like cooking, but I'm learning»: ¿por qué like va en simple?
opciones: Porque like es un verbo de estado
Porque es un hábito de esta semana

preguntas.q: «I'm taking the bus»: ¿qué idea expresa aquí?
opciones: Una situación temporal de este mes

ejercicios.explica: Lo temporal (this month, this week) va en continuo: I'm taking the bus, I'm cooking. Los gustos y opiniones (like, want, think) son verbos de estado y se quedan en simple.

ejercicios.consigna: Estás en una videollamada y alguien te pregunta qué está pasando en la oficina (o en tu casa) ahora mismo. Describe a tres personas y lo que están haciendo, y di algo que no está pasando.

requisitos.texto: Usa am / is / are + -ing
Incluye una negativa en continuo (isn't / aren't / I'm not + -ing)
Usa un marcador de ahora (right now, at the moment, today…)

ejercicios.ejemplo: Right now I'm sitting in the meeting room on the third floor. Through the glass I can see the team. Camila is answering emails and drinking a huge coffee. Andrés and two designers are standing around a laptop; they're choosing the photos for the bank campaign. Mike is talking on the phone with a client, and he's walking in circles, as always. The interns aren't working at the moment; they're having a break on the terrace.
ejercicios.explica: Una descripción en vivo es presente continuo de principio a fin: is answering, are standing, 're choosing. La llave be concuerda con el sujeto (Camila is, the interns are) y la negativa es isn't/aren't + -ing.

ejercicios.consigna: Escríbele a un colega para coordinar la semana: cuéntale qué tienes ya organizado (con día, hora o personas) y pregúntale qué está haciendo él el jueves.

requisitos.texto: Usa presente continuo con un día o una hora (on Monday, tomorrow, at 3…)
Haz una pregunta con are / is + sujeto + -ing
Menciona una hora (at 10, at 3:30…)

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Mike, quick update on my week. On Monday at 9 I'm meeting the bank team to review the brief. On Tuesday I'm working from home in the morning, and in the afternoon I'm having lunch with the production company. On Wednesday we're presenting the new storyboard at 3:30. What are you doing on Thursday? I need two hours with you to plan the pitch.
ejercicios.explica: Una agenda con citas confirmadas se cuenta en presente continuo: I'm meeting, we're presenting. La pregunta por los planes de otro también: What are you doing on Thursday?

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el presente perfecto (have / has + participio). Ojo con ever, never y yet.
ejercicios.texto: I {1} (study) English on and off since college, but this year is different. I {2} (download) a new app and I {3} (practice) almost every day for three months. My girlfriend {4} (notice) the change; she says my pronunciation is better. I {5} (not / watch) a full movie without subtitles yet, but I {6} (start) to understand podcasts. {7} (you / ever / try) to learn a language as an adult? It's hard, but I {8} (never / enjoy) it so much.
ejercicios.explica: Lo que empezó antes y sigue (since college, for three months) y lo que pasó en un periodo que no ha terminado (this year) → have/has + participio. My girlfriend → has. Ever, never y yet acompañan al presente perfecto: Have you ever tried…?, I've never enjoyed, haven't watched… yet.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Fíjate en las palabras clave: ago, yet, just, since.
ejercicios.texto: Laura: '{1} you sent the invoice to the bank?' Me: 'Yes, I {2} it an hour ago.' Laura: 'Great. And has the client approved the budget {3}?' Me: 'No, not yet. But Mike {4} spoken with their finance director this morning, and he says it looks good.' Laura: 'Perfect. Have you {5} the new contract?' Me: 'I've {6} finished it. Two minutes ago!' Laura: 'Then let's call them. They've been in the office {7} ten o'clock.'
ejercicios.explica: Have you sent…? pregunta por un resultado de ahora; an hour ago es un momento terminado → pasado simple (I sent it). Yet en preguntas y negativas; just = hace un momento. Mike → has spoken. Read → read (participio). Since + punto de inicio (ten o'clock).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el presente perfecto. Mira el sujeto para elegir have o has.
ejercicios.texto: Brava {1} (work) with the bank since 2019. In that time we {2} (make) more than forty campaigns for them and we {3} (win) two awards together. Their marketing director, Patricia, {4} (be) our main contact for three years. She {5} (not / miss) a single launch event. Recently, the bank {6} (open) offices in Peru, and they {7} (ask) us to help with the launch there. We {8} (not / say) yes yet.
ejercicios.explica: Brava, Patricia, the bank → has; we, they → have. Participios irregulares: make → made, win → won, be → been, say → said. Since 2019 y for three years marcan algo que empezó antes y sigue hoy.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige entre presente perfecto (experiencia sin fecha, hasta hoy) y pasado simple (momento terminado).
ejercicios.texto: I {1} to Mexico City four times. The first time {2} in 2015, for a design festival. I {3} the food so much that I gained three kilos. Since then, I {4} back for work three more times. Last year I {5} a client there and we {6} to a lucha libre fight. I {7} a better night in my life. I hope I can go back next year.
ejercicios.explica: Experiencia total hasta hoy (four times, since then, never in my life) → presente perfecto. Un momento concreto y terminado (in 2015, last year) → pasado simple: was, loved, visited, went. Una sola negación: I've never had.

ejercicios.texto: My dad sent me a long message this morning. 'Son, I have some news. I've bought a smartphone. Don't laugh. Your aunt has shown me how to use it, and I've already sent three photos to the family group. I haven't learned how to make video calls yet, but I've practiced with the camera a lot. I've taken forty photos of my plants! I've also downloaded an app for the radio. Have you seen my photos? Please answer. I've checked my phone ten times since breakfast.' I laughed for five minutes, and then I called him.

preguntas.q: What has his dad bought?
What hasn't his dad learned yet?
«I've already sent three photos»: ¿qué indica already?
opciones: Que ya pasó, quizá antes de lo esperado

preguntas.q: «Your aunt has shown me»: ¿qué forma es shown?

ejercicios.explica: Novedades que importan ahora → have/has + participio (I've bought, has shown, I've taken). Already y yet: lo que ya pasó y lo que todavía no. Pero this morning y for five minutes con un momento terminado → pasado simple: sent, laughed, called.

ejercicios.texto: Interviewer: So, tell me about your experience. Candidate: Well, I've worked in advertising for eight years. I've managed accounts for banks, airlines and food brands. Interviewer: Have you ever led a team? Candidate: Yes. I've led a team of six people since last year. Interviewer: And have you ever lost a client? Candidate: Once. In 2020 a client left us after a bad launch. I learned a lot from that. Since then, I've always checked every detail twice. Interviewer: Have you used any AI tools in your work? Candidate: Yes, I've used them a lot this year, mostly for research.

preguntas.q: How long has the candidate worked in advertising?
When did he lose a client?
«In 2020 a client left us»: ¿por qué pasado simple?
opciones: Porque es una experiencia sin fecha

preguntas.q: «I've led a team of six people since last year»: ¿qué significa?
opciones: Empezó el año pasado y sigue liderándolo

ejercicios.explica: En una entrevista, la trayectoria hasta hoy va en presente perfecto (I've worked, I've managed, Have you ever led…?). Si das la fecha (in 2020), cambias a pasado simple: a client left us.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe tu bio profesional para la página web de la agencia: cuánto tiempo llevas en la publicidad (for / since), qué has logrado y una experiencia que todavía no has tenido.

requisitos.texto: Usa have / has + participio
Di cuánto tiempo con for o since
Incluye yet o never

ejercicios.ejemplo: Jonathan is an account director at Brava. He has worked in advertising for twelve years and he has been at Brava since 2019. In that time he has led campaigns for banks, food brands and universities, and his team has won three local awards. He has always loved working with creative people. He hasn't run a campaign outside Latin America yet, but it's on his list.
ejercicios.explica: Una bio cuenta la trayectoria hasta hoy → has + participio (has worked, has been, has led, has won). For + periodo, since + punto de inicio. Lo pendiente: hasn't run… yet.

ejercicios.consigna: Escríbele a un amigo que no ves hace tiempo y cuéntale qué ha cambiado en tu vida este año (trabajo, casa, hábitos). Hazle una pregunta con Have you…?

requisitos.texto: Usa have / has + participio
Haz una pregunta con have you…?
Usa this year, recently o lately

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Felipe! It's been a long time. A lot has changed this year. I've moved to a bigger apartment in Chapinero, and my girlfriend has started a new job. At work, I've taken a new role: now I lead the digital team. I've also started running in the mornings. Have you finished your documentary in the Amazon? Let's have a beer soon!
ejercicios.explica: Novedades de un periodo que sigue abierto (this year) → presente perfecto: I've moved, she has started, I've taken. La pregunta: Have you finished…? Have delante del sujeto y el participio después.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el presente simple del verbo entre paréntesis. Fíjate en quién es el sujeto: he/she/it lleva -s en afirmativa.
ejercicios.texto: My alarm {1} (go) off at 5:45, but I never {2} (get) up before six. My girlfriend {3} (not / drink) coffee, so I make a cup only for me. We {4} (leave) the apartment together at seven because she {5} (work) near my office. On the way, we usually {6} (listen) to a podcast. {7} (you / know) the funny thing? She {8} (fall) asleep in the taxi almost every morning, even for a fifteen-minute ride.
ejercicios.explica: Rutinas → presente simple. La -s solo aparece con he/she/it en afirmativa (goes, works, falls); con doesn't o Do you… el verbo vuelve a la base.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta en cada hueco. Es una presentación del equipo: hechos y rutinas, no cosas de ahora.
ejercicios.texto: Let me introduce the team. Camila {1} our social media accounts and {2} most of the client calls. Andrés {3} the design team; he {4} come to the office on Fridays because he works from home that day. Mike and Sarah {5} the copy for all our campaigns. And me? I {6} the account and I make sure the client {7} happy. The whole team starts at 8:30, but nobody leaves before seven.
ejercicios.explica: Lo que cada persona hace en su trabajo es un hecho general → presente simple. Camila, Andrés, the client → -s o doesn't; Mike and Sarah, I → sin -s. Be va solo: the client is happy.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa las preguntas y las negativas. Recuerda que la pregunta necesita la llave do/does delante del sujeto.
ejercicios.texto: Hi, Sarah! Welcome to Brava. Can I ask you a few things? Where {1} (you / live)? {2} (you / take) the bus or do you drive? What time {3} (the office / open) in your old agency? {4} (your husband / work) in advertising too? And one more: {5} (you / like) spicy food? We order Mexican every Friday, and the team {6} (not / accept) excuses. Oh, and the coffee machine {7} (not / work) after 4 pm. Nobody knows why.
ejercicios.explica: En preguntas y negativas la llave sale a la luz: do (you) / does (the office, your husband, the team, the machine) y el verbo queda en base. Sin la llave, en inglés no hay pregunta.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el presente simple. Casi todo el texto habla de he: cuidado con la -s y con doesn't.
ejercicios.texto: My dad is 68 and he {1} (live) in Manizales. He {2} (not / use) a smartphone; he {3} (say) it makes people stupid. Every morning he {4} (walk) to the market, {5} (buy) fresh bread and reads the newspaper on paper. He {6} (not / watch) TV, but he {7} (listen) to the radio all day. When I visit him, he always asks me the same question: 'Why {8} (you / check) your phone so often?'
ejercicios.explica: He → verbo + s (lives, says, walks, buys, listens). La frase solo tiene una -s: si aparece doesn't, el verbo la pierde (doesn't use). Con you la llave es do.

ejercicios.texto: Brava is a mid-size agency in Bogotá with about sixty people. The day starts early: the account team arrives at 8:30 and checks emails from clients in Mexico and Miami. The creative team doesn't come in before ten; they say ideas don't wake up early. Laura, the creative director, works from home on Mondays and Fridays, but she joins every status meeting by video. The agency has three big clients and a lot of small ones. The biggest client, a bank, sends a new brief almost every week. 'They don't sleep,' Laura jokes. Lunch is at one, and on Fridays nobody works after five.

preguntas.q: What time does the creative team arrive?
Where is Laura on Mondays?
¿Por qué dice «The creative team doesn't come in» y no «don't come in»?
opciones: Porque team es singular (it) y usa does/doesn't

preguntas.q: «Laura works from home on Mondays and Fridays»: ¿por qué presente simple?
opciones: Porque es un plan de futuro

ejercicios.explica: Rutinas y hechos de una empresa → presente simple. Sujetos singulares como the team, the agency o the client funcionan como it: llevan -s o doesn't.

ejercicios.texto: Every Sunday we have lunch at my girlfriend's parents' house in Chía. Her mom, Gloria, cooks for ten people even when we are only four. Her dad, don Hernán, doesn't eat before everyone sits down; it's his rule. He asks me the same question every week: 'Do you still work with that bank?' I always say yes, and he always says banks have too much money. After lunch, Gloria takes a nap and don Hernán watches soccer. My girlfriend and I wash the dishes because nobody else does. We leave at six, full and happy, and the traffic back to Bogotá takes two hours.

preguntas.q: How many people does Gloria cook for?
What does don Hernán do after lunch?
«…because nobody else does»: ¿qué reemplaza does aquí?
opciones: wash the dishes (la llave sustituye al verbo)

preguntas.q: «He asks me the same question every week»: ¿por qué asks lleva -s?
opciones: Porque el sujeto es he y es un hábito

ejercicios.explica: Un hábito de todos los domingos → presente simple. Con he/she la -s va en el verbo (cooks, asks, takes). La llave does puede sustituir a todo el verbo: nobody else does = nadie más los lava.

ejercicios.consigna: Presenta tu agencia y tu rol a un cliente nuevo: qué hace la agencia, qué haces tú, una cosa que tu equipo no hace y una pregunta para el cliente con do/does.

requisitos.texto: Usa un verbo con -s para he/she/it (the agency, my team, the client…)
Incluye una negativa con don't / doesn't
Haz una pregunta con Do / Does

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi, I'm Jonathan and I work at Brava, an advertising agency in Bogotá. We create digital campaigns for banks and consumer brands. I lead the account team: I talk to clients every day, I review the briefs and I make sure the creative team has what it needs. My team doesn't produce TV commercials; we focus on social media and web. Our creative director, Laura, designs the big ideas and the designers build the visuals. One question before we start: do you have a brand guide we can read?
ejercicios.explica: Presentarte y explicar lo que hace tu empresa es hablar de lo general → presente simple. I/we → verbo base; the agency, my team, Laura → -s; negativa con don't/doesn't; pregunta con Do/Does delante.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe la rutina de una persona cercana (tu pareja, un amigo, tu papá): qué hace entre semana, qué hace el fin de semana, qué no hace nunca y un gusto suyo.

requisitos.texto: Usa he/she + verbo con -s
Incluye una negativa con doesn't
Usa un adverbio o expresión de frecuencia
Menciona un gusto con likes / loves / hates / prefers

ejercicios.ejemplo: My girlfriend, Camila, is a nutritionist. She wakes up at 5:30 every day and goes to the gym before work. She sees patients from eight to four and she usually eats lunch at her desk. On weekends she sleeps late and cooks for both of us. She doesn't drink alcohol and she never eats fast food, which is a problem when I want a burger. She loves hiking, so once a month we drive to a mountain near Bogotá.
