ejercicios.explica: La rutina de otra persona es la prueba de fuego de la -s: she wakes, goes, sees, eats, sleeps, cooks, loves. Los adverbios de frecuencia van antes del verbo (she usually eats, she never eats) y la negativa es doesn't + base.

ejercicios.instruccion: Escribe el pronombre indefinido que traduce la pista. Some- en afirmativa, any- en negativa y pregunta, no- con verbo afirmativo, every- para todos (con verbo en singular).
ejercicios.texto: Monday, 9 a.m. {1} (alguien) left a message for me: the client wants to talk about the budget. I asked the team, but {2} (nadie) knew the details. 'Did {3} (alguien) see the new numbers?' I asked. No answer. I looked {4} (en todas partes) for the file: my email, the shared drive, my desk. Finally, Camila said: 'I have {5} (algo) important to tell you. The file is in the old folder.' {6} (todos) was relieved. Before the call, I asked: 'Is there {7} (algo más) we need?' 'No, {8} (todo) is ready,' she said.
ejercicios.explica: Afirmativa → some- (Someone left a message, something important). Pregunta → any- (Did anyone see…? Is there anything else?). Nobody ya es negativo, el verbo va en afirmativa (nobody knew). Every- va con singular: Everyone was, everything is.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Es una llamada rápida antes de enviar una presentación al cliente. Recuerda: en inglés no hay doble negación.
ejercicios.texto: — Hi Sarah, can you hear me? — Yes. Is {1} else joining us? — Andrés, but he's late. — OK. Did you send {2} to the client yesterday? — No, I didn't send {3}. I was waiting for your OK. — Fine. {4} on our team likes the new idea, so let's send it today. — Great. Is there {5} I should change before I send it? — Just one thing: {6} wrote the wrong date on slide 4. — Oh no. Was it me? — It doesn't matter. {7} makes mistakes. — Thanks. I'll fix it now. I don't need {8} else.
ejercicios.explica: Preguntas → any- (Is anyone else…? Did you send anything?). Negativa con didn't / don't → any- (I didn't send anything, I don't need anything else), nunca nothing. Everyone / everybody + verbo en singular (likes, makes).

ejercicios.instruccion: Escribe el pronombre indefinido que traduce la pista. Las terminaciones dicen de qué hablas: -one / -body personas, -thing cosas, -where lugares.
ejercicios.texto: We want to take the team {1} (a algún sitio) special for the end-of-year dinner. Laura says there's {2} (nada) good near the office, but I don't agree. 'Does {3} (alguien) know a place with a private room?' I asked in the group chat. {4} (nadie) answered for two hours. Then Mike wrote: 'I know {5} (alguien) who works at a great restaurant in Usaquén.' The problem: they don't have {6} (nada) available on Friday. So we're going {7} (a otro sitio). {8} (todo el mundo) wants Italian food, so it's an easy choice.
ejercicios.explica: Lugares → -where (somewhere special, somewhere else; el adjetivo y else van detrás). There's nothing: no- con verbo afirmativo. They don't have anything: verbo negativo + any-. Everyone wants: singular.

ejercicios.texto: Last Thursday I arrived at the meeting room at 10, but nobody was there. I checked my calendar: everything looked correct. I called Laura, but she didn't answer. I sent a message to the group: 'Is anyone coming to the 10 o'clock?' Someone replied after five minutes: 'The meeting is online today. Didn't anyone tell you?' No, no one told me anything. I ran to my desk and joined the call. Everyone was there, including the client. 'Is everything OK, Jonathan?' she asked. 'Yes, everything's fine. Sorry, I was somewhere else,' I said. Nobody laughed, but it was funny.

preguntas.q: Why was nobody in the meeting room?
Who replied to his message?
«No one told me anything»: ¿por qué anything y no nothing?
opciones: Porque no one ya es negativo: en inglés no hay doble negación

preguntas.q: «Everyone was there»: ¿por qué was y no were?
opciones: Porque everyone va con verbo en singular
Porque es el pasado de be con plural

ejercicios.explica: Nobody was / no one told me anything: una sola negación. Is anyone…? / Didn't anyone…?: any- en preguntas. Everyone was / everything looked: every- con verbo en singular. Somewhere else: else va detrás.

ejercicios.texto: This weekend my girlfriend and I did nothing special, and it was perfect. On Saturday we didn't go anywhere. We stayed home, cooked something easy and watched a series. Nobody called me from work, and I didn't check anything on my phone. On Sunday my mom invited us to lunch at her new apartment. Everything was delicious. 'Does anyone want more?' she asked. Everybody said yes. In the afternoon someone knocked on the door: her neighbor, with a cake. My mom knows everyone in the building. Next weekend we want to go somewhere outside the city, maybe Guatavita.

preguntas.q: What did they do on Saturday?
Who knocked on the door?
«We didn't go anywhere»: ¿qué otra forma correcta hay de decirlo?
«cooked something easy»: ¿dónde va el adjetivo?

ejercicios.explica: Dos formas de negar, una sola marca: didn't go anywhere = went nowhere. Did nothing special / something easy: el adjetivo va detrás. Nobody called / everybody said: el pronombre es el sujeto.

ejercicios.consigna: Hubo un problema: nadie envió la presentación final al cliente y no encuentras el archivo. Escribe un mensaje a tu equipo explicando qué pasó y pidiendo ayuda.

requisitos.texto: Usa una palabra con some- (someone, something, somewhere)
Haz una pregunta con any- (Did anyone…? / Is there anything…?)
Usa no one / nobody / nothing con el verbo en afirmativa
Usa everyone / everything + verbo en singular

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi team, quick message about the presentation for tomorrow. Nobody sent the final version to the client yesterday, and they called me this morning. Did anyone save the file with the new numbers? I looked everywhere, but I found nothing. If someone has it, please send it to me before noon. Everyone is busy, I know, but this is important. Thanks, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Some- para afirmar (someone has it), any- para preguntar (Did anyone save…?), no- con verbo afirmativo (Nobody sent, I found nothing) y every- con verbo en singular (Everyone is busy).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa el diálogo de la reunión. Agree es un verbo (sin be), I'll + verbo base es la promesa del momento y la fecha límite va con by.
ejercicios.texto: — OK, let's get started. The client wants the campaign live by May 3. What do you think, Laura? — {1} (I / think) it's possible, but the budget is tight. — {2} (I / agree) with Laura. We need more time for the video. — Sorry to {3} (interrupt), but the client changed the date yesterday. It's April 26 now. — What do you {4} (mean) by 'changed'? Is it official? — Yes. So, {5} (why / not / we) ask for a smaller first phase? — Good idea. I {6} (will / write) to the client today. — And I {7} (will / send) the new timeline {8} (a más tardar) Friday.
ejercicios.explica: I think abre la opinión; I agree sin am. Sorry to interrupt, but… para entrar. What do you mean by…? para aclarar. Why don't we…? con don't antes de we. I'll + verbo base para comprometerte, y by Friday = a más tardar el viernes.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Es el final de una reunión de equipo: opinar, estar en desacuerdo con suavidad, aclarar, proponer y cerrar.
ejercicios.texto: — {1} the second route is the strongest. It's clear and simple. — I {2}. The client will understand it in five seconds. — I see your point, {3} I'm not sure the client will like the colors. — {4} by 'the colors'? The yellow? — Exactly. — {5} show both versions, one in yellow and one in blue? — Good idea. Laura, can you prepare them? — Sure. {6} the deck by Wednesday. — Perfect. {7}: Laura sends the deck, Andrés prepares the mockups, and {8} the client to confirm the meeting.
ejercicios.explica: In my opinion (no for my opinion). I agree, sin be. I see your point, but… What do you mean by…? Why don't we…? I'll send / I'll call para prometer (nunca will to). Para cerrar: To sum up, no in resume.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa el email de próximos pasos que se envía después de una reunión. Las promesas van con will + verbo base y las fechas límite con by.
ejercicios.texto: Hi all, thanks for the meeting today. {1} (para resumir), we agreed on three things. First, the launch moves to May 10. Second, the client {2} (agree, pasado) to a smaller first phase. Third, we need new mockups. Next steps: Laura {3} (will / send) the updated deck {4} (a más tardar) Wednesday. Andrés {5} (will / prepare) three mockups for the videos. I {6} (will / call) Sarah on Thursday to confirm the budget. If you {7} (no estar de acuerdo) with something, please tell me today. Let me know if you have any {8} (preguntas). Best, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: El email de próximos pasos es fórmula: To sum up → lo acordado (the client agreed) → quién + will + verbo base + by + fecha. No estar de acuerdo es don't agree o disagree, nunca «are not agree». Any questions, en plural.

ejercicios.titulo: The meeting where I spoke up
ejercicios.texto: For months, I stayed quiet in the Monday meeting with our client in Miami. I understood almost everything, but I didn't know how to enter the conversation. Last Monday I tried three phrases. When Mike said the budget was too high, I said, 'Sorry to interrupt, but can I just add something? I see your point, but the video is the most important part.' Then Sarah used the word 'scope' and I asked, 'What do you mean by scope?' At the end, I said, 'I'll send you a new proposal by Friday.' After the call, my boss sent me a message: 'Great job today.'

preguntas.q: Why did he stay quiet before?
opciones: He didn't know how to enter the conversation

preguntas.q: What did he promise?
«What do you mean by scope?»: ¿para qué sirve?
opciones: Para pedir que aclaren una palabra

preguntas.q: «I'll send you a new proposal by Friday»: ¿qué significa by?
opciones: Hasta el viernes, todo el tiempo

ejercicios.explica: Tres frases bastan para dejar de estar callado: Sorry to interrupt, but… (entrar), I see your point, but… (disentir), What do you mean by…? (aclarar). Y para cerrar, I'll + verbo + by + fecha.

ejercicios.texto: Kickoff notes, coffee campaign. Attendees: Sarah, Mike, Laura and Jonathan. Sarah opened the meeting and explained the goal: more sales in Colombia among people under 30. Mike thinks TikTok is the main channel. Laura agreed, but she suggested a test first: 'Why don't we try three videos before we spend the full budget?' Everybody agreed. Jonathan didn't agree with the timeline: 'I understand the urgency, but six weeks is too short for production.' Sarah said she'll check with her boss. Next steps: Laura will send three video ideas by Tuesday. Sarah will confirm the timeline by Friday. Jonathan will share the budget next Monday.

preguntas.q: Who suggested a test first?
What will Sarah do by Friday?
«Jonathan didn't agree with the timeline»: ¿cuál es el error típico del hispanohablante?
opciones: Jonathan wasn't agree with the timeline.

preguntas.q: «Why don't we try three videos…?»: ¿qué hace esta frase?

ejercicios.explica: Un acta tiene la misma estructura que la reunión: opiniones (thinks), acuerdo (agreed, nunca was agree), desacuerdo suave (I understand…, but…), propuesta (Why don't we…?) y próximos pasos con will + by.

ejercicios.consigna: Acabas de terminar una reunión con una clienta. Escríbele el email de próximos pasos: resume lo acordado, di quién hace qué y con qué fecha, e incluye tu propio compromiso.

requisitos.texto: Resume con To sum up o We agreed
Escribe Next steps
Comprométete con I'll / I will + verbo
Pon una fecha límite con by + día

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Sarah, thanks for your time today. To sum up, we agreed to launch the campaign on May 10 with a smaller first phase. Next steps: Laura will send the updated deck by Wednesday, and Andrés will prepare three mockups for the videos. I'll call you on Thursday to confirm the budget, and I will share the final timeline by Friday. Let me know if I missed anything. Best regards, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: El email de próximos pasos se arma con piezas: To sum up / We agreed para el resumen, Next steps para la lista, persona + will + verbo base para cada tarea y by + día para la fecha límite.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con it o there + el verbo entre paréntesis, en presente. It para clima, hora, tiempo y opiniones; there is / there are para decir que algo existe («hay»).
ejercicios.texto: {1} (it / be) Monday, and {2} (it / rain) again in Bogotá. I get to the office at eight, but {3} (there / be / not) any coffee in the kitchen, so I go to the café downstairs. {4} (there / be) a lot of people in the line, and {5} (it / take) fifteen minutes to get a cappuccino. At ten {6} (there / be) a meeting with a new client. {7} (there / be) three people on their team, and they all speak fast. {8} (it / be) important to start on time with them, so I run upstairs with my coffee.
ejercicios.explica: Ninguna frase en inglés va sin sujeto: el día, el clima, el tiempo que tarda algo y las opiniones van con it (It's Monday, it's raining, it takes, it's important to). Lo que existe va con there, y el be concuerda con lo que sigue: there's a meeting, there are three people.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Es un email para un cliente que viene de visita: «hay» se dice there is / there are, nunca has / have.
ejercicios.texto: Hi Mike, a few details for your visit on Thursday. Our office is in Chapinero. {1} about 20 minutes from your hotel by taxi. {2} a parking lot next to the building, but {3} many free spaces after nine, so come early. {4} a coffee shop on the first floor if you want breakfast. In the meeting room {5} two cameras and a big screen. Bring a jacket: {6} usually cold in the mornings here. — Thanks, Jonathan! {7} a place to print documents? — Yes, {8} a printer next to reception.
ejercicios.explica: Distancia y clima → it (It's 20 minutes, it's cold). Existencia → there + be: there's a parking lot, there aren't many spaces (plural), Is there a place…? en pregunta. «Hay» nunca es has ni have.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa en pasado con it o there + be (o el verbo entre paréntesis). There was + singular, there were + plural; en pregunta, Was there / Were there.
ejercicios.texto: Last Friday we had the launch event for a new coffee brand. {1} (it / be) a long day. In the morning {2} (there / be) a problem with the sound system, and {3} (there / be / not) enough chairs for the guests. {4} (there / be) more than two hundred people at seven! Then {5} (it / start) to rain, so we moved everything inside. {6} (there / be) any problems with the food? No, the food was perfect. At the end, the client said: '{7} (it / be) the best event of the year.' The next day {8} (there / be) a lot of photos on social media.
ejercicios.explica: En pasado el be de there concuerda con lo que viene detrás: there was a problem (uno), there weren't enough chairs / there were two hundred people / Were there any problems? (plural). El clima y las valoraciones siguen llevando it: it started to rain, it was a long day.

ejercicios.texto: Brava is moving to a new office in Chapinero next month. It's a big change for the team. In the old office, there was only one meeting room, and there were always problems with the internet. In the new one, there are four meeting rooms and there's a terrace with a view of the mountains. It's ten minutes from my apartment, so I can walk to work. There's one problem, though: there isn't a parking lot, and it's difficult to find parking on the street. Laura is happy because there's a gym on the first floor. Andrés is not so happy. 'It's far from my house,' he says. 'It takes me an hour by bus.'

preguntas.q: How many meeting rooms are there in the new office?
What is the problem with the new office?
«It takes me an hour by bus»: ¿por qué empieza con It?
opciones: Porque toda frase en inglés necesita sujeto, aunque en español no lo haya

preguntas.q: «there were always problems»: ¿por qué were y no was?

ejercicios.explica: El texto alterna los dos sujetos vacíos: there + be para lo que existe (there was one room, there were problems, there isn't a parking lot) e it para distancia, tiempo y opiniones (It's ten minutes, it takes me an hour, it's difficult to…).

ejercicios.texto: Every Monday I have a call with Sarah, our client in Miami. We always start with the weather. 'How's the weather in Bogotá?' she asks. 'It's cold and it's raining, as usual,' I say. 'In Miami it's hot. It's 32 degrees today!' Then we talk about work. This week there are two problems with the campaign: there isn't enough budget for the video, and there are only three weeks before the launch. 'Is there a way to make a shorter video?' Sarah asks. 'Yes, there is. It's possible to use the photos from the shoot,' I answer. It's a good solution, and she likes it. Before we finish, she says, 'It was nice to talk to you, Jonathan.'

preguntas.q: What's the weather like in Bogotá?
How many problems are there with the campaign?
«Is there a way to make a shorter video?»: ¿cómo se forma la pregunta con there?
opciones: Is / Are pasa delante de there

preguntas.q: «It's possible to use the photos»: ¿qué hace it aquí?
opciones: Es el sujeto de una opinión impersonal (It's + adjetivo + to)

ejercicios.explica: Clima, temperatura y opiniones → it (It's cold, It's 32 degrees, It's possible to…). Existencia → there is / there are, y en pregunta el be va primero: Is there a way…? Yes, there is.

ejercicios.consigna: Un cliente de Estados Unidos viene a Bogotá la semana próxima. Escríbele un email corto para describirle el clima, la distancia del hotel a la oficina y lo que hay (y no hay) cerca, y hazle una pregunta.

requisitos.texto: Usa It's / It is para el clima o la distancia
Di lo que hay con There is / There are
Usa una negativa: there isn't / there aren't
Haz una pregunta con Is there…? / Are there…?

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Mike, welcome to Bogotá next week! It's usually cold in the mornings, so bring a jacket. Our office is in Chapinero, and it's about 20 minutes from your hotel by taxi. There are two good restaurants on our street, and there's a coffee shop on the first floor. There isn't a parking lot, though, so a taxi is the best option. Is there anything special you would like to do on Friday? Best, Jonathan
ejercicios.explica: Para describir un lugar en inglés necesitas los dos sujetos vacíos: it para clima y distancia (It's cold, it's 20 minutes) y there + be para lo que existe, con el be concordando (there's a coffee shop, there are two restaurants, Is there…?).

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con used to / didn't use to / Did … use to + verbo base. Habla de hábitos que ya no existen.
ejercicios.texto: When I was a kid, life was slower. I {1} (walk) to school with my cousins, and we {2} (stop) at the bakery every morning for pandebono. My mom {3} (not / let) us watch TV during the week. On Sundays my dad {4} (take) us to see his favorite soccer team. {5} (you / have) a nickname at school? I did. My friends {6} (call) me 'el Flaco' because I {7} (be) very thin. Now nobody calls me that.
ejercicios.explica: Hábitos y estados del pasado que ya no son así → used to + base (used to walk, used to be). Con did, used pierde la -d: didn't use to let, Did you use to have?

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta. Ojo con la -d de used y con los hechos de una sola vez (esos van en pasado simple).
ejercicios.texto: Ten years ago, Brava {1} a tiny office in Chapinero with eight people. We {2} everything on paper, and the clients {3} to the office for every presentation. We {4} social media at all. Now we have sixty people and most clients prefer video calls. Last month we {5} our tenth anniversary with a big party. Some people miss the old office. I don't: the old office {6} have air conditioning, and summers were terrible.
ejercicios.explica: Afirmativa: used to + base (used to have, used to print). Negativa: didn't use to (sin -d). Un hecho de una sola vez, con fecha (last month), no es hábito: celebrated.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa la entrevista con used to en afirmativa, negativa o pregunta.
ejercicios.texto: For a school project, my niece interviewed my dad about his youth. 'Grandpa, what {1} (you / do) on Saturday nights?' 'We {2} (go) dancing at a place near the main square.' '{3} (you / have) a car?' 'No, I {4} (not / have) a car. I {5} (ride) a motorcycle.' 'And {6} (Grandma / like) the motorcycle?' 'No, she {7} (hate) it. She {8} (say) it was dangerous.'
ejercicios.explica: Pregunta: (Wh-) + did + sujeto + use to + base: what did you use to do?, did Grandma use to like…? Negativa: didn't use to have. Afirmativa: used to go, used to ride.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige entre used to (hábito que se repetía) y pasado simple (algo que pasó una vez).
ejercicios.texto: In college I {1} in a small apartment with two friends. We {2} pasta every night because it was cheap. One night in 2012 we {3} a party and the neighbors {4} the police. After that, we never {5} a party at home again. On weekends, I {6} as a waiter in a restaurant downtown. One Saturday I {7} a full tray of drinks on a customer. Funny thing: years later, that customer {8} my client.
ejercicios.explica: Lo que se repetía (vivir ahí, comer pasta cada noche, trabajar los fines de semana) → used to. Lo que pasó una vez (one night, one Saturday, years later) → pasado simple: had, called, dropped, became.

ejercicios.texto: My dad says Bogotá used to be a different city. When he moved here in the eighties, people used to wear suits and hats downtown, even on Saturdays. There didn't use to be big shopping malls; families used to walk on Carrera Séptima and eat in small cafés. The city used to be colder too, he says, and it used to rain every afternoon. Did people use to complain about traffic? 'Of course,' he laughs. 'But there were fewer cars, so we used to complain about the buses.' Now he lives in Manizales and visits Bogotá only twice a year.

preguntas.q: What did people use to wear downtown?
Where does his dad live now?
«There didn't use to be big shopping malls»: ¿por qué use y no used?
opciones: Porque didn't ya lleva el pasado

preguntas.q: «it used to rain every afternoon»: ¿qué significa?
opciones: Antes llovía casi todas las tardes

ejercicios.explica: Used to describe cómo eran las cosas antes (used to be, used to wear, used to rain) con un «pero ahora no» implícito. Con did: didn't use to be, Did people use to complain?

ejercicios.texto: My first boss, Ricardo, had a strange style. He used to arrive at seven and read every newspaper before anyone else came in. He didn't use to send emails; he used to write notes by hand and leave them on our desks. Every Friday he used to take the whole team to lunch, and he always paid. He was strict, but he used to say: 'A good idea can come from the intern.' I didn't use to understand that. Now that I lead a team, I repeat it every week.

preguntas.q: How did Ricardo use to communicate with the team?
What did he use to do every Friday?
«I didn't use to understand that»: ¿qué cambió?
opciones: Antes no lo entendía; ahora sí

ejercicios.explica: Las costumbres de alguien en el pasado → used to + base (used to arrive, used to write, used to take). La negativa con did: didn't use to send, didn't use to understand.

ejercicios.consigna: Compara cómo eras en la universidad con cómo eres hoy: hábitos, gustos y horarios. Incluye algo que no solías hacer.

requisitos.texto: Usa used to + verbo base
Incluye una negativa con didn't use to (o never used to)
requisitos.patron: \b(didn't use to|did not use to|never used to)\b

requisitos.texto: Contrasta con el presente (now, nowadays, these days)

ejercicios.ejemplo: In college I used to sleep until noon on weekends and I used to eat junk food every day. I didn't use to read the news, and I never used to plan my week. Now I get up at six, I go to the gym three times a week and I read two newspapers before work. I used to hate early meetings; now I prefer them.
ejercicios.explica: Lo que hacías antes y ya no → used to + base (used to sleep, used to eat). Negativa: didn't use to (sin -d). Lo de ahora va en presente simple: I get up, I go, I prefer.

ejercicios.consigna: Escríbele a alguien nuevo del equipo cómo eran las cosas cuando entraste a la agencia (horarios, oficina, costumbres) y pregúntale por su trabajo anterior con Did you use to…?

requisitos.texto: Usa used to + verbo base
Haz una pregunta con did you use to…?
Ubica el pasado (when i joined, years ago…)

ejercicios.ejemplo: When I joined Brava, things were very different. We used to work in a small office with no windows, and we used to have a team meeting every morning at eight. The creative team used to work until midnight before every pitch. Now we have flexible hours and most meetings are online. What about your old agency? Did you use to work late there too?
ejercicios.explica: Para contar cómo era la agencia antes: we used to work, we used to have. La pregunta lleva did y use sin -d: Did you use to work late?

plan.mensaje: Tu diagnóstico dio 72 %. El pasado simple está firme (8/8); la llave que más se rompe es [[be]] + {{-ing}}: «I preparing», «What did you doing». Esta semana: los dos continuos contrastados con el simple, modales sin «to» y, en paralelo, presente perfecto para tu bucket list del 21–22.

consignas.consigna: ¿Qué estabas haciendo ayer a las 8 pm? Cuenta algo que pasó mientras lo hacías.
consignas.objetivo: Pasado continuo + simple · was/were + -ing · when / while
consignas.ejemplo: At 8 pm I was cooking dinner when my sister called. While we were talking, the rice burned, so we ordered pizza.

consignas.consigna: Un colega te llama y estás ocupado. Explícale en qué estás trabajando esta semana y ofrécele algo para mañana.
consignas.ejemplo: Sorry, I'm finishing a presentation for a client right now. This week we're working on the new campaign. I'll call you tomorrow morning and I'll send you the numbers.

consignas.consigna: En una reunión, das tu opinión sobre una propuesta y no estás de acuerdo con una parte. Cierra comprometiéndote a algo.
consignas.objetivo: I think… · I see your point, but… · I'll…
consignas.ejemplo: I think the idea is strong. I see your point about the budget, but I don't agree with the timeline. I'll review the plan and send you a new version by Friday.

consignas.consigna: Tu bucket list: tres cosas que nunca has hecho y quieres hacer, y una que ya hiciste.
consignas.objetivo: Presente perfecto · I've never… · I've always wanted to… · I've already…
consignas.ejemplo: I've never been to Japan, and I've always wanted to see Kyoto. I've never run a marathon. I've already visited Mexico City, and I loved it.
